definition_zh: 对数；以某数为底求得某数所需的幂
definition_en: the power to which a fixed base must be raised to produce a given number
core_image: 一本旧数表摊开，密密麻麻的数字排成纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」
scene: 旧数表翻到发黄的一页，学生用指尖顺着纵列往下找。 Before calculators, students found products by looking up a logarithm in a printed table.
sceneCN: 这里 logarithm 指「对数，即为得到某数需要把底数抬到的幂」（第 1 个义项：对数的定义）；句意为在计算器出现之前，学生通过查印刷数表里的对数来求乘积。图中可辨识物件：对数表、书页、指尖、铅笔。

pos.zh: 对数；对数值

derivatives.zh: 对数的简写形式（非正式）

senses.title: The power needed to reach a number
senses.definition: the exponent to which a base must be raised to produce a given number
senses.definitionCN: 为使底数得到某个给定数而必须把底数抬到的幂
senses.example: The logarithm answers the question of how many times the base must multiply itself.
senses.exampleCN: 对数回答的是底数必须自乘多少次这个问题。
senses.why: the word was coined from Greek logoi 'ratios' plus arithmos 'number': the ratio-number, the number that measures the ratio.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由希腊语 logoi「比」与 arithmos「数」合成：比数，即衡量比值的那个数。

senses.title: The common logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base ten, written without an explicit base in many texts
senses.definitionCN: 以十为底的对数，许多教材中不写出底数
senses.example: The common logarithm of one thousand is three.
senses.exampleCN: 一千的常用对数是三。
senses.why: base ten matches the decimal system, so the ten-based logarithm became the everyday one in calculation.
senses.whyCN: 以十为底与十进制相合，因此十底对数成了计算中的日常对数。

senses.title: The natural logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to the natural constant, the base that makes growth and decay equations simplest
senses.definitionCN: 以自然常数为底的对数，这个底使增长与衰减的方程最简洁
senses.example: The natural logarithm turns multiplication of growth factors into addition.
senses.exampleCN: 自然对数把增长因子的相乘变成相加。
senses.why: calculus keeps choosing the base whose logarithm has the simplest slope, and that base is called natural for this reason.
senses.whyCN: 微积分总是选那个对数斜率最简单的底，这个底正因此被称为「自然」。

senses.title: The binary logarithm
senses.definition: a logarithm taken to base two, common in computing
senses.definitionCN: 以二为底的对数，常见于计算领域
senses.example: The binary logarithm of the number of leaves gives the depth of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子数量的二进制对数给出这棵树的深度。
senses.why: computer memory splits in two at every step, so base two measures its depth exactly.
senses.whyCN: 计算机存储每一步都一分为二，因此以二为底正好量出它的深度。

senses.title: A table of logarithms
senses.definition: a printed table listing logarithms so that products can be found by adding
senses.definitionCN: 印好的对数数值表，靠相加就能求出乘积
senses.example: The engineer carried a logarithm table in the same case as his slide rule.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把对数表和计算尺装在同一个盒子里。
senses.why: before machines, the table was the practical form of the idea: turn multiplication into addition and look it up.
senses.whyCN: 在没有机器的年代，数表就是这个想法的实用形态：把乘法变成加法再查表。

senses.title: A law of logarithms
senses.definition: a rule such as the logarithm of a product equals the sum of logarithms
senses.definitionCN: 诸如「积的对数等于对数的和」这样的规则
senses.example: The law of logarithms replaced a long multiplication with two short additions.
senses.exampleCN: 对数运算法则把一次很长的乘法换成两次短加法。
senses.why: the whole reason logarithms were invented is that they turn products into sums, which is exactly what the law states.
senses.whyCN: 对数被发明的全部理由就在于把积化为和，这条法则说的正是这件事。

senses.title: The logarithm as a function
senses.definition: the function that assigns to each positive number its logarithm
senses.definitionCN: 把每个正数对应到它的对数的函数
senses.example: The logarithm grows slowly, so it compresses huge ranges into a small interval.
senses.exampleCN: 对数函数增长缓慢，把巨大的范围压进一个小间隔。
senses.why: once the numerical value became a rule applied to every positive input, the logarithm was a function.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个数值变成对每个正输入都适用的规则，对数就成了一个函数。

senses.title: The discrete logarithm
senses.definition: the exponent that solves a power equation within a finite arithmetic system, used in cryptography
senses.definitionCN: 在有限算术系统中解出幂方程的指数，用于密码学
senses.example: The security of the protocol rests on how hard the discrete logarithm is to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这个协议的安全性取决于离散对数有多难求。
senses.why: cryptography took the ordinary logarithm and confined it to a finite system, where finding it becomes deliberately hard.
senses.whyCN: 密码学拿过普通对数，把它限制在有限系统中，找起来就变得刻意地困难。

senses.title: The complex logarithm
senses.definition: an extension of the logarithm to complex numbers, defined with an infinite family of values
senses.definitionCN: 把对数推广到复数，并用无穷多个值来定义
senses.example: The complex logarithm has infinitely many branches.
senses.exampleCN: 复对数有无限多个分支。
senses.why: extending the logarithm past zero forces a choice of branch, so the single value becomes a family.
senses.whyCN: 把对数越出零之外，就迫使人们选择分支，单个值于是变成一族值。

intro.en: Logarithm is a coined scientific term: Greek logos, here in the sense 'ratio', joined to arithmos 'number'. John Napier introduced it in 1614 to name the number that measures a ratio.
intro.cn: logarithm 是一个人造的科学术语：希腊语 logos 在此取「比」义，与 arithmos「数」结合。纳皮尔在 1614 年引入它，用来命名衡量比值的那个数。

items.en: Logos carried a wide range of meanings: word, account, reason and, in mathematics, ratio or proportion. The mathematical sense is the one used here.
items.cn: logos 的含义很广：言词、账目、理性，在数学里则指比或比例。这里用的是数学义。

items.en: Arithmos meant 'number'. Its earlier origin is not securely established, and any pre-Greek form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数」。它更早的来源没有可靠定论，凡为其给出的前希腊语形式都属重构。

items.en: John Napier combined the two Greek elements to mean a number measuring a ratio, and published the new word in his description of the logarithmic tables.
items.cn: 纳皮尔把这两个希腊构件合起来，指「衡量比值的数」，并在他介绍对数表的著作中公布了这一新词。

items.en: The coinage was Latinized as logarithmus and passed into the European languages through scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 这个新造词被拉丁化为 logarithmus，再经学术拉丁语传入欧洲各语言。

items.en: English adopted logarithm in the seventeenth century together with the tables, and the shorter form log followed in usage.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪随对数表一起接受了 logarithm，更短的 log 随后也在使用中出现。

items.en: The coining and its date are documented, but the deeper origin of arithmos is source uncertain; the commonly repeated pre-Greek etymology is a reconstruction rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: 造词与年代有文献可查，但 arithmos 的更早来源不确定；常被转述的前希腊语词源是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to logarithm; the second group names the quantities and tools that sit beside it.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 logarithm 相近；第二组是与它相邻的量与工具。

entries.definition: The adjective of logarithm; it describes scales and curves, not the number itself.
entries.definitionCN: logarithm 的形容词，描述刻度与曲线，而非那个数本身。

entries.definition: From Greek arithmetike 'the art of counting', built on the same arithmos 'number'; it names the subject, not a ratio-measuring number.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 arithmetike「计数的技艺」，同样建立在 arithmos「数」上；它指这门学科，不是衡量比值的数。

entries.definition: From the name al-Khwarizmi through Medieval Latin; it looks like logarithm but has no Greek logos or arithmos inside.
entries.definitionCN: 经中世纪拉丁语来自花拉子米的名字；看似 logarithm，里面却没有希腊的 logos 或 arithmos。

entries.definition: From Greek logistikos 'skilled in calculation', but it developed separately to mean supply management and a growth model.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 logistikos「精于计算」，但独立发展出后勤管理与一种增长模型的意思。

entries.definition: The number whose logarithm is given; it reverses the lookup rather than performing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数为某值的那个数；它把查表反过来，而非执行查表。

entries.definition: The power itself; a logarithm is that power asked as a question about a result.
entries.definitionCN: 指幂本身；对数则是把这个幂当作「要得到某结果」的问题来问。

entries.definition: The result of repeated multiplication; the logarithm names the count of repetitions.
entries.definitionCN: 指重复相乘的结果；对数命名的则是重复的次数。

entries.definition: A relation between two amounts; the 'ratio' inside logarithm names what the number measures, not a quotient itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个量之间的关系；logarithm 里的「比」说明这个数衡量什么，而不是指商本身。

entries.definition: A calculating tool that works by adding lengths proportional to logarithms.
entries.definitionCN: 一种计算工具，靠相加与对数成比例的长度来运算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Greek logos 'ratio' plus arithmos 'number': a ratio-number, the number that measures a ratio.
normal.cn: 希腊 logos「比」加 arithmos「数」：比数，衡量比值的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs logarithm, logarithmic, logarithmically and antilogarithm.
normal.cn: 同族词有 logarithm、logarithmic、logarithmically 与 antilogarithm。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the bases: common logarithm, natural logarithm, binary logarithm.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出底数：常用对数、自然对数、二进制对数。

normal.en: The whole point is stated in one line: the log of a product is the sum of the logs.
normal.cn: 全部要点可以写成一行：积的对数等于对数的和。

normal.en: Before machines, people turned multiplication into addition and then read the answer off a table.
normal.cn: 在没有机器的年代，人们把乘法变成加法，再从表上读出答案。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose steps get shorter and shorter but never quite end.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，台阶越来越矮，却始终走不完。

abstract.en: Picture a giant compressed into a small box, still recognizable in outline.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨人被压进小盒子，轮廓仍然认得出来。

abstract.en: Picture a question that asks not 'what is the answer' but 'how many times did you multiply'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题不问「答案是多少」，而问「你乘了几次」。

examples.en: The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms of its factors.
examples.cn: 积的对数等于各因子对数的和。

examples.en: Engineers once read logarithms from books the way we now read screens.
examples.cn: 工程师曾像我们今天读屏幕一样从书本上读对数。

examples.en: On a logarithmic scale the logarithm itself becomes the distance along the axis.
examples.cn: 在对数尺度上，对数本身就变成沿轴的这段距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「逻各」配「节奏」——按固定的「比例节奏」一层层数上去 → 对数

root: 希腊 logos（比、比例、言词）+ arithmos（数）→ 近代拉丁 logarithmus，纳皮尔 1614 年造词。arithmos 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all ask the same question in different settings: how many times must the base be multiplied? The answer is read from a definition, a base, a table, a law, a function, a cipher or a complex branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同场合问同一个问题：底数要乘多少次？答案分别从定义、底数、数表、法则、函数、密码系统或复分支中读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old table of columns, each column answering the question 'raised how many times'.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧数表排着纵列，每一列都在回答「要抬到几次」。

branches.en: THE QUESTION ITSELF: the exponent needed to reach a given number.
branches.cn: 问题本身：为得到某个给定数所需的幂。

branches.en: THE CHOICE OF BASE: ten for decimals, the natural constant for calculus, two for machines.
branches.cn: 底数的选择：十进制用十，微积分用自然常数，机器用二。

branches.en: THE OLD TOOL: a printed table and the law that turns products into sums.
branches.cn: 旧工具：印好的数表，以及把积化为和的法则。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the same value applied to every positive input.
branches.cn: 函数：把同一个值应用到每个正输入上。

branches.en: BEYOND ORDINARY NUMBERS: a deliberately hard exponent in ciphers, and an infinite family of branches in the complex plane.
branches.cn: 越出普通数之外：密码中刻意难求的指数，以及复平面上无穷多个分支。

intro.en: Logarithm is a modern coinage from two Greek nouns, so its building blocks are combining forms rather than inherited prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: logarithm 是由两个希腊名词合成的近代新词，因此它的构件其实是组合形式，而非继承下来的前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek elements logos and arithmos entered Latin as logos and arithmus; the coinage logarithmus is modern Latin, not classical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊构件 logos 与 arithmos 以 logos、arithmus 的形式进入拉丁语；logarithmus 是近代拉丁造词，不属于古典拉丁。

items.example: The first element contributes the idea of ratio.
items.exampleCN: 第一个构件贡献「比」这个意思。

items.example: The second element contributes the idea of number.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件贡献「数」这个意思。

items.example: The logarithm measures how often the base is raised.
items.exampleCN: 对数衡量底数被抬了几次。

items.example: The scale is logarithmic.
items.exampleCN: 这个刻度是对数的。

items.example: The values grow logarithmically.
items.exampleCN: 这些数值按对数方式增长。

items.meaning: the number matching a given logarithm
items.example: The antilogarithm reverses the lookup.
items.exampleCN: 反对数把查表反过来。

items.example: Arithmetic uses the same number element.
items.exampleCN: 算术用的是同一个「数」构件。

items.meaning: logarithm in informal and technical use
items.example: The program takes the log of the input.
items.exampleCN: 程序对输入取对数。

definition_zh: 还原论的；化约论的；还原论者
definition_en: explaining a complex whole by its simpler parts, or a person who advocates that approach
core_image: 一座完整的花园被拆成一格格土壤样本，每格只标成分编号
scene: 这里指「还原论的」。 A reductionist account of love describes only hormones and neural firing.
sceneCN: 这里 reductionist 是「还原论的」（第 1 个义项：把复杂现象解释为其组成部分）；句意：对爱情的还原论解释只谈激素与神经放电。图中可辨识物件：花园平面图、编号土壤样本、放大镜、成分表。

pos.zh: 还原论的；化约论的（常带批评语气）
还原论者；主张化约解释的人

senses.title: Explaining by simpler parts
senses.titleCN: 以部分解释整体：把复杂现象拆到更低层级
senses.definition: describing an approach that explains a complex system through its simpler components
senses.definitionCN: 形容把复杂系统通过其更简单组成部分来解释的做法
senses.example: A reductionist account of love describes only hormones and neural firing.
senses.exampleCN: 对爱情的还原论解释只谈激素与神经放电。
senses.why: The suffix -ist marks a practitioner or a stance, and reduction already means 'leading back'; together they name the habit of leading a whole back to its parts.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记实践者或立场，reduction 已含「带回」义；两者合起来命名「把整体带回部分」的做法。

senses.title: Oversimplifying
senses.titleCN: 过度简化：把整体削成几个变量
senses.definition: used critically for an explanation that loses essential features by simplifying too far
senses.definitionCN: 带批评地形容因简化过头而丢失关键特征的说明
senses.example: The review rejected the reductionist claim that culture is only economics.
senses.exampleCN: 评论否决了「文化只是经济」这一还原论主张。
senses.why: The same term turns into a reproach when the lost features matter: what is left out is exactly what made the whole what it is.
senses.whyCN: 当被丢掉的特性很重要时，同一个词就转为贬义：被省略的恰恰是使整体成为整体的东西。

senses.title: A person who advocates it
senses.titleCN: 还原论者：主张化约解释的人
senses.definition: a person who holds that complex phenomena should be explained by their simplest constituents
senses.definitionCN: 主张复杂现象应由其最简单构成部分来解释的人
senses.example: As a reductionist, she insists that biology must ultimately rest on chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 作为还原论者，她坚持生物学最终必须建立在化学之上。
senses.why: The -ist suffix turns the adjective into a person: the stance becomes an identity, and the debate becomes about people as well as claims.
senses.whyCN: -ist 后缀把形容词变成人：立场成为身份，争论也随之涉及人而不只是主张。

senses.title: Scientific reductionism
senses.titleCN: 科学还原论：高层学科归于低层规律
senses.definition: describing the program of deriving higher-level sciences from more fundamental ones such as physics
senses.definitionCN: 形容把高层学科从物理学等更基础学科推导出来的纲领
senses.example: Scientific reductionism has scored great successes in molecular biology.
senses.exampleCN: 科学还原论在分子生物学上取得了巨大成功。
senses.why: Physics is treated as the base layer; each higher layer is expected to be led back to it, which is exactly what the word says.
senses.whyCN: 物理学被视为底层；每一更高层都被期望带回它，这正是该词字面所述。

senses.title: Philosophical reductionism
senses.titleCN: 哲学还原论：心智归于大脑过程
senses.definition: describing the view that one kind of entity, such as mind, is really nothing over and above another, such as brain processes
senses.definitionCN: 形容认为某一类实体（如心智）实际上不外乎另一类实体（如大脑过程）的观点
senses.example: Philosophical reductionism about mind remains fiercely debated.
senses.exampleCN: 关于心智的哲学还原论仍争论激烈。
senses.why: Here reduction is ontological, not merely explanatory: the claim is that the higher thing is the lower thing, viewed from another level.
senses.whyCN: 这里的还原是本体论的，而不只是解释性的：它主张高层事物就是低层事物，只是从另一层级看。

senses.title: Methodological, not ontological
senses.titleCN: 方法论的还原：只是研究策略
senses.definition: describing a research strategy that studies parts first, without claiming that the whole is nothing but those parts
senses.definitionCN: 形容先研究部分的研究策略，但不宣称整体只是这些部分
senses.example: Methodological reductionism is compatible with saying that the whole has new properties.
senses.exampleCN: 方法论的还原论可以与「整体具有新性质」的说法相容。
senses.why: The distinction matters because many scientists are reductionist only about method: break the system down to study it, then put it back.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分很重要，因为许多科学家只在方法上还原：拆开系统来研究，再装回去。

senses.title: Genetic reductionism
senses.titleCN: 基因还原论：把复杂性状归于单个基因
senses.definition: describing the tendency to explain behaviour or disease as the product of specific genes
senses.definitionCN: 形容把行为或疾病解释为特定基因产物的倾向
senses.example: Genetic reductionism underestimated the role of environment.
senses.exampleCN: 基因还原论低估了环境的作用。
senses.why: Genetics supplied a concrete lower layer, so the general habit of leading things back found a new target: the gene.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学提供了一个具体的低层，于是「把事物带回低层」的一般习惯找到了新目标：基因。

senses.title: Critique in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的批评：人不能被化约为变量
senses.definition: used in social science and the humanities to criticize explanations that dissolve people, meanings or institutions into measurable variables
senses.definitionCN: 在社会科学与人文学科中，批评把人、意义或制度消解为可测量变量的解释
senses.example: Historians warned against a reductionist reading of religious movements as mere economics.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家警告，不要把宗教运动还原论地读成纯粹的经济现象。
senses.why: The word becomes a boundary marker: it tells the reader that a method has crossed from analysis into loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了边界标记：它提醒读者，某种方法已从分析越界成了丢失。

intro.en: Reductionist is an English derivative: reduction (from Latin reducere 'lead back') plus the agent suffix -ist, through French and Latin -ista and Greek -istes.
intro.cn: reductionist 是英语派生词：reduction（出自拉丁 reducere「带回」）加施动后缀 -ist，后者经法语与拉丁 -ista、希腊 -istes 传入。

items.en: Reduction rests on reducere, from re- 'back' and ducere 'to lead'. The physical image is bringing something back down.
items.cn: reduction 基于 reducere，由 re-「回」与 ducere「引导」构成，其物理意象是把某物带回下方。

items.en: The Latin noun reductio named a leading back. In logic, reductio ad absurdum led a claim back to contradiction.
items.cn: 拉丁名词 reductio 指「带回」。逻辑中的 reductio ad absurdum 把主张带回到矛盾。

items.en: The English noun reductionism appeared in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries for the doctrine that higher phenomena can be explained by lower ones.
items.cn: 英语名词 reductionism 于 19 至 20 世纪出现，指高层现象可由低层现象解释的学说。

items.en: The suffix -ist comes through French -iste from Latin -ista and Greek -istes, marking a person who practices or supports something.
items.cn: 后缀 -ist 经法语 -iste 来自拉丁 -ista 与希腊 -istes，标记实践或支持某事物的人。

items.en: Adding -ist to reduction produced both a noun for the advocate and an adjective for the approach.
items.cn: 在 reduction 上加 -ist，既产生指拥护者的名词，也产生指该方法路的形容词。

items.en: The exact first use of reductionist in English is uncertain, and its critical sense grew gradually rather than from a single source.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与语义形成时间）：reductionist 英语首用确切年代存疑，其批评义是逐渐形成的，并非出自单一来源。

note.en: The first group separates the reduction family; the second gives near-synonyms for simplifying or explanatory stances.
note.cn: 第一组区分 reduction 词族；第二组给出表示简化或解释立场的近义词。

entries.definition: The theory itself, not the person or the adjective. Reductionist can describe a claim or a person; reductionism names the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指学说本身，不是人或形容词。reductionist 可描述主张或人；reductionism 命名的学说是其本身。

entries.definition: A decrease, a chemical gain of electrons, or a simplification. It does not by itself imply the philosophical doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指减少、化学还原或简化；本身不暗示那套哲学学说。

entries.definition: Describing an explanation that simplifies, often disapprovingly. Reductionist is more specific: it names a stance about levels of explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容简化的解释，常带贬义。reductionist 更具体：它命名关于解释层级的立场。

entries.definition: A rare word about deriving conclusions by deduction; the prefix points away, not back, and it is not the same debate.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的词，指靠演绎得出结论；前缀方向是「带走」而非「带回」，不属于同一争论。

entries.definition: Treating a complex matter as simpler than it is. It criticizes the result, while reductionist criticizes the method or stance.
entries.definitionCN: 指把复杂问题看得过于简单；批评的是结果，而 reductionist 批评方法或立场。

entries.definition: Explaining things as machines with parts and forces. It overlaps sense 1 but stresses mechanics rather than levels.
entries.definitionCN: 指以机器、部件与力来解释；与第 1 个义项重叠，但强调机械而非层级。

entries.definition: Breaking a whole into separate units. It is close to sense 1 but historically tied to atomism in philosophy and society.
entries.definitionCN: 指把整体拆成独立单元；接近第 1 个义项，但历史上与哲学及社会的原子论相连。

entries.definition: Explaining by physical matter or economic interests. It is a specific lower layer, not the general level-reducing stance.
entries.definitionCN: 指以物质或经济利益解释；是一个具体低层，而非一般的「降层」立场。

entries.definition: Treating the whole as more than its parts. It is the direct counter-term, useful for contrast rather than as a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指把整体看作多于部分之和；是直接对立词，适于对比而非同义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: reduction + -ist: a person or stance that leads a whole back to its parts.
normal.cn: reduction + -ist：把人或立场「把整体带回部分」。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reduction, reductive, reductionism, reductionist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reduction、reductive、reductionism、reductionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the debate: reductionist approach, reductionist explanation, reductionist fallacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出争论：还原论方法、还原论解释、还原论谬误。

normal.en: Methodological reductionism studies parts without denying that the whole has new properties.
normal.cn: 方法论还原论研究部分，但不否认整体具有新性质。

normal.en: holistic is its opposite; mechanistic and atomistic are narrower cousins.
normal.cn: holistic 是它的对立词；mechanistic 与 atomistic 是范围更窄的近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a garden cut into numbered soil samples, with the paths and scents left out.
abstract.cn: 想象花园被切成编号土样，路径与花香都被略去。

abstract.en: Picture a watch explained only by listing the metals in its gears.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手表只靠列出齿轮中的金属来解释。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step must be traced down to the stone floor before it counts.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每一级都必须追到石地面才算成立。

examples.en: The authors defended a reductionist model but denied that it captured the whole story.
examples.cn: 作者为还原论模型辩护，但否认它道出了全貌。

examples.en: Reductionist explanations of disease once ignored social conditions.
examples.cn: 对疾病的还原论解释曾忽视社会条件。

examples.en: A methodological reductionist can still study emergent behaviour.
examples.cn: 方法论还原论者仍可研究涌现行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「reduction（还原）+ ist（人）」——凡事都要拆回零件的人 → reductionist 还原论者

root: 拉丁 reducere「带回」→ reduction「还原、减少」+ -ist（人／立场后缀）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split a stance into layers: part-explanation, oversimplification, the person, scientific base-layers, ontology, method, genes, and the social-science objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把一种立场拆成各层：以部分解释、过度简化、持论者、科学底层、本体论、方法论、基因，以及社会科学方面的反对意见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garden cut into numbered samples, paths and scents omitted.
core.cn: 核心意象：花园被切成编号样本，路径与花香被省略。

branches.en: EXPLANATION AND ITS COST: explaining by parts, and the reproach when parts replace the whole.
branches.cn: 解释与其代价：以部分解释，以及部分取代整体时招来的批评。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the stance hardens into an identity held by someone.
branches.cn: 持论者：立场固化为某人的身份。

branches.en: LEVELS OF REALITY: higher sciences or minds are said to rest on lower layers.
branches.cn: 实在层级：高层学科或心智被说成建立在低层之上。

branches.en: METHOD AND GENE: one version only studies parts, another makes a specific gene the cause.
branches.cn: 方法与基因：一种版本只研究部分，另一种把特定基因当成原因。

branches.en: THE OBJECTION: people, meanings and institutions resist being dissolved into variables.
branches.cn: 反对意见：人、意义与制度不愿被消解为变量。

intro.en: Reductionist combines a Latin noun of action with a Greek-derived agent suffix; the word labels both a method and the person who follows it.
intro.cn: reductionist 把拉丁动作名词与希腊来源的施动后缀结合，既标记一种方法，也标记遵循该方法的人。

latinIntro.en: The ducere family supplies reduce and reduction; the -ist family supplies scientist, economist, realist and reductionist, all naming practitioners or adherents.
latinIntro.cn: ducere 词族提供 reduce 与 reduction；-ist 词族提供 scientist、economist、realist、reductionist，均命名实践者或拥护者。

items.meaning: one who explains wholes by their parts
items.meaningCN: 以部分解释整体的人或立场
items.example: The debate pitted reductionists against holists.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论让还原论者与整体论者对垒。

items.meaning: the doctrine of explaining by lower levels
items.meaningCN: 以更低层级解释的学说
items.example: Reductionism shaped modern molecular biology.
items.exampleCN: 还原论塑造了现代分子生物学。

items.example: The reduction of the problem took two steps.
items.exampleCN: 该问题的化简用了两步。

items.example: The summary was reductive but useful.
items.exampleCN: 这份摘要虽简化，却有用。

items.example: We reduced the model to three variables.
items.exampleCN: 我们把模型缩减为三个变量。

items.example: A holistic view asks how the parts interact.
items.exampleCN: 整体论视角追问各部分如何互动。

items.example: An atomistic account treats society as isolated individuals.
items.exampleCN: 原子论式说明把社会视为孤立个体。

items.example: The mechanistic model ignored feedback.
items.exampleCN: 该机械模型忽略了反馈。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 命名拥护者的施动后缀

definition_zh: 排斥；放逐；孤立
definition_en: the act of shutting a person out of a group, so that no one will speak to or deal with him
core_image: 一圈人站成环，把一个人留在圈外，地上那道线谁也不肯跨过去
scene: 他因为说了真话，被整条街的人不再打招呼，连杂货店都懒得找零。 Because he had told the truth, the whole street stopped greeting him, and even the grocer could not be bothered to give change, a quiet ostracism.
sceneCN: 这里 ostracism 指社会排斥（第 1 个义项：社会排斥）；句意为他说了真话后，整条街的人不再打招呼，连杂货店也懒得找零，这是一种无声的排斥。

pos.zh: 排斥；放逐；孤立

senses.title: Social exclusion
senses.definition: the condition of being kept outside a group that once included you
senses.definitionCN: 被留在曾经接纳自己的群体之外的状态
senses.example: The ostracism began with silence at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这种排斥从校门口的沉默开始。
senses.why: The word's force is collective: many people each do a little nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的力量是集体的：许多人各自做了一点点「什么都不做」。

senses.title: Athenian ostracism
senses.definition: the ancient Athenian vote by which a citizen could be sent away for ten years
senses.definitionCN: 古雅典以投票把公民放逐十年的制度
senses.example: Under Athenian ostracism, a name scratched on a potshard could end a career.
senses.exampleCN: 在雅典的陶片放逐中，刻在陶片上一个名字就能终结一段仕途。
senses.why: The original is political and procedural, not merely social.
senses.whyCN: 原初义项是政治的、程序的，不只是社交的。

senses.title: Deliberate shunning
senses.definition: an organised refusal to speak to or deal with a person
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地拒绝与某人说话或往来
senses.example: The village practised ostracism against the family for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 村里人对那家人施行了一季的回避。
senses.why: Shunning is the everyday engine of ostracism; no law is needed.
senses.whyCN: 回避是排斥的日常引擎；不需要任何法律。

senses.title: Workplace exclusion
senses.definition: the quiet removal of a colleague from meetings, decisions and talk
senses.definitionCN: 把同事悄悄移出会议、决策与谈话
senses.example: His ostracism at the firm was never written down.
senses.exampleCN: 他在公司里被孤立，从未被写进任何文件。
senses.why: Modern institutions ostracize by omission rather than decree.
senses.whyCN: 现代机构靠遗漏而非命令来排斥。

senses.title: Political exclusion
senses.definition: the pushing of a rival out of influence while keeping the forms intact
senses.definitionCN: 在保留形式的同时把对手挤出影响力
senses.example: The party used ostracism instead of expulsion.
senses.exampleCN: 该党用排挤代替开除。
senses.why: Here the group keeps its rules and still removes the person.
senses.whyCN: 这里群体保留规则，却仍然移除了那个人。

senses.title: A child left out
senses.definition: the playground practice of excluding one child from every game
senses.definitionCN: 操场上把某个孩子排除在所有游戏之外的作法
senses.example: Teachers now treat ostracism as a form of harm.
senses.exampleCN: 教师如今把孤立视为一种伤害。
senses.why: Small groups rehearse the same politics with smaller stakes.
senses.whyCN: 小群体用更小的代价排练同样的政治。

senses.title: Cultural exclusion
senses.definition: the refusal of a community to count a person or practice as its own
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群拒绝把某人或某种做法算作自己的
senses.example: The ostracism of the dialect lasted two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 对方言的排斥持续了两代人。
senses.why: Cultures can ostracize a whole way of speaking, not only a speaker.
senses.whyCN: 文化可以排斥一整套说话方式，而不只是排斥某个人。

senses.title: Rejection of ideas
senses.definition: the refusal to admit a view into respectable discussion
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝让某种看法进入体面的讨论
senses.example: The ostracism of the theory was slow and complete.
senses.exampleCN: 对那个理论的排斥缓慢而彻底。
senses.why: Ideas are ostracized by the same silence that removes people.
senses.whyCN: 观念被排斥，靠的是移除人时那种同样的沉默。

intro.en: Ostracism is a word made of potsherds: the Athenians wrote a name on a broken piece of pottery and counted the pieces.
intro.cn: ostracism 是一个由陶片构成的词：雅典人把名字写在碎陶片上，然后数陶片。

items.en: Ostrakon meant 'a shell or a potsherd', the cheap material used for a vote.
items.cn: ostrakon 意为「贝壳或陶片」，是投票用的廉价材料。

items.en: Ostrakizein meant 'to vote by potsherd', hence 'to send a man out of the city'.
items.cn: ostrakizein 意为「用陶片投票」，因此意为「把一个人送出城」。

items.en: Ostrakismos named the institution itself, the ten-year exile decided by a majority of shards.
items.cn: ostrakismos 命名制度本身：由多数陶片决定的十年放逐。

items.en: English borrowed ostracism in the seventeenth century, first as a classical curiosity.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ostracism，最初是作为古典典故。

items.en: Modern usage widened it from a vote to any group's refusal to keep a member.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从投票扩展到任何群体对成员的拒绝。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ostrakon family; the near-meaning group separates exclusion, shunning, exile and banishment.
note.cn: 形近组是 ostrakon 词族；近义组把「排斥」「回避」「流放」与「放逐」分开。

entries.definition: to shut a person out of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人排斥在群体之外。

entries.definition: shut out by a group.
entries.definitionCN: 被群体排斥的。

entries.definition: in the act of shutting out.
entries.definitionCN: 正在排斥的。

entries.definition: a potsherd used for voting.
entries.definitionCN: 用于投票的陶片。

entries.definition: the act of keeping someone out.
entries.definitionCN: 把人挡在外的行为。

entries.definition: deliberately avoiding a person.
entries.definitionCN: 刻意避开某人。

entries.definition: enforced absence from one's country.
entries.definitionCN: 被迫离开本国。

entries.definition: official expulsion from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 被正式驱逐出某地。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a ring of people and one gap nobody will close.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一圈人和一道谁都不肯补上的缺口」的画面。

normal.en: Ostracism holds ostrakon, a potsherd: the Athenians voted a man out with broken pottery.
normal.cn: ostracism 里藏着 ostrakon（陶片）：雅典人用碎陶片把一个人投出去。

normal.en: Think of a circle of chairs with one chair pushed outside the line.
normal.cn: 想象一圈椅子，其中一把被推到线外。

normal.en: Os-tra-cism: the middle sounds like 'trace', the line on the ground no one crosses.
normal.cn: os-tra-cism：中间听起来像 trace，地上那道没人越过的线。

normal.en: Say OS-truh-siz-um; the first syllable is the group, the rest is the pushing out.
normal.cn: 读成 OS-truh-siz-um，第一个音节是群体，其余是把人推出去。

normal.en: Pair it with silence: ostracism is mostly done by not speaking.
normal.cn: 把它和 silence 配对：排斥多半是靠不说话完成的。

abstract.en: Ostracism needs no enemy, only a majority that finds it easier to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 排斥不需要敌人，只需要一个觉得沉默更省事的多数。

abstract.en: It is the punishment a group gives for the crime of making it uncomfortable.
abstract.cn: 这是群体对「让它不舒服」这一罪名的惩罚。

abstract.en: The old potsherd and the modern cold shoulder do the same work: they count the person out.
abstract.cn: 古老陶片与现代冷遇做的是同一件事：把人从数里减去。

examples.en: Because he had told the truth, the whole street stopped greeting him, a quiet ostracism.
examples.cn: 因为他说了真话，整条街的人不再打招呼，这是一种无声的排斥。

examples.en: Under Athenian ostracism, a name on a potsherd could end a career.
examples.cn: 在雅典的陶片放逐中，陶片上的一个名字就能终结一段仕途。

examples.en: The ostracism of the theory was slow and complete.
examples.cn: 对那个理论的排斥缓慢而彻底。

dict_mnemonic.text: ostracon（陶片）+ ism（制度）：雅典人用陶片投票把人放逐，就是「排斥」。

root: 希腊语 ostrakismos（陶片放逐），源自 ostrakon（陶片、贝壳）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all draw a line around a group: a city, a street, a firm, a party, a playground, a culture and a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在群体周围画一道线：一座城、一条街、一家公司、一个政党、一片操场、一种文化与一个学科。

core.en: A RING OF PEOPLE WITH ONE GAP
core.cn: 一圈人和一道缺口

branches.en: The condition of exclusion and the daily practice of shunning.
branches.cn: 被排斥的状态与日常回避的做法。

branches.en: The Athenian vote that started the word.
branches.cn: 开启这个词的雅典投票。

branches.en: A colleague removed quietly and a rival pushed aside.
branches.cn: 被悄悄移出的同事与被挤到一边的对手。

branches.en: A child left out and a dialect refused.
branches.cn: 被排除的孩子与被拒绝的方言。

branches.en: A view kept out of respectable talk.
branches.cn: 被挡在体面讨论之外的看法。

intro.en: The ostrakon family is about shells and shards: ostracism was a vote, ostracize the act, ostracon the material.
intro.cn: ostrakon 词族关乎贝壳与碎片：ostracism 是制度，ostracize 是行为，ostracon 是材料。

latinIntro.en: Greek ostrakon gives the material and ostrakizein gives the action; the suffix -ismos names the institution.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ostrakon 提供材料，ostrakizein 提供动作，后缀 -ismos 命名制度。

items.example: Ostracism removed him for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 陶片放逐把他逐出十年。

items.example: The group ostracized him.
items.exampleCN: 群体排斥他。

items.example: He felt ostracized.
items.exampleCN: 他感到被排斥。

items.example: Their ostracizing was silent.
items.exampleCN: 他们的排斥是无声的。

items.example: The ostracizer was never named.
items.exampleCN: 排斥者从未被点名。

items.example: Each ostracon bore one name.
items.exampleCN: 每片陶片写着一个名字。

items.example: Ostracods live in the mud.
items.exampleCN: 介形虫生活在泥里。

items.example: Ostracoderms are long extinct.
items.exampleCN: 甲皮鱼类早已灭绝。

definition_zh: 咸水；海水；咸水的；海生的；（口语）老水手
definition_en: water containing a large amount of dissolved salt, especially sea water; living in or relating to such water
core_image: 潮水沿着河口倒灌进田里，水面泛着白沫，稻叶由绿转黄
scene: 潮水灌进河口旁的田里，水变得又咸又涩，稻叶开始发黄。 The tide pushed saltwater into the fields beside the river mouth, and the rice leaves turned yellow.
sceneCN: 这里 saltwater 指「含盐量高的水、海水」（第 1 个义项：溶解大量盐分的水体）；句意：潮水把咸水推进河口旁的田里，稻叶因此发黄。图中可辨识物件：倒灌的潮水、田埂、发黄的稻叶、水面白沫。

pos.zh: 咸水；海水（含大量溶解盐的水）
咸水的；海生的；海水环境的

collocations.zh: 海水入侵（咸水侵入淡水层）
咸水池（用盐电解消毒的泳池）

senses.title: Water with much dissolved salt
senses.titleCN: 含大量溶解盐的水（咸水）
senses.definition: water in which a large amount of salt is dissolved, as in the sea or in salt lakes
senses.definitionCN: 溶解了大量盐分的水，如海水或咸水湖
senses.example: The tide pushed saltwater into the fields beside the river mouth, and the rice leaves turned yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水把咸水推进河口旁的田里，稻叶因此发黄。
senses.why: the compound names water by its salt content, so the defining measure is salinity, not the presence of any particular mineral.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词按含盐量命名水，界定尺度是盐度，而非某种特定矿物。

senses.title: Sea water as opposed to fresh water
senses.definition: the water of the ocean, used especially when contrasting it with river or lake water
senses.definitionCN: 海洋中的水，尤用于与河流或湖泊的淡水对照时
senses.example: The channel mixes saltwater and river water twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这条水道每天两次混合海水与河水。
senses.why: seawater is the prototype of salty water, so the compound works as a plain synonym in everyday and technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 海水是咸水的原型，因此这个复合词在日常与技术写作中可作普通同义词。

senses.title: Marine organisms kept in salty water
senses.titleCN: 生活在咸水中的（海生生物）
senses.definition: describing fish, plants and invertebrates that live in sea water rather than fresh water
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在海水而非淡水中的鱼、植物与无脊椎动物
senses.example: Saltwater fish must drink constantly to avoid dehydrating.
senses.exampleCN: 海水鱼必须不断饮水，以免脱水。
senses.why: the adjective before organism names turns salinity into a habitat label, contrasting with freshwater species.
senses.whyCN: 置于生物名称前作定语时，这个词把盐度变成生境标签，与淡水物种相对。

senses.title: Saltwater aquaculture and aquariums
senses.definition: relating to the farming or tank keeping of marine organisms
senses.definitionCN: 与海水生物的养殖或水族箱饲养有关
senses.example: The saltwater section of the hatchery rears two native shrimp species.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场的海水区养育着两种本地虾。
senses.why: hobby and industry both need a short label for the saline half of their work, and saltwater fills it.
senses.whyCN: 爱好与产业都需要一个简短标签指其工作的咸水部分，saltwater 正好填补。

senses.title: Brine used in cooking or industry
senses.definition: strongly salted water used to preserve food or as an industrial fluid
senses.definitionCN: 用于腌制食物或作为工业流体的高盐浓度水
senses.example: The olives were cured in saltwater for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄在盐水中腌了三周。
senses.why: the same salt-and-water idea narrows to a prepared brine, where salt is added deliberately rather than geologically present.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「盐加水」的概念收窄为人工配制的盐水，盐是刻意加入的，而非地质存在。

senses.title: Salt water invading a freshwater aquifer
senses.titleCN: 海水入侵（咸水侵入淡水层）
senses.definition: the movement of salty water into coastal groundwater or soils, usually because of overpumping or sea-level rise
senses.definitionCN: 咸水进入沿海地下水或土壤，通常因过量抽水或海平面上升
senses.example: Saltwater intrusion has forced two farms to abandon their wells.
senses.exampleCN: 海水入侵迫使两家农场废弃了水井。
senses.why: the technical sense turns the compound into a named process, where saltwater is the agent and fresh groundwater the victim.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把这个复合词变成一个有名目的过程：咸水是施动者，淡水地下水是受害者。

senses.title: Saline wetlands and lagoons
senses.definition: describing coastal marshes, lagoons and pools whose water is brackish or fully salty
senses.definitionCN: 描述水体微咸或全咸的海岸沼泽、潟湖与水池
senses.example: Saltwater marshes absorb storm surge better than sea walls do.
senses.exampleCN: 咸水沼泽比海堤更能吸收风暴潮。
senses.why: coastal ecology uses the adjective for transition zones, where the water is salty enough to exclude most freshwater plants.
senses.whyCN: 海岸生态学用这个形容词指过渡带，那里的咸度足以排除多数淡水植物。

senses.title: A saltwater sailor: an experienced one
senses.titleCN: 习语：真正出过海的老水手
senses.definition: informal, a sailor with long experience of the open sea, as opposed to a freshwater sailor
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指长期在开阔海域航行的老水手，与 freshwater sailor 相对
senses.example: The old saltwater sailor knew the reef by the colour of the water.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老水手能凭水色辨认礁石。
senses.why: salt water is the sailor's true element, so the idiom marks genuine sea experience, mirroring the insult freshwater sailor.
senses.whyCN: 咸水是水手真正的元素，因此这一习语标记真实的海上经验，正好与 freshwater sailor 的讥讽相对。

intro.en: Saltwater is an English compound of salt and water, both native Germanic words. Salt has a genuine Latin cognate in sal, but the English word does not descend from Latin, so no Latin source is claimed.
intro.cn: saltwater 是 salt 与 water 构成的英语复合词，两者都是日耳曼语本族词。salt 与拉丁 sal 确实是同源词，但英语这个词并非由拉丁语派生，因此不称其有拉丁来源。

items.en: Old English sealt 'salt' is the direct ancestor; the noun and the adjective shared one form, as they still do in part.
items.cn: 古英语 sealt「盐」是直接祖形；名词与形容词曾共用一词形，至今仍部分如此。

items.en: The Germanic form *saltaz and the Indo-European base *sal- are reconstructions supported by many related languages, but no single recorded ancestor exists.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 *saltaz 与印欧语词根 *sal- 都是靠多种亲属语言支持的重构，并不存在单一有记录的祖形。

items.en: Latin sal 'salt' belongs to the same *sal- family, so saline and salinity are cognates of salt rather than its source.
items.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」属于同一 *sal- 词族，因此 saline 与 salinity 是 salt 的同源词，而非其来源。

items.en: Salt water appears as a plain phrase from the Middle English period, and the closed form saltwater later became the technical adjective.
items.cn: salt water 自中古英语时期便作为普通短语出现，闭合形式 saltwater 后来成为技术形容词。

items.en: The phrase saltwater sailor is recorded in the nineteenth century as the positive counterpart of freshwater sailor.
items.cn: saltwater sailor 这一短语在 19 世纪有记载，是 freshwater sailor 的正面对应说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Germanic and Indo-European forms are reconstructions, and the earliest compound citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：日耳曼语之前与印欧语的形式均属重构，复合词最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates the closed compound from its open spelling and from words built on the salt stock with different referents; group two contrasts it with other saline-water terms.
note.cn: 第一组区分闭合复合词与分写形式，并辨明同出 salt 词族却指别物的词；第二组对照其它咸水词语。

entries.definition: The two-word phrase for salty water; the closed form saltwater is usual when the word modifies another noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指咸水的两词短语；当该词修饰另一名词时，通常用闭合形式 saltwater。

entries.definition: Containing salt, or a salt solution used medically; it comes from Latin salinus, a cognate rather than the source of saltwater.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的，或医用的盐溶液；来自拉丁 salinus，是 saltwater 的同源词而非其来源。

entries.definition: A thin crisp cracker made with a little salt; the salt root is shared but the referent is food.
entries.definitionCN: 加少量盐的薄脆饼干；盐词根相同，所指却是食物。

entries.definition: Potassium nitrate, a mineral used in gunpowder and fertiliser; its second element is not water, so the resemblance to saltwater is partial.
entries.definitionCN: 硝酸钾，用于火药与肥料；其第二部分并非 water，因此与 saltwater 只是部分形近。

entries.definition: Water of the ocean, typically about three and a half percent salt; it is the concrete case that saltwater generalises.
entries.definitionCN: 海洋中的水，盐度通常约百分之三点五；它是 saltwater 所概括的具体原型。

entries.definition: Water saturated or nearly saturated with salt; it is stronger than ordinary saltwater and usually made deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 被盐饱和或接近饱和的水；比普通咸水更浓，通常是人工配制的。

entries.definition: Slightly salty, as where river water mixes with sea water; it is weaker than saltwater and marks a transition.
entries.definitionCN: 略咸的，如河水与海水混合处；比 saltwater 淡，标记的是过渡状态。

entries.definition: Water with little dissolved salt; it is the exact antonym that gives saltwater its meaning by contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解盐分很少的水；它正是通过对照赋予 saltwater 意义的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real salt and water roots, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 salt 与 water 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Salt plus water gives the compound, and the open form salt water is still common in ordinary prose.
normal.cn: salt 加 water 构成该复合词，普通散文中仍常见分写形式 salt water。

normal.en: Saltwater fish, saltwater marsh and saltwater intrusion are the standard technical collocations.
normal.cn: saltwater fish、saltwater marsh、saltwater intrusion 是标准技术搭配。

normal.en: Saline and salinity come from Latin sal, a cognate of English salt rather than its ancestor.
normal.cn: saline 与 salinity 来自拉丁 sal，是英语 salt 的同源词而非其祖形。

normal.en: The idiom saltwater sailor marks real sea experience, the opposite of freshwater sailor.
normal.cn: 习语 saltwater sailor 标记真实的海上经验，与 freshwater sailor 相反。

normal.en: Saltwater intrusion names the process by which the sea moves into coastal wells.
normal.cn: saltwater intrusion 指海水侵入沿海水井的过程。

abstract.en: Picture a field turning pale as the tide quietly salts the roots.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水悄悄给根系上盐，田地一点点褪成枯黄。

abstract.en: Picture an old sailor who can taste the reef before he sees it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老水手，还没看见礁石就先尝出了它的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a well that draws up the sea instead of the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一口井抽上来的不是雨水，而是海水。

examples.en: Saltwater covers most of the planet's surface but is unfit to drink.
examples.cn: 咸水覆盖了地球表面的大部分，却不能饮用。

examples.en: The marsh is fed by saltwater at every high tide.
examples.cn: 每次涨潮，咸水都会灌入这片沼泽。

examples.en: Overpumping the coastal wells invited saltwater intrusion.
examples.cn: 过量抽取沿海水井招来了海水入侵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「salt（盐）+ water（水）」——加了盐的水就是咸水；真正出过海的老水手也叫 saltwater sailor

root: 英语复合词：salt（古英语 sealt「盐」，日耳曼语 *saltaz，与拉丁 sal 同源）+ water（古英语 wæter）；英语词本身无拉丁来源，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the salt: water itself, the sea, its organisms, aquaculture, prepared brine, the invasion of coastal aquifers, saline wetlands, and finally the old sailor whose element is salt water.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「盐」展开：水本身、海水、其中的生物、海水养殖、人工盐水、沿海含水层入侵、咸水湿地，最后是以咸水为元素的老水手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water carrying enough salt to exclude ordinary life and ordinary crops.
core.cn: 核心意象：含盐量足以排除寻常生命与农作物的水。

branches.en: SALTY WATER ITSELF: the compound names the medium and its largest natural body.
branches.cn: 咸水本身：复合词命名介质及其最大的天然水体。

branches.en: LIFE AND CULTURE: organisms and their farming are labelled by salinity.
branches.cn: 生命与养殖：生物及其养殖按盐度被命名。

branches.en: BRINE: salt is added on purpose, turning water into a tool.
branches.cn: 盐水：盐被刻意加入，水变成工具。

branches.en: SALINE LANDSCAPES: intrusion and coastal marshes show salt water moving into land.
branches.cn: 咸水景观：入侵与海岸沼泽显示咸水向陆地推进。

branches.en: THE SAILOR'S ELEMENT: experience at sea is named by the water itself.
branches.cn: 水手的元素：海上经验直接以这种水命名。

intro.en: Saltwater is a native English compound whose parts, salt and water, also build saltwater fish, saltwater intrusion, saline, salty and salinity; the Latin sal is a cognate, not an ancestor.
intro.cn: saltwater 是英语本族复合词，其构件 salt 与 water 还构成 saltwater fish、saltwater intrusion、saline、salty 与 salinity；拉丁 sal 是同源词而非祖形。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is the source of saltwater. Latin sal 'salt' is a genuine cognate through Indo-European *sal-, and salinus yields English saline, but neither is an ancestor of this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词是 saltwater 的来源。拉丁 sal「盐」经印欧语 *sal- 确为同源词，salinus 衍生英语 saline，但两者都不是这个复合词的祖形。

items.meaning: sodium chloride; to preserve with salt
items.example: Salt preserves fish for months.
items.exampleCN: 盐能把鱼保存数月。

items.example: Water dissolves the salt in the estuary.
items.exampleCN: 水溶解河口处的盐。

items.example: Saltwater corrodes the old hull.
items.exampleCN: 海水腐蚀着旧船体。

items.example: Saltwater fish drink sea water continuously.
items.exampleCN: 海水鱼不断饮用海水。

items.example: Saltwater intrusion ruined three wells.
items.exampleCN: 海水入侵毁了三口水井。

items.meaning: a tidal marsh of salty water
items.example: Saltwater marsh grass holds the mud in place.
items.exampleCN: 咸水沼泽的草固定住泥滩。

items.example: The wind left a salty film on the windows.
items.exampleCN: 海风在窗上留下一层盐膜。

items.meaning: the amount of salt in water
items.example: Salinity rises where the river flow falls.
items.exampleCN: 河流流量下降处盐度上升。

items.example: The nurse hung a bag of saline.
items.exampleCN: 护士挂上一袋生理盐水。

definition_zh: 标准差；样本标准差；总体标准差；离散程度；波动幅度
definition_en: a statistical measure of how widely values spread around their mean, equal to the square root of the variance
core_image: 一条钟形曲线两侧的坡，坡越缓，数据离中心越远
scene: 老师在黑板上画出成绩分布，并标出数据偏离平均值的典型幅度。 A small standard deviation means the scores cluster near the average.
sceneCN: 这里指「衡量数据偏离平均值多远的统计量」（第 1 个义项：标准差）；句意为标准差小，说明分数都挤在平均值附近。可辨识物件：黑板、曲线、中心线、刻度。

pos.zh: 标准差；离散程度；波动幅度

senses.title: The statistical measure
senses.definition: the square root of the variance, expressing spread in the original units
senses.definitionCN: 方差的平方根，用原有单位表示离散程度
senses.example: A small standard deviation means the scores cluster near the average.
senses.exampleCN: 标准差小，说明分数都挤在平均值附近。
senses.why: Deviation is a turning off the road, and statistics uses it for distance from the mean; taking the square root returns the measure to ordinary units.
senses.whyCN: 「偏离」本指离开道路，统计学用它指离平均值的距离；开平方使这个量回到普通单位。

senses.title: The sample standard deviation
senses.definition: the estimate computed from a sample, usually with a divisor one less than the count
senses.definitionCN: 由样本算出的估计值，除数通常比个数少一
senses.example: The sample standard deviation was reported with the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把样本标准差与平均值一起列出。
senses.why: A sample is only part of a population, so its version carries a small correction in the divisor.
senses.whyCN: 样本只是总体的一部分，因此它的版本在除数上有一个小修正。

senses.title: The population standard deviation
senses.definition: the measure computed when every member of a population is known
senses.definitionCN: 已知总体每一个成员时算出的量
senses.example: The population standard deviation is often denoted by a single letter.
senses.exampleCN: 总体标准差常用一个希腊字母表示。
senses.why: With the whole population in hand there is nothing to correct, so the divisor is simply the count.
senses.whyCN: 手里有整个总体时无需修正，除数就是个数本身。

senses.title: A way of stating spread
senses.definition: a way of saying how far values typically lie from the centre
senses.definitionCN: 说明数值通常离中心多远的说法
senses.example: The two classes differ by one standard deviation in height.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个班的身高相差一个标准差。
senses.why: The measure is useful because it can be spoken of in units of itself, turning spread into a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个量好用，是因为可以用它自己的单位来说它，从而把离散变成一把尺。

senses.title: A measure of market volatility
senses.titleCN: 金融市场中的波动度量
senses.definition: a quantity used to express how much a price or return tends to move
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示价格或收益通常变动多少的量
senses.example: Traders quote the standard deviation of daily returns.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员报出日收益的标准差。
senses.why: Finance needs a single number for how far returns stray from their average, and the statistical measure supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 金融需要一个数来表示收益偏离平均多少，统计量正好提供。

senses.title: A process-control figure
senses.titleCN: 质量控制中的过程波动
senses.definition: a figure used in industry to describe how much a process varies around its target
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用来描述过程围绕目标值波动多少的量
senses.example: The line was stopped when the standard deviation exceeded the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 标准差超过限值时，生产线被停了下来。
senses.why: Manufacturing compares each batch with a target, and the measure turns that comparison into a control rule.
senses.whyCN: 制造把每批产品与目标比对，这个量把比对变成一条控制规则。

senses.title: A figure in error analysis
senses.titleCN: 误差分析中的离散指标
senses.definition: a quantity describing the scatter of repeated measurements
senses.definitionCN: 描述重复测量结果散布程度的量
senses.example: Repeated readings were reported with their standard deviation.
senses.exampleCN: 重复读数连同其标准差一起报告。
senses.why: Repeated measurements rarely agree exactly, and the measure summarises that disagreement in one number.
senses.whyCN: 重复测量很少完全一致，这个量把这种不一致收进一个数。

senses.title: The typical distance from the average
senses.titleCN: 抽象：偏离平均的典型幅度
senses.definition: a plain way of naming how far a thing usually stands from what is typical
senses.definitionCN: 用朴素说法指出某物通常离通常状态有多远
senses.example: In that family, lateness beyond a standard deviation was rare.
senses.exampleCN: 在那家人里，迟到超过一个典型幅度的情况很少见。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops the arithmetic and keeps the picture: a usual distance from the centre.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉算术，只保留画面：离中心的一段惯常距离。

intro.en: Standard deviation joins two words of different origin. Standard comes from Old French estandart 'rallying banner', from a Germanic compound meaning 'stand firm'; deviation comes from Latin deviare 'to turn off the road'. The statistical term was named in the late nineteenth century.
intro.cn: standard deviation 由两个来源不同的词合成。standard 出自古法语 estandart「集合旗」，再上溯一个意为「站稳」的日耳曼复合词；deviation 出自拉丁 deviare「离开道路」。这个统计术语在十九世纪后期得名。

items.en: The Germanic source meant 'stand firm, stand hard'. The form is reconstructed from the French and Germanic records, so it is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 其日耳曼来源意为「站稳、立定」。这一形式由法语与日耳曼语的书证重构而来，属重构形式，并非有直接记录的词。

items.en: Estandart named a rallying banner, the fixed point troops gathered around; English standard kept both the banner and the fixed-point senses.
items.cn: estandart 指集合旗，即部队聚集的固定点；英语 standard 同时保留「旗」与「固定点」两义。

items.en: Via meant 'way, road'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and any older root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: via 意为「道路」。其更早来源不确定，凡为其拟出的更古老词根都属假说。

items.en: De- 'off' plus via produced deviare 'to leave the road, stray'; deviatio named the straying.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 via 构成 deviare「离开道路、走偏」；deviatio 指这种偏离。

items.en: The phrase standard deviation was introduced in the 1890s in the circle of Karl Pearson to name the square root of the mean squared deviation; the naming is documented, though early uses vary.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪九十年代由皮尔逊一系学者引入，用来命名均方偏差的平方根；命名过程有文献可查，早期用法略有出入。

items.en: From statistics the term spread into finance, manufacturing and measurement, where it now names any typical distance from a target.
items.cn: 这个词从统计学扩散到金融、制造与测量，如今指任何离目标的惯常距离。

note.en: Group one holds technical neighbours whose names are easily confused with standard deviation; group two holds words for spread or departure.
note.cn: 第一组是名称极易与标准差混淆的技术近邻；第二组是表示散布或偏离的词。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of a sample's mean, not of the values themselves; it shrinks as the sample grows.
entries.definitionCN: 指样本平均值的标准差，而非各个数值的标准差；样本越大它越小。

entries.definition: A value expressed in units of standard deviation from the mean, also called a z-score.
entries.definitionCN: 用「离平均值多少个标准差」表示的值，也称 z 分数。

entries.definition: The distance of one value from the mean without squaring and without a square root.
entries.definitionCN: 单个值离平均值的距离，既不开方也不平方。

entries.definition: The average squared deviation; its square root is the standard deviation.
entries.definitionCN: 平方偏差的平均值；它的平方根就是标准差。

entries.definition: Any measure of how widely values are distributed, of which the standard deviation is one.
entries.definitionCN: 衡量数值分布宽窄的任何量，标准差只是其中一种。

entries.definition: The range or width of a distribution in ordinary language.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言里指一个分布的跨度或宽度。

entries.definition: The difference between the highest and lowest values, a cruder measure of spread.
entries.definitionCN: 最大值与最小值之差，是更粗疏的离散度量。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or a course, the plain word behind the technical phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或航道，是这个技术短语背后的普通词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase is two words: a fixed standard plus a turning off the road; statistics measures distance from the mean.
normal.cn: 这个短语由两个词组成：固定的标准，加一次离开道路；统计学用它量离平均值的距离。

normal.en: The measure is the square root of the variance, so the two always appear together.
normal.cn: 这个量是方差的平方根，因此两者总是成对出现。

normal.en: Standard error and standard score are neighbours with different jobs: one is about a mean, the other about a converted value.
normal.cn: 标准误与标准分数是职责不同的邻居：一个关于平均值，一个关于换算后的值。

normal.en: The usual shorthand is a pair of letters or a single Greek letter for the population version.
normal.cn: 常用简写是两个字母，或用一个希腊字母表示总体版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: sample standard deviation, within one standard deviation, daily returns.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：样本标准差、在一个标准差之内、日收益。

abstract.en: Picture a bell-shaped hill; a steep pair of slopes means everything stays near the top, a gentle pair means it wanders far.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟形的山丘：坡陡说明东西都留在山顶附近，坡缓说明它跑得很远。

abstract.en: Picture a target with shots scattered around the centre, most inside a ring of one width.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靶子，弹着点散在中心周围，多数落在宽度相同的一圈之内。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line where every batch must stay inside a band of fixed width, or the line stops.
abstract.cn: 想象一条生产线，每批产品都必须留在一条固定宽度的带子里，否则就停机。

examples.en: The report gives the mean and the standard deviation for each group.
examples.cn: 报告给出每一组的平均值与标准差。

examples.en: Returns moved by more than one standard deviation on that day.
examples.cn: 那天的收益变动超过了一个标准差。

examples.en: A wide standard deviation warns that the process is unstable.
examples.cn: 标准差偏大，说明这个过程不稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前一个词是「固定的标准」，后一个词是「离开道路」：合起来就是「各个数值通常离平均值多远」的量。它等于方差的平方根，用原有单位说话。

root: 复合术语。standard 出自古法语 estandart「集合旗」，再上溯意为「站稳」的日耳曼复合词，该形式为重构；deviation 出自拉丁 deviare「离开道路」＝ de-（离开）＋ via「道路」，via 更早来源不确定。统计义在十九世纪九十年代命名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure one thing: how far values usually stand from their centre. The same figure is then read as a sample estimate, a population value, a scale for comparison, a market volatility, a control limit, a measurement error and, at last, a plain typical distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量同一件事：各个数值通常离它们的中心多远。同一个量再依次读作样本估计、总体值、比较用的尺度、市场波动、控制限、测量误差，最后读作朴素的惯常距离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bell-shaped hill whose slopes show how far things wander from the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座钟形山丘，两侧的坡显示东西离山顶能跑多远。

branches.en: ONE NUMBER: the measure exists in sample and population versions that differ only in the divisor.
branches.cn: 一个数：这个量有样本与总体两个版本，只差除数。

branches.en: A SCALE: spread can be stated in units of itself, which also summarises measurement error.
branches.cn: 一把尺：离散可以用它自己的单位来说，这也顺带概括了测量误差。

branches.en: MARKET SWING: finance borrows the measure for how far returns stray.
branches.cn: 市场摆动：金融借用这个量表示收益偏离多远。

branches.en: CONTROL LIMIT: industry turns the measure into a rule that stops a line.
branches.cn: 控制限：工业把这个量变成一条停机的规则。

branches.en: TYPICAL DISTANCE: with the arithmetic dropped, it is simply how far things usually stand from the centre.
branches.cn: 惯常距离：去掉算术之后，它就是东西通常离中心多远。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Germanic noun and a Latin verb, so its parts come from two different families and should be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个日耳曼名词与一个拉丁动词构成，两部分来自不同词族，应分开来读。

latinIntro.en: Germanic stand gives standard; Latin via and deviare give deviate and deviation. The two halves meet only in the technical phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼语 stand 给出 standard；拉丁 via 与 deviare 给出 deviate 与 deviation。两半只在技术短语里相遇。

items.example: The Germanic root supplies the idea of standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「站稳」的意思。

items.structure: -ard (Germanic noun suffix, often pejorative or emphatic)
items.meaning: a person or thing marked by
items.example: The suffix forms the noun for a fixed rallying point.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示固定集合点的名词。

items.example: The French noun is the direct source of standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词是 standard 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a fixed rule or model; a banner
items.example: The standard was agreed in advance.
items.exampleCN: 标准是事先约定的。

items.example: The root supplies the road in deviation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 deviation 里的「道路」。

items.meaning: to leave the road; to stray
items.example: The verb pictures stepping off a road.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘离开道路的一步。

items.meaning: the act of straying from a course
items.example: The deviation was small.
items.exampleCN: 偏差很小。

items.example: Do not deviate from the plan.
items.exampleCN: 不要偏离计划。

items.example: A devious route avoids the checkpoint.
items.exampleCN: 绕行的路线避开了检查站。

definition_zh: 共识；共同意见；一致意见
definition_en: general agreement among a group, especially after discussion, or the view most people in a field hold
core_image: 一圈人围桌而坐，最后所有手都放在同一张纸上
scene: 表决之前，主持人再问一遍，无人再提出新的修改。 After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
sceneCN: 这里 consensus 指「一群人在讨论之后形成的共同意见」（第 1 个义项：群体内的一致）；句意为辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。可辨识物件：长桌、摊开的报告、举手表决前的沉默、记录本。

pos.zh: 共识；一致意见
（某领域）主流看法

senses.title: Agreement across a group
senses.titleCN: 一个群体内部的共同意见
senses.definition: a general agreement reached by the members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一群成员形成的普遍一致
senses.example: After two days of debate, the committee reached a consensus on the wording of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论两天之后，委员会就报告的措辞达成了共识。
senses.why: Latin consensus simply meant 'agreement', and English kept that breadth: the noun names the state without saying how it was reached.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 consensus 本来就只表示「一致」，英语保留了这个宽度：这个名词命名状态，不说明它是怎么达成的。

senses.title: The view most people hold
senses.definition: the opinion that prevails in a field or a population at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或人群在某一时期占上风的看法
senses.example: The consensus in the field is that the warming is real.
senses.exampleCN: 该领域的主流看法是变暖确实在发生。
senses.why: when a shared view becomes the background assumption, consensus means the default position rather than a fresh agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当共同看法变成背景假设，consensus 指的就是默认立场，而不是新达成的协议。

senses.title: Agreement produced by talk
senses.titleCN: 经讨论而非表决形成的一致
senses.definition: a shared position arrived at through discussion rather than through a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨论而非正式表决得到的共同立场
senses.example: Consensus was reached without a formal ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 没有正式投票就形成了共识。
senses.why: meetings needed a word for agreement that is felt in the room before it is counted, and this noun supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 会议需要一个词，来形容那种先在会场里被感觉到、之后才被计数的同意，这个名词正好补上。

senses.title: Agreement among experts
senses.definition: the settled judgement of specialists in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域专门研究者已定下来的判断
senses.example: Scientific consensus on the age of the rock took decades to form.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这块岩石年龄的科学共识，花了几十年才形成。
senses.why: science does not vote, but it does converge, and the noun describes that convergence without implying unanimity.
senses.whyCN: 科学不作表决，却会收敛；这个名词描述这种收敛，但并不暗示全体一致。

senses.title: Sympathy among body parts
senses.titleCN: 旧医学：身体各部分的同感
senses.definition: an old physiological notion that the organs act in sympathy with one another
senses.definitionCN: 旧生理学中的观念：各器官彼此同感相应
senses.example: Early physicians wrote of a consensus among the organs.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医生写到各器官之间的同感。
senses.why: the Latin noun was borrowed first for bodily sympathy, because parts that act together were said to feel together.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最早被借用来指身体各部的同感，因为共同起作用的部位被说成「一同感受」。

senses.title: Cross-party agreement
senses.definition: a shared position adopted by rival political groups
senses.definitionCN: 对立政治团体共同采取的立场
senses.example: A consensus emerged between the parties on health funding.
senses.exampleCN: 各党在医疗拨款上出现了共同立场。
senses.why: politics uses the word precisely when rivals stop contesting an issue, which is agreement seen as a truce.
senses.whyCN: 政界在对手停止争夺某议题时才用这个词，那是把一致看作停战。

senses.title: A process short of unanimity
senses.titleCN: 不要求全体赞成的一致程序
senses.definition: a decision method in which no one blocks a proposal, though not everyone need approve it
senses.definitionCN: 一种决定方式：无人阻止提议，尽管并非人人都赞成
senses.example: Consensus decision-making does not mean everyone must agree.
senses.exampleCN: 共识决策并不等于人人都必须赞成。
senses.why: groups that cannot afford majority rule redefine consensus as the absence of objection, and the noun follows them.
senses.whyCN: 无法承受多数决的团体，把共识重新定义为「无人反对」，这个名词也跟着这样用。

senses.title: The averaged professional forecast
senses.titleCN: 市场或预测中的平均预期
senses.definition: the central estimate that analysts or forecasters collectively expect
senses.definitionCN: 分析师或预测者集体预期的中心估计
senses.example: The consensus forecast puts growth at two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 市场平均预期把增长定在百分之二。
senses.why: finance takes the many separate views and treats their middle as one voice, which is consensus by aggregation.
senses.whyCN: 金融界把许多分散的看法取其中间，当作一个声音，这是靠汇总得到的共识。

intro.en: Consensus is a Latin noun built on consentire 'to feel together', from com- 'together' and sentire 'to feel'. English borrowed it in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consensus 是一个拉丁名词，出自 consentire「一同感受」，由 com-「共同」与 sentire「感受」构成。英语在十七世纪借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think', and it also gives English sense, sentiment and sentence through related Latin forms.
items.cn: sentire 意为「感觉、知觉、思考」，它还经相关的拉丁形式衍生出英语的 sense、sentiment 与 sentence。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire produced consentire, 'to feel together, to be of one mind, to agree'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire 构成 consentire，意为「一同感受、心意相同、同意」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun consensus named the state of feeling together: agreement, accord, harmony.
items.cn: 第四变格法名词 consensus 命名「一同感受」的状态：一致、和谐、同心。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century, first in learned writing about the body and about philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最初见于关于身体与哲学的学术写作。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries it meant general agreement in any group, and later produced the political phrase consensus politics.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，它指任何群体中的普遍一致，后来又产生「共识政治」这一说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest English example is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the deeper pre-Latin shape of sentire is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：各家词典对最早的英语书证年代说法不一；sentire 在拉丁语之前的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like consensus but belong to other Latin families; group two holds nouns for collective agreement, each with a different width.
note.cn: 第一组收形似 consensus、却属于别的拉丁词族的词；第二组收表示集体一致的名词，覆盖面各不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin censere 'to assess, estimate', the verb behind censorship and censor: a counting of the population, not a state of agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 censere「评估、估算」，也是 censorship 与 censor 背后的动词：指人口清点，而非意见一致。

entries.definition: Built on the same consentire, but it names permission given by one party rather than agreement across a group.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 consentire，但它指一方给出的许可，而非一群人的普遍一致。

entries.definition: The adjective of this noun: resting on mutual consent, used of contracts, relations and shared reality.
entries.definitionCN: 本名词的形容词：以双方同意为基础，用于合同、关系与共同认定的现实。

entries.definition: A compound naming the work of bringing a group to a shared position before a decision.
entries.definitionCN: 由本名词构成的复合词，指在决定之前把一群人带到共同立场的工作。

entries.definition: Complete agreement of all members; consensus can exist without every member approving.
entries.definitionCN: 全体成员完全一致；而 consensus 可以在并非人人赞成时存在。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between parties, often states; it is an instrument, where consensus is a state of mind.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式协定，常指国家间；它是一份文书，而 consensus 是一种心态。

entries.definition: The part of a question on which opponents already agree; it need not cover the whole issue.
entries.definitionCN: 争论各方已经同意的那一部分；它不必覆盖整个议题。

entries.definition: The opinion held by more than half; it is a matter of numbers, whereas consensus is a matter of acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 超过半数持有的意见；它靠数人头，而 consensus 靠接受程度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Com- 'together' plus sentire 'feel': to feel together, hence to agree.
normal.cn: com-「共同」加 sentire「感受」：一同感受，因而同意。

normal.en: The family runs consensus, consensual, consent, consenting, consensus-building.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 consensus、consensual、consent、consenting、consensus-building。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the scale: broad consensus, scientific consensus, the consensus view.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出规模：广泛共识、科学共识、主流看法。

normal.en: The plural is consensuses, since the Latin fourth-declension ending does not survive in English.
normal.cn: 复数是 consensuses，因为拉丁第四变格法的词尾在英语中没有保留。

normal.en: The near relative census comes from a different verb and means a count, not an agreement.
normal.cn: 形近的 census 出自另一个动词，意为清点，而非一致。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs in which every person finally leans the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，最后每个人都朝同一个方向倾身。

abstract.en: Picture many small streams joining into one wide, slow river.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小溪汇成一条宽而缓的河。

abstract.en: Picture a room going quiet not because anyone was silenced but because no one wished to speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子安静下来，不是有人被制止，而是无人再想开口。

examples.en: No consensus emerged, so the chair postponed the vote.
examples.cn: 没有形成共识，于是主席推迟了表决。

examples.en: The consensus among clinicians is to wait another week.
examples.cn: 临床医生之间的共识是再等一周。

examples.en: Consensus in a large group often hides two or three determined minorities.
examples.cn: 大团体里的共识，常常掩盖着两三个坚定的少数派。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ sensus（感觉）」——大家感觉一样 → 共识

root: 拉丁 consensus「一致」出自 consentire「一同感受」= com-（共同）+ sentire（感受）；英语十七世纪借入，最初用于生理与哲学论述。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a room reaching agreement to a market averaging forecasts: the same noun covers a feeling shared by bodies, by committees, by experts and by traders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一间屋子里达成一致，一直到市场把预测取平均：同一个名词涵盖身体、委员会、专家与交易者所共享的那种「同感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people at one table, every hand finally resting on the same sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈人围着一张桌子，最后所有手都落在同一张纸上。

branches.en: THE ROOM: agreement in a group, produced by talk rather than by a count.
branches.cn: 会场：群体中的一致，由谈话而非计数产生。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the prevailing view, and the settled judgement of specialists.
branches.cn: 领域：占上风的看法，以及专家已定下的判断。

branches.en: THE BODY: the oldest loan sense, where organs are said to feel together.
branches.cn: 身体：最早的借入义，器官被说成一同感受。

branches.en: POLITICS: rivals stop contesting, and a process treats silence as consent.
branches.cn: 政治：对手停止争夺，而某种程序把沉默当作同意。

branches.en: THE MARKET: many forecasts averaged into one voice.
branches.cn: 市场：许多预测被平均成一个声音。

intro.en: Consensus is a Latin noun whose prefix and root both survive in English, so the whole word can be read as 'feeling together'.
intro.cn: consensus 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根都留存于英语，因此整词可以读作「一同感受」。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire gives sense, sentiment, consent and consensus, while com- adds the sense of doing something together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 衍生 sense、sentiment、consent 与 consensus，而 com- 增添「共同」之意。

items.example: The prefix makes the feeling shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「感受」成为共享的。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of feeling.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「感受」的意思。

items.example: The verb underlies both consent and consensus.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 consent 与 consensus 的共同底子。

items.example: The committee reached a consensus.
items.exampleCN: 委员会达成了共识。

items.example: The contract is consensual.
items.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同。

items.structure: com- + sentire, as a noun and verb
items.example: She gave her consent in writing.
items.exampleCN: 她以书面形式表示同意。

items.example: The consenting parties signed separately.
items.exampleCN: 表示同意的各方分别签署。

items.example: Consensus-building took most of the week.
items.exampleCN: 凝聚共识占了这一周的大部分时间。

items.example: The word has a narrow sense here.
items.exampleCN: 这个词在这里是窄义。

items.example: Public sentiment turned against the plan.
items.exampleCN: 公众情绪转而反对该方案。

definition_zh: 被保险人；投保的；受保障的
definition_en: a person or thing covered by insurance; covered by insurance
core_image: 一个人身上披着一件印有保险公司标志的长斗篷，斗篷上写着 covered
scene: 奶奶住院的医疗费大部分被报销了，她感叹幸好五年前买了那一份保险。 The insured received the full payment promised in the policy.
sceneCN: 这里 insured 指「被保险人」（第 1 个义项：被保险保障覆盖的人）；句意为 insured 收到了保单承诺的全额赔付。图中可辨识物件：医院收据、保险单、报销支票。

pos.zh: 投保的；受保障的
被保险人（可数）

senses.title: person covered by insurance
senses.definition: a person who has bought insurance and is protected against specified losses
senses.definitionCN: 购买了保险并在特定损失下受到保护的人
senses.example: The insured must pay premiums every month.
senses.exampleCN: 被保险人每月都要交保费。
senses.why: insure + -ed = one who has been insured.
senses.whyCN: insure 加 -ed 就是被 insure 过的人。

senses.title: property covered
senses.definition: a house, car or other asset covered by insurance
senses.definitionCN: 被保险覆盖的房屋、汽车或其他资产
senses.example: The insured was destroyed in the hurricane.
senses.exampleCN: 被保险的财产在飓风中被毁。
senses.why: In practice, insured can name the thing as well as the person.
senses.whyCN: 在实际使用中，insured 可以指物也可以指人。

senses.title: group insured under one policy
senses.definition: multiple people covered under a single group policy
senses.definitionCN: 在一张团体保单下被保障的多人
senses.example: All employees became insured under the company plan.
senses.exampleCN: 所有员工都被公司计划纳入保障。
senses.why: A group policy covers many insureds at once.
senses.whyCN: 一张团体保单同时覆盖许多 insured。

senses.title: fully insured
senses.definition: having insurance that covers the full value or risk
senses.definitionCN: 拥有覆盖全部价值或风险的保险的
senses.example: He was fully insured before taking the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发旅行前他全额投保了。
senses.why: The adjective sense describes the state of being covered.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义描述被保障的状态。

senses.title: self-insured
senses.definition: setting aside your own money to cover losses, not buying insurance
senses.definitionCN: 自己留钱赔损失，而不是买保险
senses.example: Large firms often remain self-insured for small risks.
senses.exampleCN: 大公司常对小风险实行自保。
senses.why: You are your own insurer, so you are self-insured.
senses.whyCN: 你自己就是自己的 insurer，所以你是 self-insured。

senses.title: named insured
senses.definition: a specific person or entity explicitly named in the policy
senses.definitionCN: 保单中明确指名的个人或实体
senses.example: The named insured was the company, not its directors.
senses.exampleCN: 指名被保险人是公司，不是其董事。
senses.why: Policies distinguish the named from additional insureds.
senses.whyCN: 保单区分指名被保险人和附加被保险人。

senses.title: additional insured
senses.definition: someone added to the policy after the named insured
senses.definitionCN: 在指名被保险人之后被加入保单的人
senses.example: The contractor added the client as an additional insured.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商把客户加为附加被保险人。
senses.why: Additional layers of protection, still insured.
senses.whyCN: 额外的保障层，仍然是 insured。

senses.title: uninsured counterpoint
senses.definition: the opposite of uninsured; a person or thing without cover
senses.definitionCN: uninsured 的反面；没有保障的人或物
senses.example: More than ten percent of drivers remain uninsured.
senses.exampleCN: 超过一成的司机没有投保。
senses.why: By contrast: insured and uninsured form a pair.
senses.whyCN: 对比之下：insured 和 uninsured 构成一对。

intro.en: Insured is the past participle of insure, used as an adjective and noun: 'having been made safe (against loss)'.
intro.cn: insured 是 insure 的过去分词，用作形容词和名词：「已经被使安全（免受损失）的」。

items.en: insure (verb) + -ed (past participle suffix) = insured.
items.cn: insure（动词）+ -ed（过去分词后缀）= insured。

items.en: By the 17th century insured was used as an adjective meaning 'covered by insurance'.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪 insured 已用作形容词，意为「被保险覆盖的」。

items.en: Using the participle as a noun is common in English: the insured = the person insured.
items.cn: 英语里把分词用作名词很常见：the insured = 被保险的那个人。

items.en: Compounds like uninsured, self-insured, underinsured developed later.
items.cn: uninsured、self-insured、underinsured 等复合词后来才出现。

items.en: Insurant, another noun form, is borrowed from French and is less common.
items.cn: insurant 是另一个名词形式，借自法语，较少用。

items.en: All etymology straightforward; no disputed roots.
items.cn: 词源直接明了，无争议词根。

note.en: Look-alikes are other -ed participles of sure-family verbs; near meanings are related parties in insurance.
note.cn: 形近是 sure 家族动词的其他 -ed 分词；近义是保险中的相关方。

entries.definition: Past participle of ensure 'make certain'; not financial.
entries.definitionCN: ensure「使确定」的过去分词；与财务无关。

entries.definition: Past participle of assure; also means confident.
entries.definitionCN: assure 的过去分词；也指自信的。

entries.definition: Certain, not a participle.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的，不是分词。

entries.definition: Not covered by insurance.
entries.definitionCN: 没有被保险覆盖的。

entries.definition: Same meaning as insured, borrowed from French insurant.
entries.definitionCN: 与 insured 同义的法语借词。

entries.definition: One who receives the insurance payment; not necessarily the insured.
entries.definitionCN: 接收保险赔付的人；不一定是 insured。

entries.definition: The one who owns and pays for the policy; usually also the insured.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并支付保单的人；通常也是 insured。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes and real pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实配对。

normal.en: insure + -ed past participle → insured = one who has been insured.
normal.cn: insure 加 -ed 过去分词 → insured = 被保险过的人。

normal.en: insured ↔ insurer: one is covered, the other covers.
normal.cn: insured ↔ insurer：一个被保障，一个去保障。

normal.en: insure ↔ ensure ↔ assure: all share sure, split into finance / certainty / reassurance.
normal.cn: insure ↔ ensure ↔ assure：都来自 sure，分成财务 / 确定 / 安慰。

normal.en: Compound opposites: insured vs uninsured, fully insured vs underinsured.
normal.cn: 复合反义词：insured vs uninsured，fully insured vs underinsured。

normal.en: Named insured vs additional insured on a policy.
normal.cn: 保单上的 named insured vs additional insured。

abstract.en: Picture a cloak that protects whoever wears it: insured = the wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件斗篷，谁穿上就保护谁；insured = 穿的人。

abstract.en: Picture a policy as a contract between insured and insurer, with coins in a pot between them.
abstract.cn: 想象保单是 insured 和 insurer 之间的合同，中间有一罐子硬币。

abstract.en: Picture the opposite: uninsured = standing out in the rain without an umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象对立面：uninsured = 没伞站在雨里。

examples.en: The insurer denied the claim because the insured had failed to disclose a prior condition.
examples.cn: 保险公司拒赔，因为被保险人未披露既往病史。

examples.en: Once the building was insured, the owner could relax a little about the fire risk.
examples.cn: 大楼一投保，业主对火灾风险就能松一口气。

examples.en: Self-insured employers set aside funds instead of buying a group health plan.
examples.cn: 自保的雇主自己留钱而不是购买团体健康险。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold: person covered → property covered → group under one policy → fully covered adjective → self-insured → named insured → additional insured → contrast with uninsured.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展开：被保障的人 → 被保障的财产 → 一张保单下的群体 → fully 形容词 → 自保 → 指名被保险人 → 附加被保险人 → 与 uninsured 对比。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wearing a protective cloak labelled INSURED; coins are placed in the cloak pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人穿着标有 INSURED 的保护斗篷，口袋里放着硬币。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the insured party is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 人：被保险的当事人是核心名词义。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND GROUPS: insured covers objects too, and groups under one policy.
branches.cn: 财产与群体：insured 也指物，也指一张保单下的群体。

branches.en: THE ADJECTIVE STATE: fully covered.
branches.cn: 形容词状态：被充分覆盖的。

branches.en: SELF-INSURED: you yourself act as your own insurer.
branches.cn: 自保：你自己就是自己的 insurer。

branches.en: CONTRACTUAL ROLES AND CONTRAST: named, additional, and the opposite uninsured.
branches.cn: 合同角色与对比：指名、附加，以及反义词 uninsured。

intro.en: insured = insure + -ed (past participle). insure = in- + sure.
intro.cn: insured = insure + -ed（过去分词）。insure = in- + sure。

latinIntro.cn: sure ← 拉丁 securus；in- 来自拉丁语；-ed 是古英语过去分词。
