definition_zh: 超新星；恒星生命终结时的剧烈爆发；也指爆发后的天体
definition_en: the explosive end of a star's life, or the extremely bright object produced by that explosion
core_image: 一颗星在几天里亮到能在白天看见，随后把外壳炸成一圈不断扩散的光环
scene: 记录一颗突然亮到白天可见的星，你说 That supernova outshone its whole galaxy.
sceneCN: 这里 supernova 指「恒星终结时的剧烈爆发」（第 1 个义项：恒星爆发的整体事件）；句意为那颗超新星比整个星系还亮。图中可辨识物件：极亮的星点、被照亮的星系旋臂、扩散的光环、观测记录。

pos.zh: 超新星（复数 supernovae 或 supernovas）

collocations.phrase: the light curve of a supernova

derivatives.zh: nova 为拉丁「新」，指新星；supernova 是在其前加 super- 形成的复合词
supernova + remnant：超新星遗迹，爆发后残留的膨胀气体
supernova 的拉丁式复数，见 forms
super- + luminous：超亮的；同一前缀的平行构词

senses.title: The explosive death of a star
senses.titleCN: 恒星生命终结时的剧烈爆发
senses.definition: the catastrophic explosion that ends the life of certain stars
senses.definitionCN: 某些恒星终结生命时的灾难性爆发
senses.example: That supernova outshone its whole galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗超新星比整个星系还亮。
senses.why: the name says what it is: nova is Latin for 'new', and super- marks an event far brighter than an ordinary new star.
senses.whyCN: 名字直说其性质：nova 是拉丁语「新」，super- 标出比普通「新星」亮得多的事件。

senses.title: A thermonuclear runaway
senses.titleCN: 热核失控：白矮星吸积后整体爆炸
senses.definition: a supernova produced when a white dwarf gains too much mass and detonates
senses.definitionCN: 白矮星吸积过多质量后整体引爆产生的超新星
senses.example: A Type Ia supernova destroys the white dwarf completely.
senses.exampleCN: Ia 型超新星把白矮星彻底摧毁。
senses.why: this type has no collapsing core but a runaway fusion front, which is why its light is so uniform.
senses.whyCN: 这一类没有坍缩的核心，而是失控的聚变前沿，因此亮度异常一致。

senses.title: A collapsing massive star
senses.titleCN: 大质量恒星核心坍缩引发的爆发
senses.definition: a supernova produced when the core of a massive star collapses and the outer layers rebound
senses.definitionCN: 大质量恒星核心坍缩、外层回弹引发的爆发
senses.example: A core-collapse supernova leaves a neutron star or a black hole.
senses.exampleCN: 核心坍缩型超新星会留下中子星或黑洞。
senses.why: the core falls inward in less than a second, and the rebound sends a shock through the envelope.
senses.whyCN: 核心在不到一秒内向内塌陷，回弹把冲击波送过外层。

senses.title: The remnant it leaves
senses.titleCN: 爆发留下的遗迹与膨胀气体
senses.definition: the expanding shell of gas and dust left behind by the explosion
senses.definitionCN: 爆炸留下的膨胀气体与尘埃壳
senses.example: The supernova remnant is still expanding after centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个超新星遗迹在几百年后仍在膨胀。
senses.why: remnant is what remains: the star is gone, but the shell keeps moving outward and carries the story.
senses.whyCN: remnant 即残留：恒星已不在，壳层仍向外运动，带着这段历史。

senses.title: A brightness standard
senses.titleCN: 作为亮度标准的超新星
senses.definition: a supernova used as a standard candle to measure cosmic distances
senses.definitionCN: 被当作标准烛光来测量宇宙距离的超新星
senses.example: Type Ia supernovae let astronomers measure far galaxies.
senses.exampleCN: Ia 型超新星让天文学家测量遥远星系。
senses.why: because the peak brightness is nearly the same each time, the event becomes a ruler rather than a curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 由于每次峰值亮度几乎相同，这一事件就从奇观变成了量尺。

senses.title: A factory for heavy elements
senses.definition: an event in which fusion and explosive burning create elements heavier than iron
senses.definitionCN: 在其中通过聚变与爆炸燃烧生成比铁更重元素的事件
senses.example: Gold in the earth was forged in supernovae and mergers.
senses.exampleCN: 地球上的金在超新星与并合事件中被锻造。
senses.why: iron is the end of ordinary fusion, so only an explosion can push nuclei past it.
senses.whyCN: 铁是普通聚变的终点，只有爆炸才能把原子核推向更远处。

senses.title: A recorded historical event
senses.titleCN: 历史上被记录下来的爆发
senses.definition: a dated supernova recorded by observers, used to date and to test models
senses.definitionCN: 被观测者记录下来的带日期超新星，用于断代与检验模型
senses.example: Chinese astronomers recorded a supernova in 1054.
senses.exampleCN: 中国天文学家记录了 1054 年的一次超新星爆发。
senses.why: a supernova can be seen in daylight, so old records exist across cultures and serve as fixed points.
senses.whyCN: 超新星可在白天看见，因此各文化都留有记录，可作固定参照点。

senses.title: Figurative: a spectacular burst
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：惊人的骤然爆发
senses.definition: a figurative use for a sudden, spectacular rise or outburst
senses.definitionCN: 比喻突然而惊人的上升或爆发
senses.example: The launch was a supernova of publicity.
senses.exampleCN: 那次发布是宣传上的一次超新星。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps two features: suddenness and a brilliance that outshines everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留两个特征：突然，以及盖过周围一切的光亮。

intro.en: Supernova is super- 'above, beyond' plus nova, Latin for 'new', from the phrase stella nova 'new star'. The term was coined in twentieth-century astrophysics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: supernova 是 super-「在上、超出」加 nova「新的」，后者出自短语 stella nova「新星」。这个术语产生于 20 世纪天体物理学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Novus 'new' gave the adjective nova in stella nova 'new star', the label early observers used for a star that suddenly appeared.
items.cn: novus「新的」在短语 stella nova「新星」中给出形容词 nova，那是早期观测者对突然出现的恒星所用的称呼。

items.en: Nova became a noun in its own right, naming such an apparition; the plural is novae.
items.cn: nova 独立成为名词，指这类突然出现的天体；复数为 novae。

items.en: Super is the Latin preposition and prefix 'above, over, beyond', also seen in superior and superimpose.
items.cn: super 是拉丁介词与前置成分「在上、超过」，也见于 superior 与 superimpose。

items.en: Supernova is generally attributed to the 1930s, when Walter Baade and Fritz Zwicky needed a term for explosions far more luminous than ordinary novae.
items.cn: 一般认为 supernova 于 1930 年代被造出，当时沃尔特·巴德与弗里茨·兹威基需要一个词，指比普通新星亮得多的爆发。

items.en: The division into thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae was established later in the twentieth century as spectra and light curves were classified.
items.cn: 热核型与核心坍缩型的划分在 20 世纪后期随光谱与光变曲线的分类而确立。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European source of novus is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the exact year of the coinage is not documented, and the 1930s attribution is generally believed rather than proven.
items.cn: 词根存疑：novus 的印欧来源属重构。仅首见年代存疑：造词的确切年份没有文献记录，1930 年代的说法一般认为成立但未获证明。

note.en: Group one holds the stellar-explosion terms that are routinely confused; group two holds the related objects and the figurative near-equivalents.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的恒星爆发术语；第二组是相关天体与比喻近义词。

entries.definition: A nova is a thermonuclear flash on a white dwarf's surface that leaves the star intact; a supernova destroys or collapses the star.
entries.definitionCN: 新星是白矮星表面的热核闪光，恒星仍存；超新星则毁掉或坍缩恒星。

entries.definition: The expanding debris after the event; it names the aftermath, not the explosion itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指事件之后膨胀的碎片，是余烬而非爆发本身。

entries.definition: An informal term for an especially energetic core collapse, sometimes linked to long gamma-ray bursts; it is not a standard classification.
entries.definitionCN: 对特别高能的核心坍缩的非正式说法，有时与长伽马射线暴相关；不是标准分类。

entries.definition: A plain description covering any explosive stellar event; supernova is the classified term.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何恒星爆发事件的朴素说法；supernova 是分类学术语。

entries.definition: One possible end product of a core-collapse supernova, not the event itself.
entries.definitionCN: 核心坍缩型超新星可能留下的产物之一，并非事件本身。

entries.definition: A brief flash of gamma rays from distant sources; some accompany supernovae but the terms are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 来自遥远源的短暂伽马射线闪；有些与超新星相伴，但两个术语不能互换。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: super- 'beyond' + nova 'new': a new star beyond all others.
normal.cn: super-「超出」+ nova「新」：超出一切的新星。

normal.en: Two main types: thermonuclear and core-collapse.
normal.cn: 两大类：热核型与核心坍缩型。

normal.en: The remnant is the expanding shell left behind.
normal.cn: 遗迹就是留下的膨胀壳层。

normal.en: The plural keeps the Latin: supernovae.
normal.cn: 复数保留拉丁式：supernovae。

normal.en: Type Ia works as a standard candle.
normal.cn: Ia 型可作标准烛光。

abstract.en: Picture one lamp flaring so brightly that the whole street looks lit for a night.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯突然亮到整条街像被照亮一夜。

abstract.en: Picture a shell of smoke still expanding long after the fire is out.
abstract.cn: 想象火早已熄灭，烟壳仍在向外扩散。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet career that explodes into fame in a single week.
abstract.cn: 想象一段平静的事业在一周内炸成名声。

examples.en: A supernova can briefly outshine the galaxy that hosts it.
examples.cn: 超新星能短暂地比宿主星系更亮。

examples.en: The supernova remnant expands into the surrounding gas.
examples.cn: 超新星遗迹向周围气体中膨胀。

examples.en: Astronomers use Type Ia supernovae to measure cosmic distances.
examples.cn: 天文学家使用 Ia 型超新星测量宇宙距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super（超级）+ nova（新）」——超级新的星 → 超新星

root: 拉丁 super「在上、超出」+ nova「新的」（出自 stella nova「新星」，novus 为「新」）；术语一般认为于 1930 年代由巴德与兹威基提出。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one explosion: a star dies, then the two mechanisms that cause it, the shell it leaves, the brightness used as a ruler, the elements it forges, the records it leaves in history and finally the image of any spectacular sudden burst.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一场爆炸展开：一颗星死去；再分两种机制、留下的壳层、被当作量尺的亮度、被锻造的元素、留在史册的记录，最后是任何惊人骤爆的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one point flaring brighter than a whole galaxy, then a shell drifting outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点亮过整个星系，随后一圈壳层向外漂去。

branches.en: THE EVENT: a star's life ends in a single catastrophic release.
branches.cn: 事件本身：恒星的生命在一次灾难性释放中结束。

branches.en: TWO MECHANISMS: a white dwarf detonates, or a massive core collapses.
branches.cn: 两种机制：白矮星引爆，或大质量核心坍缩。

branches.en: THE AFTERMATH: the expanding shell that keeps the record.
branches.cn: 余烬：继续携带记录的膨胀壳层。

branches.en: A MEASURABLE AND DATED LIGHT: a standard candle, and a recorded event.
branches.cn: 可测且有日期的光：标准烛光与被记录的事件。

branches.en: FORGED ELEMENTS AND THE METAPHOR: matter made in the blast, and any brilliant sudden rise.
branches.cn: 锻造的元素与比喻：爆炸中生成物质，以及任何耀眼的骤升。

intro.en: Supernova is a Latin prefix plus a Latin adjective turned noun, and the whole family stays close to its Latin shapes.
intro.cn: supernova 是拉丁前缀加一个转为名词的拉丁形容词，整个词族都紧贴拉丁词形。

latinIntro.en: Latin super gives superimpose and superior; Latin novus gives novel, innovate and nova itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 super 给出 superimpose 与 superior；拉丁 novus 给出 novel、innovate 与 nova 本身。

items.example: The prefix marks an event beyond the ordinary class.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出超出普通类别的事件。

items.example: Nova began as an adjective in stella nova.
items.exampleCN: nova 最初是 stella nova 中的形容词。

items.example: The root supplies novel and innovate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出 novel 与 innovate。

items.meaning: a star exploding beyond nova brightness
items.example: The compound was coined in astrophysics.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在天体物理学中被造出。

items.example: Astronomers often prefer the Latin plural.

definition_zh: 差距；悬殊；不平等；不一致；差异
definition_en: a clear and often unfair difference in amount, level or treatment between two or more groups or things
core_image: 一条被两端拉开的橡皮尺，刻度越拉越疏，尺子两头各站着一群人
scene: 同一座城市里，两个街区的收入曲线越拉越开，一边不断盖起新楼，一边仍是旧屋。 The report measured the widening disparity between the two districts.
sceneCN: 这里指两个群体在收入与发展水平上的明显落差（第 1 个义项：群体之间可测量的差距）；句意为报告测量了两个街区之间不断扩大的差距。图中可辨识物件：两排新旧不同的房屋、一道逐渐变宽的缝隙、一份摊开的报表。

pos.zh: 差距；悬殊；不平等；不一致

derivatives.zh: 同一词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「迥然不同的；不相干的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以迥然不同的方式」
由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「互不相同的性质」

senses.title: A measurable gap between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体之间可测量的落差
senses.definition: a difference in amount or level between two groups that can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 两个群体在数量或水平上可以被测量、比较的差别
senses.example: The disparity between urban and rural incomes has drawn public attention.
senses.exampleCN: 城乡收入的差距已经引起公众关注。
senses.why: The Latin word meant simply unequal; the noun keeps that neutral arithmetic sense of two things failing to match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本义就是「不相等」；这个名词保留了「两者对不上」的中性算术含义。

senses.title: Unequal distribution of money
senses.definition: the unequal spread of income, wealth or assets across a population
senses.definitionCN: 收入、财富或资产在一国人口中分配不均
senses.example: Wealth disparity inside the country grew faster than average income.
senses.exampleCN: 该国境内的财富悬殊比平均收入的增长更快。
senses.why: Once the gap is counted in money, the word takes on the policy charge of unfair distribution.
senses.whyCN: 一旦差距用金钱来衡量，这个词就带上了「分配不公」的政策色彩。

senses.title: Regional development imbalance
senses.definition: a persistent difference in prosperity, services or infrastructure between regions
senses.definitionCN: 不同地区在繁荣程度、公共服务或基础设施上的持续差别
senses.example: Regional disparity in hospital funding remains wide.
senses.exampleCN: 各地区在医院拨款上的差距依然很大。
senses.why: The noun was extended from people to places: a map can also be pulled out of shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从人群扩展到地方：一张地图同样可以被拉得变形。

senses.title: Gender gap
senses.definition: a difference between men and women in pay, promotion, health or representation
senses.definitionCN: 男女在薪酬、晋升、健康或代表性上的差别
senses.example: The study linked the gender disparity in promotions to biased review criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把晋升中的性别差距归因于有偏向的评审标准。
senses.why: Social statistics gave the old word a new pair of columns, one for each sex.
senses.whyCN: 社会统计给这个旧词添了一对新栏目，男女各占一栏。

senses.title: Racial and ethnic difference
senses.definition: a difference in outcomes or treatment that falls along racial or ethnic lines
senses.definitionCN: 结果或待遇上沿种族、族裔界线出现的差别
senses.example: Racial disparity in school discipline has been documented for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 学校纪律处分中的种族差异已被记录了数十年。
senses.why: Where the two groups are named by race or ethnicity, the neutral gap becomes evidence of unequal treatment.
senses.whyCN: 当两组人按种族或族裔来命名时，中性的落差就变成了待遇不公的证据。

senses.title: Health outcome gap
senses.definition: a difference in illness, access to care or life expectancy between populations
senses.definitionCN: 不同人群在患病率、就医机会或预期寿命上的差别
senses.example: Health disparity between insured and uninsured patients widened during the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 传染病流行期间，有保险与无保险患者之间的健康差距扩大了。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word to describe bodies that receive unequal care, not unequal numbers.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词，用来描述得到不平等照护的身体，而不是不平等的数字。

senses.title: Unequal access to opportunity
senses.definition: an uneven chance to obtain schooling, jobs or advancement
senses.definitionCN: 获得教育、工作或上升通道的机会不均等
senses.example: Educational disparity begins before children enter school.
senses.exampleCN: 教育机会的差距在孩子入学之前就已开始。
senses.why: The gap is no longer a result but a starting line drawn in different places.
senses.whyCN: 这时的差距不再是结果，而是一条画在不同位置上的起跑线。

senses.title: Numerical inconsistency in records
senses.titleCN: 数据记录上的数值不一致
senses.definition: a failure of two sets of figures to agree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 两套数字彼此对不上
senses.example: Auditors found a disparity between the two ledgers.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员发现两份账簿之间存在对不上的数字。
senses.why: The oldest sense of unequal survives in bookkeeping, where two columns should have matched.
senses.whyCN: 「不相等」最古老的含义在记账中留存下来：两栏数字本应相符。

senses.title: Difference in treatment
senses.definition: an unequal standard applied to people who are in comparable positions
senses.definitionCN: 对处境相当的人适用不同标准
senses.example: Employees complained of disparity in overtime pay.
senses.exampleCN: 员工抱怨加班费的发放标准悬殊。
senses.why: When the comparison moves from amounts to rules, disparity means one rule for two similar people.
senses.whyCN: 当比较从数量转向规则，这个词就指对两个相似的人用了两套标准。

intro.en: Latin gives disparity a clean line: a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun of state. English took the noun through French and later loaded it with social statistics.
intro.cn: 拉丁语为这个词提供了清楚的线索：一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根，以及一个表状态的名词词尾。英语经法语借入该名词，后来又让它承担社会统计的含义。

items.en: par meant equal, a match, a pair; it named things that stand level with one another.
items.cn: par 意为「相等、对等、一对」，指彼此齐平的事物。

items.en: dis- marked separation or negation, so dispar described a pair that does not stand level.
items.cn: dis- 表示分开或否定，因此 dispar 描述一对站不平齐的事物。

items.en: The abstract noun disparitas named the state itself: inequality, unlikeness.
items.cn: 抽象名词 disparitas 直接命名这种状态：不相等、不相同。

items.en: Middle French carried the noun forward, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪法语把这个名词继续传下去，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: The first English record is dated to the sixteenth century; the exact year is not certain, but the source line itself is not in dispute.
items.cn: 英语首见记录可定在十六世纪；具体年份不确定，但来源线索本身没有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century social science attached the word to income, gender, race, health and regional columns.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会科学把这个词挂到收入、性别、种族、健康与地区这些栏目上。

note.en: The first group shares shape or root with disparity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a gap or a mismatch.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 disparity 相近；第二组是与「落差、对不上」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning markedly different or not comparable; it is the quality behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迥然不同的、不可比的」，正是这个名词背后的性质。

entries.definition: Equality of level or status; it is the positive counterpart built on the same root for equal.
entries.definitionCN: 指水平或地位相等；是同一「相等」词根构成的正面反义对应词。

entries.definition: To speak of someone or something as of little value; it looks close but came through a French verb about lowering rank, not from the unequal pair.
entries.definitionCN: 指贬低某人或某物；形近，但来自法语表示「降低门第」的动词，并非出自「不相等」这一对词。

entries.definition: The plural form used when several gaps are counted together.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，用于把多处差距合在一起计数。

entries.definition: An unfair difference in status, wealth or opportunity; broader and more political than a measured gap.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位、财富或机会上的不公平差别；比一个可测量的落差更宽泛，也更带政治色彩。

entries.definition: The open distance between two levels or groups; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个水平或群体之间的空档；更朴素，也更口语。

entries.definition: A lack of proportion between parts, often suggesting something needs correcting.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分比例失调，常暗示需要纠正。

entries.definition: A failure of two accounts or figures to agree; it stresses contradiction rather than social distance.
entries.definitionCN: 指两份说法或数字对不上；强调矛盾，而非社会性落差。

entries.definition: A failure of statements or figures to agree with one another; it is a mismatch in consistency, not a measured gap between groups.
entries.definitionCN: 指说法或数字彼此对不上；它是「是否一致」的失配，而不是群体之间可测量的落差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts dis- and par, the real sister words parity and peer, and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词部件 dis- 与 par、真实的同根词 parity 与 peer，以及真实的统计搭配。

normal.en: dis- means apart, par means equal: pull equal things apart and you have a disparity.
normal.cn: dis- 表示分开，par 表示相等：把相等的东西拉开，就有了差距。

normal.en: Parity and peer share the same root, so disparity is the unequal twin of equality.
normal.cn: parity 与 peer 同根，因此 disparity 是「平等」那个词的不平等双胞胎。

normal.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan resting lower: that tilt is the gap.
normal.cn: 想象一架天平，一边盘子垂得更低：那份倾斜就是差距。

normal.en: Income disparity, gender disparity and health disparity are three real policy phrases.
normal.cn: 收入差距、性别差距与健康差距是三个真实的政策说法。

normal.en: Two columns of statistics sit side by side; disparity is the distance between them.
normal.cn: 两列统计数字并排而立；差距就是两列之间的距离。

abstract.en: A gap is not a wall: it is a distance that can be measured and therefore can be closed.
abstract.cn: 落差不是一堵墙，而是一段可以测量、因而也可以弥合的距离。

abstract.en: Every average hides a disparity: the mean is a line, and the gap is the space around it.
abstract.cn: 每一个平均值都藏着一处落差：均值是一条线，落差是线周围的空间。

abstract.en: Disparity is inequality turned into a number, which is why it can be argued about.
abstract.cn: 差距是被换算成数字的不平等，所以它才可以被争论。

examples.en: The survey found a sharp disparity between what men and women earn for the same work.
examples.cn: 调查发现，男女做同样的工作，报酬却有明显差距。

examples.en: Regional disparity in school funding has narrowed since the new formula was adopted.
examples.cn: 自从采用新的拨款公式，各地区的学校教育经费差距已经缩小。

examples.en: A disparity of two units between the inventories delayed the shipment.
examples.cn: 两份库存清单上有两个单位的出入，导致发货延迟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪斯帕若提」——把「相等」分开，剩下的就是差距

root: 来自拉丁语 disparitas「不相等」← dispar「不相等的」，由 dis-「分开、不」与 par「相等」构成，经中世纪法语 disparité 进入英语。词源链清楚，仅首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a neutral measured gap through money, regions, gender, race, health and opportunity to records and treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个中性的可测落差出发，经过金钱、地区、性别、种族、健康与机会，最后落到账目与待遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one rubber ruler is pulled wider at one end, and its marks drift apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把橡皮尺的一端被拉宽，刻度随之越走越疏。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL MEASURE: two groups simply fail to match on the same scale.
branches.cn: 中性的测量：两个群体在同一把尺子上就是对不上。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE MAP: income distribution and regional development pull apart.
branches.cn: 钱与地图：收入分配和地区发展各自被拉开。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE GROUP: gender, race and health outcomes carry the gap into daily life.
branches.cn: 身体与群体：性别、种族与健康结果把落差带进日常生活。

branches.en: THE STARTING LINE: schooling and opportunity begin at different points.
branches.cn: 起跑线：教育与机会从不同的位置开始。

branches.en: THE LEDGER AND THE PAY SLIP: figures that disagree and rules applied unevenly.
branches.cn: 账簿与工资单：对不上的数字，以及适用不均的规则。

intro.en: Disparity is built from a negative prefix, a root meaning equal, and a noun ending of state.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个否定前缀、一个表示「相等」的词根和一个表状态的名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies par, dispar and disparitas; parity is the positive noun from the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 par、dispar 与 disparitas；parity 是同根词构成的正面名词。

items.example: It turns equal into unequal.
items.exampleCN: 它把「相等」变成「不相等」。

items.example: The root names things that stand level.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名彼此齐平的事物。

items.example: The prefix and root first meet here.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根在这里首次结合。

items.example: The abstract noun adds a state ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词加上表状态词尾。

items.example: It turns the adjective into the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成英语名词。

items.example: It forms disparate, the adjective of difference.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示差异的形容词 disparate。

items.example: The positive counterpart of disparity.
items.exampleCN: 是 disparity 的正面对应词。

items.example: The same root survives in the word for an equal.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根在表示「同等者」的词里留存。

items.example: The plural marks more than one measured gap.
items.exampleCN: 复数标记不止一处可测的落差。

definition_zh: 辅助的；附属的；补充的；（名词）助手；辅助人员
definition_en: providing necessary support to the primary activities of an organization or process; subordinate or auxiliary
core_image: 主菜旁的小配菜：本身不是主角，缺了它整顿饭就不完整
scene: 手术室外，护士正准备器械。 The hospital hired ancillary staff to support the surgeons during long operations.
sceneCN: 这里 ancillary 是「辅助的、从属的」（第 1 个义项：为主要活动提供支持）；句意为：医院聘请辅助人员在外科医生进行长时间手术时提供支持。

pos.zh: 辅助的；附属的；补充的
助手；辅助人员

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语借词，义为「女仆；帮手」，是 ancillary 的直接词源
罕见派生，义为「辅助性；从属性」

senses.title: Providing support to the main activity
senses.definition: giving help or support to the primary work of a person, organization, or system
senses.definitionCN: 为个人、组织或系统的主要工作提供帮助或支持
senses.example: Ancillary departments keep the main office running smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 辅助部门使主办公室顺利运转。
senses.why: A servant exists to serve the master's work, so the meaning grew from serving to supporting.
senses.whyCN: ancilla 本义是婢女，婢女的存在是为主人的工作服务，词义由此从「服侍」引申为「辅助」。

senses.title: Subordinate in importance or rank
senses.definition: less important than something else and dependent on it
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物重要性低，且依附于它
senses.example: The paperwork is ancillary to the actual teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 文书工作从属于真正的教学。
senses.why: A servant holds a lower position, so the word extended to anything of secondary standing.
senses.whyCN: 婢女地位低于主人，因此词义延伸到一切处于次要地位的事物。

senses.title: Additional but necessary
senses.definition: added to something else to complete or extend it
senses.definitionCN: 添加在另一事物之上，使之完整或扩展
senses.example: The airline profits from ancillary fees like baggage charges.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司从行李费等附加费用中获利。
senses.why: Support services attach themselves alongside the core, just as extras attach to a main purchase.
senses.whyCN: 辅助服务附着于核心业务之旁，正如附加项目附着于主消费之上。

senses.title: A person who provides support
senses.definition: a worker whose job is to assist the main professional staff
senses.definitionCN: 职责是协助主要专业人员的工作人员
senses.example: The lab hired two ancillaries to prepare samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室雇了两名辅助人员来准备样本。
senses.why: The noun keeps the original Latin sense of a serving person, applied to modern workplaces.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了拉丁语「服侍者」的本义，被应用到现代职场语境。

senses.title: Something accessory to a main thing
senses.definition: a thing that is subordinate or accessory to something else
senses.definitionCN: 从属于另一事物或作为其配件的事物
senses.example: Legal work is often an ancillary of the merger process.
senses.exampleCN: 法律事务常常是并购流程的附属环节。
senses.why: What serves the master can be a person or a task, so the noun widened to things.
senses.whyCN: 为主人服务者可以是人也可以是事务，名词词义因此扩展到事物。

senses.title: Relating to subordination in law or contracts
senses.definition: in law, secondary to and dependent on a principal agreement or document
senses.definitionCN: 法律语境中，从属于并依附于主协议或主文件
senses.example: The guarantee clause is ancillary to the main contract.
senses.exampleCN: 担保条款从属于主合同。
senses.why: Law borrows the master–servant hierarchy to rank documents by importance.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用「主人—仆人」的等级关系给文件按重要性排序，附属性由此而来。

senses.title: Ancillary to something: functioning in service of it
senses.definition: existing or functioning in order to serve a larger purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为服务于更大的目的而存在或运作
senses.example: Every ancillary to the festival, from parking to security, was planned early.
senses.exampleCN: 为音乐节服务的各项配套，从停车到安保，都早早做了规划。
senses.why: The image of the servant standing by for orders becomes purpose-built support systems.
senses.whyCN: 婢女在旁待命的画面，转化为围绕目标建立的配套支持体系。

senses.title: Supporting scientific or technical work
senses.definition: used to describe equipment or industries that support a main technical process
senses.definitionCN: 形容支持主要技术流程的设备或行业
senses.example: Ancillary industries supply parts to the car plant.
senses.exampleCN: 配套产业为汽车厂供应零部件。
senses.why: Machines also have servants; the supporting equipment image comes from the serving relation.
senses.whyCN: 机器也有自己的「仆人」，配套设备的意象同样源于「服侍」关系。

intro.en: Ancillary descends from a humble Latin household word for a maidservant, rising through the idea of service to mean whatever supports the main work.
intro.cn: ancillary 源自拉丁语一个指「婢女」的家常用词，经由「服侍」之意上升为「辅助主要工作之物」。

items.en: The noun ancilla meant a maidservant, a female household servant; its origin before Latin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 ancilla 意为「婢女、家内女仆」；其更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The adjective ancillaris was formed with the suffix -aris, meaning relating to a servant or serving.
items.cn: 后拉丁时期用后缀 -aris 构成形容词 ancillaris，义为「仆人的；服侍性的」。

items.en: English adopted the adjective as ancillary around the 1620s, first in the literal sense of serving like a handmaid.
items.cn: 英语约在 17 世纪 20 年代借入 ancillary，最初用于「如婢女般服侍」的本义。

items.en: The sense widened from personal service to any subordinate or supporting function.
items.cn: 词义从「人身服侍」扩展到「任何从属或辅助性职能」。

items.en: Today ancillary chiefly describes support roles, services, and industries, and can also name the supporting people or things themselves.
items.cn: 如今 ancillary 主要形容辅助角色、服务与产业，也可名词化指辅助人员或配套事物。

note.en: The words below are grouped by spelling kinship and by closeness of meaning to ancillary.
note.cn: 下面按拼写亲缘与语义接近两组列出与 ancillary 相关的词。

entries.definition: the Latin source word, meaning a maidservant
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语源头词，义为「婢女」，与 ancillary 同根

entries.definition: situated in the armpit; relating to an axil in botany
entries.definitionCN: 腋下的；（植物学）腋生的，与 ancillary 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: providing supplementary help, especially extra troops or verbs
entries.definitionCN: 辅助的；补充的（如辅助部队、助动词），与 ancillary 同源近义但侧重增援

entries.definition: lower in rank or importance
entries.definitionCN: 级别或重要性较低的，从属的

entries.definition: added to complete or extend a thing
entries.definitionCN: 补充性的，用来补足或扩展主体

entries.definition: a thing that adds to or completes something else
entries.definitionCN: 附件；配件，强调附加而非从属

normalIntro.en: These memory hooks are built on the real Latin root ancilla and real word family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆锚点基于真实的拉丁词根 ancilla 与真实词族。

normal.en: ancilla = Latin maidservant; an ancillary worker is like a helper beside the master.
normal.cn: ancilla 是拉丁语「婢女」；ancillary 人员就像主人身旁的帮手。

normal.en: Same root family: ancilla → ancillaris → ancillary, a straight line from servant to support.
normal.cn: 同根词链：ancilla → ancillaris → ancillary，从「仆人」一路到「辅助」。

normal.en: Auxiliary troops and ancillary staff both come from servant-related roots.
normal.cn: auxiliary（辅助部队）与 ancillary（辅助人员）的词源都与「仆役」相关。

normal.en: The phrase ancillary to marks what serves what, like ancillary to the main task.
normal.cn: 搭配 ancillary to 标明谁服务于谁，如「从属于主要任务」。

normal.en: In hospitals, ancillary services mean the departments behind the doctors.
normal.cn: 在医院里，ancillary services 指医生身后的各个支持科室。

abstract.en: Picture a maid quietly arranging the room while the master works: she is ancillary.
abstract.cn: 想象主人工作时女仆在一旁悄悄整理房间：她就是 ancillary（辅助者）。

abstract.en: See the main dish at the center of a table with small side dishes orbiting it, each one ancillary.
abstract.cn: 想象主菜在餐桌中央，小配菜围绕四周，每一样都是 ancillary（配套）。

abstract.en: Feel the word tilting sideways: the main beam stands upright, ancillary beams lean in to hold it.
abstract.cn: 感受这个词的「斜倚感」：主梁直立，辅助的梁斜撑在旁，即为 ancillary。

examples.en: The university cut ancillary services to save money.
examples.cn: 大学削减了辅助服务以节省开支。

examples.en: Transport is ancillary to the main business of publishing.
examples.cn: 运输从属于出版这一主营业务。

examples.en: Ancillary staff keep the hospital clean and running.
examples.cn: 辅助人员保持医院的清洁与运转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺尽力辅助」——俺虽是配角，但尽力辅助主角，正是 ancillary（辅助的）的画面。

root: 拉丁语 ancilla（婢女，来源不确定）+ 后缀 -aris（属于……的）→ 拉丁语 ancillaris「仆人的」→ 英语 ancillary。词义核心是「服侍 → 辅助」。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin image of a maidservant, the word fans out into adjectival senses of support, subordination, and supplementation, plus noun uses for the people and things that serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语「婢女」的画面出发，词义铺展为「支持、从属、补充」等形容词义项，以及指代辅助者与配套事物的名词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the servant standing beside the master's work
core.cn: 核心意象：站在主人工作之旁的仆役

branches.en: helping the main activity
branches.cn: 辅助主要活动

branches.en: ranking below the principal thing
branches.cn: 地位低于主体（含法律附属性）

branches.en: extras attached to the core
branches.cn: 附着于核心的附加部分

branches.en: the people and things that serve
branches.cn: 作为辅助者的人与物

branches.en: support systems around a technical process
branches.cn: 技术流程周围的配套体系

intro.en: The word family of ancillary is small but clear: one Latin noun plus adjective and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: ancillary 的词族不大但脉络清晰：一个拉丁名词加形容词、名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin built the family on ancilla with the adjective suffix -aris.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 ancilla 为基础，用形容词后缀 -aris 构建了这个词族。

items.example: The ancilla kept the Roman household in order.
items.exampleCN: 婢女维持罗马家庭的秩序。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a servant
items.example: Munera ancillaria were the servant's daily tasks.
items.exampleCN: ancillaria 指仆人的日常职责。

items.meaning: relating to; a place or collection
items.meaningCN: 与……有关的；（名词）场所或集合
items.example: Honorary and salary share this productive suffix.
items.exampleCN: honorary 与 salary 都用了这一能产后缀。

items.example: The opening an- of ancilla is generally treated as part of the whole root.
items.exampleCN: ancilla 开头的 an- 一般视为整个词根的一部分。

items.meaning: the serving element of the word
items.meaningCN: 词中承载「服侍」义的词干
items.example: Ancillary and ancilla share the stem -cill-.
items.exampleCN: ancillary 与 ancilla 共享词干 -cill-。

items.example: Auxiliary verbs help the main verb.
items.exampleCN: 助动词辅助主要动词。

items.example: Servile duties once meant household service.
items.exampleCN: servile duties 曾指家内仆役工作。

items.example: A subsidiary company supports the parent firm.
items.exampleCN: 子公司支持母公司。

items.example: Car accessories are ancillary products in a loose sense.
items.exampleCN: 汽车配件宽泛地说是附加产品。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语原词借入英语，义为「婢女；女仆」

definition_zh: 机密的；已分类的；分类的（广告、目录）
definition_en: officially secret and restricted in access, or arranged into classes; also used of small advertisements grouped by category
core_image: 一份文件封面上盖着红色密级章，旁边挂着一把锁
scene: 档案馆的接待室里，工作人员把一份文件放进保险柜，访客只能看到空空的桌面。 In the reading room a clerk locks a classified file in the safe, so visitors see only an empty desk.
sceneCN: 这里 classified 是「机密的」（第 1 个义项：受保密限制的信息）；句意：接待室里，工作人员把一份机密文件锁进保险柜，访客只能看到空桌面。图中可辨识物件：保险柜、红色密级章、文件封套、访客登记簿。

pos.zh: 机密的；已分类的
分类广告（常用复数 classifieds）

senses.title: Officially secret
senses.definition: of information or documents, marked as restricted and available only to authorised people
senses.definitionCN: 指信息或文件被标记为受限，只有获授权者可以接触
senses.example: The general refused to discuss the classified report.
senses.exampleCN: 将军拒绝讨论这份机密报告。
senses.why: This is the dominant modern sense. The past participle freezes an official act: someone has already placed this document in a restricted class, and the adjective records that decision.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最主要的义项。过去分词冻结了一个官方动作：某人已经把这份文件归入受限类别，形容词记录的就是这个决定。

senses.title: Placed in a category
senses.definition: assigned to a group according to shared features
senses.definitionCN: 按共同特征被分配到某一组
senses.example: The insects are classified by wing structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这些昆虫按翅的结构被分类。
senses.why: Here the participle keeps the plain verbal sense: an item has received a class. Nothing is hidden; the point is where the item was put.
senses.whyCN: 这里分词保留朴素的动词义：一个项目已经获得了类别。没有隐藏任何东西，重点在于它被放到了哪里。

senses.title: Classified advertisements
senses.definition: short advertisements printed together under subject headings, or the section containing them
senses.definitionCN: 按主题归在一起刊登的短广告，或刊载它们的版面
senses.example: He found the apartment through the classifieds.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过分类广告找到了那套公寓。
senses.why: Newspapers sorted small ads into columns by category, so the adjective became a noun. The word now names a whole genre of paid notices.
senses.whyCN: 报纸把小块广告按类别排进专栏，于是形容词变成了名词。这个词现在命名一整类付费启事。

senses.title: Graded by quality
senses.definition: sorted into quality grades, as of wool, timber or eggs
senses.definitionCN: 按质量等级分选，如羊毛、木材或鸡蛋
senses.example: Classified wool sells at a higher price.
senses.exampleCN: 分级羊毛卖价更高。
senses.why: Market grading uses the same verb: the class is a price band. The participle tells the buyer that inspection has already happened.
senses.whyCN: 市场分级用的是同一个动词：类别就是价格带。这个分词告诉买家，检验已经做过了。

senses.title: A post requiring security clearance
senses.definition: of a job or position, requiring access to secret material and therefore a clearance check
senses.definitionCN: 指需要接触机密材料、因而须通过安全审查的工作或职位
senses.example: She applied for a classified position at the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了部里的一个涉密职位。
senses.why: This sense shifts the restriction from the document to the person. The class no longer marks the paper but the level of trust granted to an employee.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把限制从文件移到人身上。这个“类”不再标记纸张，而是标记授予雇员的信任等级。

senses.title: Assigned a biological taxon
senses.titleCN: 在生物分类中被归入的
senses.definition: placed in a species, genus or higher rank by taxonomy
senses.definitionCN: 由分类学归入某一物种、属或更高阶元
senses.example: The fossil was classified as a new species.
senses.exampleCN: 该化石被归为一个新物种。
senses.why: Biology uses the participle for a completed judgement. Once classified, a specimen has a name and a place in the tree, and later work may move it.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用这个分词表示已完成的判断。一旦被分类，标本就有了名称与在树上的位置，后来的工作可能把它移走。

senses.title: Labelled in a dataset
senses.definition: in computing, assigned a category label in training or reference data
senses.definitionCN: 在计算中，在训练或参考数据里被指定类别标签
senses.example: The model learns from thousands of classified images.
senses.exampleCN: 模型从上万张已标注图像中学习。
senses.why: Machine learning borrows the participle for data whose category is already known. The adjective marks the difference between raw input and answered input.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习借用这个分词，指类别已知的数据。这个形容词标出原始输入与已给答案的输入之间的差别。

senses.title: Officially listed as a status
senses.definition: formally designated as having a particular status, such as endangered or a controlled substance
senses.definitionCN: 被正式指定具有某种身份，如濒危或受管制物质
senses.example: The bird is classified as endangered.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟被列为濒危。
senses.why: The phrase classified as marks an official designation with legal force. It is not a description but a decision that changes what may be done.
senses.whyCN: 短语 classified as 标示具有法律效力的官方认定。它不是描述，而是一个改变“可以做什么”的决定。

senses.title: Arranged in a classified catalogue
senses.definition: of a catalogue or index, arranged by subject class rather than alphabetically
senses.definitionCN: 指目录或索引按主题类别而非字母顺序编排
senses.example: The old library used a classified catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 旧图书馆使用分类目录。
senses.why: A classified catalogue lets a reader browse by subject. The adjective describes the arrangement of the finding aid, not the secrecy of its contents.
senses.whyCN: 分类目录让读者按主题浏览。这个形容词描述检索工具的编排，而不是其内容的机密性。

intro.en: Classified is the past participle of classify plus the native English suffix -ed, so its history is the history of classify. The Latin halves are classis, 'division', and facere, 'to make'. What is worth noting is that the suffix is English, not Latin, and that the secrecy sense is a 20th-century specialization of a much older idea of sorting.
intro.cn: classified 是 classify 的过去分词，加上英语本族后缀 -ed，所以它的历史就是 classify 的历史。拉丁的两个半部是 classis“划分”与 facere“做”。值得注意的是：后缀是英语的，不是拉丁的；而“机密”义是 20 世纪对一个更古老的“分选”观念的特殊化。

items.en: Classis named a division of Roman citizens and also a fleet. Its deeper origin is disputed; a link with calare, 'to summon', has been proposed but not settled.
items.cn: classis 指罗马公民的一个等级划分，也指舰队。其更深来源有争议；与 calare“召集”的关联被提出过，但未有定论。

items.en: Facere, 'to make', is the second half of the compound. In classificare it carries the sense 'to make into classes'.
items.cn: facere“做”是复合词的后半。在 classificare 中，它带有“使成为类别”的意思。

items.en: Classificare appears in medieval Latin for the arranging of knowledge or objects into ranks. Its participle classificatus is the formal ancestor of the English adjective.
items.cn: classificare 出现在中世纪拉丁，指把知识或物件编排成等级。它的分词 classificatus 是英语形容词的形式祖先。

items.en: English took classify from French classifier in the 18th century, when natural history made classification a central science. The verb was then regular: classify, classified, classified.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪从法语 classifier 接来 classify，当时博物学使分类成为核心科学。随后动词按规则变化：classify、classified、classified。

items.en: The adjective first meant simply 'arranged in classes', and classified ads belong to 19th-century newspapers. The secrecy sense developed in the 20th century, especially through military and government practice.
items.cn: 这个形容词最初只表示“按类别编排”，分类广告属于 19 世纪报纸的做法。“机密”义在 20 世纪发展起来，尤其通过军事与政府实践。

items.en: Modern English uses classified for documents, jobs, species, data labels, official statuses and catalogues. The same participle now covers both 'sorted' and 'hidden', two outcomes of the same administrative act.
items.cn: 现代英语把 classified 用于文件、职位、物种、数据标签、官方身份与目录。同一个分词现在同时覆盖“已分选”与“被隐藏”，这是同一行政动作的两种结果。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from the verb, the noun of action and the plural noun for advertisements. The second group compares levels of restriction and of labelling.
note.cn: 第一组把形容词与动词、动作名词、表示广告的复数名词分开。第二组比较限制与标注的不同层级。

entries.definition: to assign to a class. Classified is what has happened to the thing; classify is what someone did.
entries.definitionCN: 把……归入某类。classified 是事物经历的结果；classify 是某人做的动作。

entries.definition: the act or system of grouping. It names the process or scheme, not the item.
entries.definitionCN: 分组的行为或体系。它命名过程或方案，而不是项目。

entries.definition: the section of a newspaper containing small category-sorted advertisements. The plural is a separate noun, not just a plural adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸中刊登按类别归置的小广告的版面。这个复数是独立名词，不只是形容词的复数。

entries.definition: meant to be kept private between the parties concerned. It stresses a relationship of trust rather than an official secrecy level.
entries.definitionCN: 意图在相关方之间保密的。它强调信任关系，而不是官方密级。

entries.definition: known only to a few. It is the plain word; classified is the administrative and legal term.
entries.definitionCN: 只有少数人知道的。它是朴素说法；classified 是行政与法律术语。

entries.definition: available only to people with permission. It describes the limit itself, while classified names the system that imposes it.
entries.definitionCN: 只对获许可者开放。它描述限制本身，而 classified 命名施加限制的制度。

entries.definition: sorted into quality levels. It ranks within a scale, while classified usually separates into categories.
entries.definitionCN: 按质量层级分选。它在一个尺度内排序，而 classified 通常把事物分成类别。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the adjective from classify and then attach it to the two worlds it now serves: secrecy and sorting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 classify 搭起这个形容词，再把它系到它现在服务的两个世界：保密与分选。

normal.en: See the chain: class, classify, classified. The -ed means the job is done.
normal.cn: 看见链条：class、classify、classified。后缀 -ed 表示事情已经做完。

normal.en: Picture the red stamp on a folder: that is the secrecy sense.
normal.cn: 想象文件夹上的红色印章：那就是机密义。

normal.en: Picture the newspaper columns: small ads sorted by category.
normal.cn: 想象报纸的专栏：小块广告按类别归置。

normal.en: Keep the phrase classified as for official designations such as endangered.
normal.cn: 记住 classified as，用于濒危等官方认定。

normal.en: Contrast it with unclassified: the same word with the lid removed.
normal.cn: 与 unclassified 对比：同一个词，盖子被拿掉。

abstract.en: Hold one act: a decision has been made about where this belongs. Everything else follows from that decision.
abstract.cn: 抓住一个动作：关于它属于哪里，已经作出了决定。其余一切都从这个决定而来。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by what is classified: documents, things, ads, goods, jobs, species, data, statuses, catalogues.
abstract.cn: 按被分类的对象分组：文件、物品、广告、货物、职位、物种、数据、身份、目录。

abstract.en: Notice the double edge: the same stamp that sorts a thing can also hide it.
abstract.cn: 留意双刃：同一个印章既能给事物分类，也能把它藏起来。

examples.en: The minister was shown classified intelligence before the meeting.
examples.cn: 会前部长看到了机密情报。

examples.en: The tablets are classified as controlled substances.
examples.cn: 这些药片被列为受管制物质。

examples.en: He sold his old bicycle through the classified ads.
examples.cn: 他通过分类广告卖掉了旧自行车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“克拉斯法爱德”：class 是类别，-fied 是“被做成”——已经被分进某个类里，文件进了“机密”这一类，就是 classified。

root: 拉丁语 classis“等级、划分”加 facere“做”，中世纪拉丁 classificare“分为等级”；18 世纪英语 classify，其过去分词 classified 加本族后缀 -ed。

sensesIntro.en: Classified is a decision already made, seen from the side of the thing decided about. That thing may be a document placed in a secrecy level, a species placed in a genus, a sheep's fleece placed in a grade, a job placed under clearance rules, or an image placed in a training label. The two modern poles are sorting and hiding, and both come from the same administrative act: someone with authority said where this belongs.
sensesIntro.cn: classified 是一个已经作出的决定，从被决定者的角度看到的结果。这个被决定者可以是归入某密级的文件、归入某属的物种、归入某等级的羊毛、归入审查规则的职位，或归入训练标签的图像。现代的两极是“分选”与“隐藏”，两者都来自同一个行政动作：有权限的人说了它属于哪里。

core.en: A decision has been made: this belongs here, and access follows from that.
core.cn: 决定已经作出：它属于这里，接触权限由此而来。

branches.en: SECRECY: the document and the post that guard it.
branches.cn: 保密：文件本身，以及守着它的岗位。

branches.en: ORDER: the plain assignment, and the catalogue built from it.
branches.cn: 秩序：朴素的归类，以及由此建立的目录。

branches.en: MARKET: advertisements and quality grades.
branches.cn: 市场：广告与质量等级。

branches.en: OFFICIAL STATUS: species names and legal designations.
branches.cn: 官方身份：物种名称与法律认定。

branches.en: DATA: labels that teach a machine.
branches.cn: 数据：教机器认类的标签。

intro.en: Classified is classify plus the native English -ed. The items below follow that chain, then add the un-, de- and re- forms and three compounds where the adjective has become a fixed label.
intro.cn: classified 是 classify 加英语本族后缀 -ed。下面的条目沿这条链展开，再加上 un-、de-、re- 形式，以及三个形容词已成固定标签的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the noun of division, the medieval verb, and its participle. The participle is the formal model behind the English adjective, even though the English suffix itself is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出表示划分的名词、中世纪动词及其分词。尽管英语后缀本身是本族的，这个分词仍是英语形容词背后的形式样板。

items.meaning: placed in a class; officially secret
items.example: The files are classified until 2030.
items.exampleCN: 这些文件保密至 2030 年。

items.structure: Latin classis + facere, via French classifier
items.example: The library classifies books by subject.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆按主题给书分类。

items.meaning: the act or system of grouping
items.example: The classification of the archive took months.
items.exampleCN: 档案的分类花了几个月。

items.example: The classifier flagged the suspicious file.
items.exampleCN: 分类器标记了可疑文件。

items.meaning: not secret; open to the public
items.example: Only unclassified material was released.
items.exampleCN: 只公开了非机密材料。

items.example: The declassified papers revealed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 解密文件揭示了该计划。

items.meaning: given a different class or level
items.example: The substance was reclassified as hazardous.
items.exampleCN: 该物质被重新归类为危险品。

items.meaning: a short newspaper advertisement placed under a category
items.example: She placed a classified ad for the room.
items.exampleCN: 她登了一则出租房间的分类广告。

definition_zh: 国会的；美国国会的；由国会授权的
definition_en: relating to a congress, especially the United States Congress, or authorized by it
core_image: 一间挂着两排木牌的房间，每块牌子都写着同一座大厅的编号
scene: 走廊墙上挂满木牌，每块牌子都印着同一座大厅的座位号。 A congressional committee opened the hearing on the tax bill.
sceneCN: 句中这个词指属于美国国会的（第 1 个义项：与美国国会有关的）；句意为一个国会委员会就税收法案开启了听证。图中可辨识物件：木牌、座位号、委员会名牌、听证桌、麦克风。

pos.zh: 国会的；与国会有关的
由国会授权的

senses.title: Relating to the United States Congress
senses.definition: concerning the American national legislature, its members or its business
senses.definitionCN: 与美国国家立法机关、其议员或事务有关的
senses.example: A congressional committee opened the hearing on the tax bill.
senses.exampleCN: 一个国会委员会就税收法案开启了听证。
senses.why: The adjective comes from the noun congress plus -al, and in American use the capitalised noun points to one legislature.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由名词 congress 加 -al 构成，在美式用法中大写名词专指一个立法机关。

senses.title: Of hearings and committees
senses.definition: describing the investigative and deliberative organs through which Congress works
senses.definitionCN: 形容国会赖以运作的调查与审议机构
senses.example: The congressional hearing lasted five hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这场国会听证持续了五小时。
senses.why: Committee work is where most congressional business happens, so the adjective is used most often with those nouns.
senses.whyCN: 大部分国会事务在委员会里发生，因此这个形容词最常与这类名词连用。

senses.title: Authorized by Congress
senses.definition: approved or required by statute of Congress rather than by the executive
senses.definitionCN: 由国会立法批准或要求，而非由行政决定
senses.example: The programme needs congressional approval before it can start.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划需要国会批准才能启动。
senses.why: Only Congress can pass federal statutes, so its adjective marks the source of legal authority.
senses.whyCN: 只有国会能通过联邦法规，因此这个形容词标记法律权威的来源。

senses.title: Of a district or seat
senses.definition: relating to the constituency that elects a member of the House
senses.definitionCN: 与选举众议员的选区有关的
senses.example: The state gained one congressional seat after the census.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查后这个州多了一个国会席位。
senses.why: Seats are counted by district, so the adjective attaches to maps and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 席位按选区计数，因此这个形容词附着在地图与数字上。

senses.title: Of the Continental Congress
senses.definition: historical use for the revolutionary assemblies that met before the Constitution
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，指制宪前召开的革命时期会议
senses.example: Congressional delegates signed the declaration in 1776.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆会议的代表在 1776 年签署了宣言。
senses.why: American usage dates from 1776, when the word described the Continental Congress rather than the later bicameral body.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法可追到 1776 年，当时这个词描述的是大陆会议，而非后来的两院制机构。

senses.title: Of any congress
senses.definition: relating to a scholarly, party or diplomatic congress
senses.definitionCN: 与学术、政党或外交大会有关的
senses.example: Congressional papers from the medical meeting filled two volumes.
senses.exampleCN: 这次医学会议的论文装满了两卷。
senses.why: The ending -al is general, so the adjective can serve any body called a congress.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -al 是通用的，因此这个形容词可用于任何被称为 congress 的机构。

senses.title: Of congressional procedure
senses.definition: describing the rules and customs by which the chamber conducts debate and votes
senses.definitionCN: 形容议院进行辩论与表决所依的规则与惯例
senses.example: A congressional rule limited each speaker to five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一条国会规则把每位发言者限制在五分钟。
senses.why: Procedure is what turns a majority into a lawful decision, so the adjective marks those rules.
senses.whyCN: 程序是把多数变成合法决定的东西，因此这个形容词标记这些规则。

senses.title: Of congressional staff and resources
senses.definition: relating to the employees, offices and budget that support the legislature
senses.definitionCN: 与支撑立法机关运转的雇员、办公室与预算有关
senses.example: Congressional staff drafted most of the amendment.
senses.exampleCN: 国会工作人员起草了大部分修正案。
senses.why: A modern legislature is an institution with employees, so its adjective covers the machinery behind the votes.
senses.whyCN: 现代立法机关是有雇员的机构，因此这个形容词覆盖投票背后的机器。

intro.en: Congressional is recorded from the 1690s, from Latin congressus through congressionem plus -al. The specific American sense appears from 1776 and was at first disliked as a new coinage.
intro.cn: congressional 自十七世纪九十年代见于记录，由拉丁 congressus（经由 congressionem）加 -al 构成。特指美国国会的义项自 1776 年出现，起初曾被当作生造词而受排斥。

items.en: Congressus named a meeting or encounter, from congredi 'to come together', built on com- and gradi 'to walk'.
items.cn: congressus 指会合或遭遇，出自 congredi「走到一起」，由 com- 与 gradi「走」构成。

items.en: The oblique stem congression- supplied the base to which the English ending was attached.
items.cn: 斜格词干 congression- 提供了英语接上词尾的基础。

items.en: The adjective appears in the 1690s with the general sense 'of or pertaining to a congress'.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪九十年代出现，泛指「与代表大会有关的」。

items.en: From 1776 it was used specifically of the Congress of the American states; some writers called the new usage barbarous.
items.cn: 自 1776 年起，它专门用于美国各州的国会；当时有些作者称这个新用法粗野。

items.en: Later it covered committees, districts, staff and procedure, since those are the parts of the institution that act.
items.cn: 后来它覆盖委员会、选区、人员与程序，因为这些都是该机构行动的部分。

items.en: The form and root are documented; only the earliest citation of each sense is approximate, so nothing is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词形与词根均有记录；只有各义项的最早书证是约数，因此没有需要标为来源不确定的部分。

note.en: Group one holds the words of the congress family, which differ only by ending; group two holds other adjectives of legislative relation.
note.cn: 第一组是 congress 词族的词，差别只在词尾；第二组是其他表示立法关系的形容词。

entries.definition: The legislature or the meeting itself; the adjective only describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指立法机关或会议本身；形容词只描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: A member of the United States Congress, usually of the House; it names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指美国国会议员，通常指众议员；它命名人。

entries.definition: A neutral word for a member of Congress, avoiding the gender of congressman and congresswoman.
entries.definitionCN: 指国会议员的中性说法，避开 congressman 与 congresswoman 的性别标记。

entries.definition: Relating to a parliament; it is the counterpart of congressional in systems where the executive sits in the assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 指与议会有关的；在行政坐于议会的体制里，它是 congressional 的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to lawmaking or to any legislature; it is broader than congressional and names no particular country.
entries.definitionCN: 指与立法或任何立法机关有关的；比 congressional 宽泛，不限定国家。

entries.definition: Relating to the central government of a union of states; congressional business is federal, but the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指由州组成的联邦中央政府的；国会事务属联邦层面，但两词不可互换。

entries.definition: Required or created by a written law; a congressional mandate is statutory in force, but statutory says nothing about who passed it.
entries.definitionCN: 指由成文法规定或创设的；国会授权确实具有成文法效力，但 statutory 不说明是谁通过的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real suffix, the real root and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词尾、真实词根与真实的机构搭配。

normal.en: congress plus -al 'relating to': whatever belongs to the coming-together chamber.
normal.cn: congress 加 -al「与……有关」：一切属于那个「会合议院」的东西。

normal.en: The family runs congress, congressional, congressman and congresswoman.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 congress、congressional、congressman 与 congresswoman。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institution: congressional committee, congressional district, congressional approval.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机构用法：国会委员会、国会选区、国会批准。

normal.en: The root gradi 'to walk' also sits in progress and egress.
normal.cn: 词根 gradi「走」也出现在 progress 与 egress 中。

normal.en: The word was once attacked as an American barbarism, a fact worth remembering in style debates.
normal.cn: 这个词曾被指为美式生造词，这一点在文体争论中值得一提。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses attach one adjective to every working part of a legislature: the body, its hearings, its authorisation, its districts, its revolutionary past, its namesake meetings, its procedure and its staff.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词贴到立法机关的每个工作部件上：机关本身、听证、授权、选区、革命时期的前身、同名会议、程序与人员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of nameplates all bearing the same hall number.

branches.en: TWO CONGRESSES: the American legislature and any scholarly congress share one adjective.
branches.cn: 两种大会：美国立法机关与任何学术大会共用一个形容词。

branches.en: THE WORKING ROOM: hearings and procedure are how a chamber turns argument into decision.
branches.cn: 工作间：听证与程序是议院把争论变成决定的方式。

branches.en: AUTHORITY AND MACHINERY: statutes need staff to draft them and votes to pass them.
branches.cn: 权威与机器：法规需要人员起草，也需要投票通过。

branches.en: THE MAP: seats are counted in districts, which is why the adjective attaches to geography.
branches.cn: 地图：席位按选区计数，所以这个形容词附着在地理上。

branches.en: THE FIRST CONGRESS: the revolutionary assembly gave the word its American start.
branches.cn: 第一届国会：革命时期的会议给了这个词美式起点。

intro.en: Congressional is a Latin noun plus an English relational ending, and its family splits into persons, places and procedures.
intro.cn: congressional 是一个拉丁名词加英语关系词尾，其词族分成人物、地点与程序三支。
