definition_zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓某领域的（也可作名词：识字的人）
definition_en: able to read and write, educated, or knowledgeable about a particular subject
core_image: 一位老人坐在窗边的木桌前，手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌角摞着几本翻旧的书
scene: 窗边的木桌前，一位老人用手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌上摞着翻旧的书。 By eighty she was still a keen reader, wholly literate and never without a book.
sceneCN: 这里指「具备读写能力」（第 1 个义项：能够读书写字）；句意为她到八十岁仍爱读书，完全识字，手边从不缺书。可辨识物件：木桌、书页、旧书、窗光。

pos.zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓的
识字的人；有文化的人（较少用）

senses.title: Able to read and write
senses.definition: having the basic ability to read and write simple texts
senses.definitionCN: 具备读懂并写出浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Only half the adults in the district were literate in nineteen fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 一九五零年，这个区只有一半成年人识字。
senses.why: the adjective is the direct Latin word for 'lettered', so its first sense is the plain possession of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自拉丁语「写有字母的」，因此第一义就是字面意义上的「认得字母」。

senses.title: Educated and well read
senses.definition: having a broad education and familiarity with serious writing
senses.definitionCN: 受过良好教育并熟悉严肃著作
senses.example: Her letters show a literate mind at work.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信显出一个有教养的心灵在运转。
senses.why: knowing letters grew into knowing books, and knowing books grew into general cultivation.
senses.whyCN: 「认得字母」长成「读过书」，「读过书」又长成「有教养」。

senses.title: Functionally literate in daily life
senses.titleCN: 能应付日常事务的书信能力
senses.definition: able to handle forms, instructions and ordinary paperwork without help
senses.definitionCN: 无需他人帮助即可处理表格、说明与日常文书
senses.example: Applicants must be functionally literate to fill the form alone.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人须具备实用读写能力，才能独立填表。
senses.why: administration turned the broad ability into a practical threshold.
senses.whyCN: 行政事务把宽泛的能力变成一个实用门槛。

senses.title: Computer literate
senses.titleCN: 会用计算机与常用软件
senses.definition: confident with computers and common software, usually in the fixed phrase computer literate
senses.definitionCN: 能熟练使用计算机与常用软件，通常见于「会用电脑」这一固定说法
senses.example: New staff must be computer literate before they start.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工入职前必须会用电脑。
senses.why: a computer's keyboard and menus became the new letters, so the old adjective was reused.
senses.whyCN: 计算机的键盘与菜单成了新的「字母」，这个旧形容词因此被复用。

senses.title: Literate in a subject
senses.definition: knowing enough of a subject's language to read and judge its material
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某学科的语言，足以阅读并判断其材料
senses.example: Voters should be economically literate enough to read a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 选民应具备足够的经济素养，能读懂一份预算。
senses.why: the pattern 'knows the letters of a field' is reused for every specialty.
senses.whyCN: 「认得某领域的字母」这一模式被复用到每一门专业上。

senses.title: A literate style of writing
senses.definition: describing prose that is clear, polished and clearly the work of a reader
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字清楚、打磨过、明显出自读书人之手
senses.example: The report was literate without being showy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告写得有文气，却不炫耀。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the product as well as the person, because style was seen as the mark of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也能形容作品而非人，因为文风被视为读书的印记。

senses.title: A largely literate population
senses.definition: describing a society or group in which most adults can read and write
senses.definitionCN: 描述多数成年人都能读写的群体或社会
senses.example: A literate workforce adapted quickly to printed instructions.
senses.exampleCN: 识字的劳动力能迅速适应书面说明。
senses.why: the adjective can describe a whole population, because it was originally a description of persons.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初描述个人，因此也能描述整个人口。

senses.title: A person who can read (noun use)
senses.definition: a person who has learned to read and write, especially in accounts of schooling
senses.definitionCN: 已学会读写的人，尤见于教育记述中
senses.example: The program graduated eight hundred literates in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目第一年培养出八百名识字者。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for the people who bear the quality.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接用作名词，指具备该性质的人。

intro.en: Literate comes from Latin litteratus 'marked with letters, learned', an adjective on littera 'letter'. English borrowed it in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，该形容词建于 littera「字母」之上，十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural a letter, a document or writings. The deeper origin of the word is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指书信、文书或著作。这个词更深的来源未获证明。

items.en: The ending -atus formed adjectives of possession, so litteratus meant 'furnished with letters', hence able to read and, by extension, learned.
items.cn: 表「具有」的拉丁形容词词尾构成这类形容词，因此 litteratus 意为「带有字母的」，引申为能读书，再引申为有学问。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fifteenth century, at first describing clergy and scholars rather than ordinary readers.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，最初描述神职人员与学者，而非普通读者。

items.en: With mass printing and schooling the word spread to anyone who could read, and to whole populations.
items.cn: 随着大众印刷与学校教育普及，这个词扩展到任何能读书的人，也用于整个人口。

items.en: Late twentieth-century usage produced computer literate and financially literate, applying the adjective to specific competences.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的用法产生了「会用电脑的」「懂金融的」等说法，把这个形容词用于具体能力。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and no single first recorded use of the modern everyday sense can be verified.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，现代日常义的最早书证亦无法确证。

note.en: Group one holds words and forms from the same root that are often confused; group two holds adjectives describing an educated person.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词形；第二组是描述受教育者的形容词。

entries.definition: The ability itself, not the person who has it; it is what a literate person possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身，而非拥有能力的人；它是识字者所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Meaning 'word for word'; it looks close but describes translation, not reading ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「逐字的」，外形接近，却描述翻译方式而非读写能力。

entries.definition: Relating to literature as an art; a literate person need not be literary.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为艺术的文学有关；识字的人未必有文学趣味。

entries.definition: Unable to read or write; it is the exact opposite, built with a prefix of denial.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能读写，是它的确切反义，由否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: Having had formal schooling; it says nothing about the bare ability to read.
entries.definitionCN: 指受过正规学校教育，不涉及最基本的读写能力。

entries.definition: An older word for widely read and scholarly; it is close in meaning but dated in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的说法，指博览而博学，意思接近但语气古旧。

entries.definition: Having read widely in serious books; it is narrower than a general literate upbringing.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛读过严肃书籍，范围比一般「有文化」窄。

entries.definition: Comfortable with numbers and quantitative reasoning, coined on the model of literate.
entries.definitionCN: 指熟悉数字与定量推理，仿「识字的」造出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The ending means 'furnished with', so the word literally says a person is furnished with letters.
normal.cn: 那个词尾意为「带有」，因此这个词字面上是说一个人「带着字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases add the specialty: computer literate, financially literate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配补上专业领域：会用电脑、懂金融。

normal.en: The positive and negative forms differ only by a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 肯定式与否定式只差一个否定前缀。

normal.en: The family runs literacy, illiteracy, literature, literal, literary.
normal.cn: 同族包括「读写能力」「文盲状态」「文学」「字面的」「文学的」。

normal.en: The noun use is rare but real, as in counts of literates.
normal.cn: 名词用法少见但真实存在，如统计识字者人数。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying a bag of letters that opens every official door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人背着一袋字母，能打开每一扇公务的门。

abstract.en: Picture glasses that turn a page of marks into sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一副眼镜，把满页符号变成句子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp kept lit at the same desk for fifty years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张书桌上点了五十年的灯。

examples.en: A literate population reads instructions and changes behaviour faster.
examples.cn: 识字的人口能更快读懂说明并改变行为。

examples.en: She was literate in three languages before she left school.
examples.cn: 她离开学校前已能用三种语言读写。

examples.en: Any computer-literate volunteer can update the parish register.
examples.cn: 任何会用电脑的志愿者都能更新教区登记册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特瑞特」——里面特别认得那些小字，就是识字的。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「具有」的形容词后缀构成 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，十五世纪进入英语，后扩展指任何能读写的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain ability to read through cultivation, practical paperwork, computers, specialist fields and style, until the adjective finally names the people themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最基本的读写能力出发，经过教养、日常文书、电脑、专业领域与文风，最后用这个形容词直接指人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tracing lines of print on a page beside a stack of worn books.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在页面上顺着印刷字行移动，旁边是一摞翻旧的书。

branches.en: THE BASE: the plain ability to read and write comes first.
branches.cn: 基底：能读能写这一朴素能力排在最前。

branches.en: BOOKS AND BEARERS: reading widely shades into cultivation, and the adjective can name the reader.
branches.cn: 书与读书人：广泛阅读渐成教养，而这个形容词也能直接指读者。

branches.en: PAPERWORK: forms and instructions set a practical threshold for the word.
branches.cn: 文书：表格与说明为这个词设下实用门槛。

branches.en: TOOLS AND FIELDS: screens and specialties each have letters of their own.
branches.cn: 工具与领域：屏幕与专业各自拥有自己的「字母」。

branches.en: STYLE AND SOCIETY: polished prose and a reading public are the word written large.
branches.cn: 文风与社会：打磨过的文字与读书的公众，是这个词的放大形态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective carried into English, built from a noun for a letter and a suffix meaning 'provided with'.
intro.cn: 这是一个直接借入英语的拉丁形容词，由表「字母」的名词与表「被赋予」的后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera supplied letter, literature and literal, while the adjective litteratus supplied literate and, with a prefix of denial, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」，形容词 litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀则成「不识字的」。

items.example: The noun names the unit a reader must first master.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指读者必须首先掌握的单位。

items.example: The ending turns a possession into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「拥有某物」变成对人的描述。

items.meaning: provided with letters, able to read
items.example: The witness was literate and signed her own name.
items.exampleCN: 这名证人识字，自己签了名。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy rose sharply after the new school opened.
items.exampleCN: 新学校开办后识字率迅速上升。

items.example: The notice was rewritten for illiterate readers.
items.exampleCN: 这则通知为不识字者重写了一遍。

items.meaning: a sign for a speech sound; a written message
items.example: She wrote the letter in one sitting.
items.exampleCN: 她一口气写完了这封信。

items.example: The magazine reviews literary fiction.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志评论文学小说。

items.example: The old phrase 'a man of letters' still survives.
items.exampleCN: 「文人」这一旧称仍然存在。

definition_zh: 数量的；定量的；可量化的；以数字表示的；按量计的；（经济）数量型的
definition_en: relating to amount or number, especially when data are measured and expressed as figures
core_image: 一架天平把两堆东西换成两排数字
scene: 这里指「数量的」。 The paper combined quantitative data from weather stations with interviews from farmers.
sceneCN: 这里 quantitative 是「定量的」（第 2 个义项：可计数、可统计的数值资料）；句意：这篇论文把气象站的定量数据与农民的访谈结合起来。图中可辨识物件：一排排读数、温度曲线、访谈记录本。

pos.zh: 数量的；定量的；可量化的

senses.title: About amount
senses.definition: concerned with amount, size or number rather than kind
senses.definitionCN: 关心数量、规模或数目，而非种类
senses.example: The report offers a quantitative picture of how many households lack clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用数量呈现了有多少家庭缺乏清洁用水。
senses.why: Quantus asked 'how much'. Quantitative marks whatever deals with that question instead of the question 'what kind'.
senses.whyCN: quantus 问的是“多少”。quantitative 标记处理这个问题的东西，而不是处理“何种”问题的东西。

senses.title: Measured and counted
senses.definition: based on measurement, counting and numerical records
senses.definitionCN: 以测量、计数与数值记录为基础
senses.example: Quantitative evidence showed a steady fall in soil moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 定量证据显示土壤含水量持续下降。
senses.why: Data become quantitative when they can be counted or measured, so that another researcher could repeat the count and get the same figure.
senses.whyCN: 数据在可被计数或测量时才算定量，因为另一位研究者可以重复计数并得到同一数字。

senses.title: Expressible as a number
senses.definition: able to be stated as a figure, rate or percentage
senses.definitionCN: 可以表述为数字、比率或百分比的
senses.example: Speed is quantitative because it can be given a number and a unit.
senses.exampleCN: 速度是定量的，因为它可以用一个数字加单位给出。
senses.why: The property itself is not a number, but it accepts one: give it a unit and a scale and it can be written as a figure.
senses.whyCN: 这种属性本身不是一个数字，但它接受数字：给它一个单位与一把尺，它就能写成一个数值。

senses.title: The style of a study
senses.definition: of research: using statistical samples and numerical analysis rather than interviews or interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指研究使用统计样本与数值分析，而非访谈或解释
senses.example: The team ran a quantitative study of sleep and exam performance.
senses.exampleCN: 团队开展了一项关于睡眠与考试成绩的定量研究。
senses.why: A quantitative study is one whose design turns behaviour into variables. Interviews may accompany it, but the spine is the number.
senses.whyCN: 定量研究是设计把行为变成变量的研究。访谈可以并存，但骨架是数字。

senses.title: Amount-based policy
senses.definition: of economic policy: working by expanding the amount of money or credit rather than by setting interest rates
senses.definitionCN: 指经济政策通过扩大货币或信贷数量、而非设定利率来运作
senses.example: The central bank turned to quantitative easing when rates were already near zero.
senses.exampleCN: 利率已接近零时，央行转向量化宽松。
senses.why: Economics uses the adjective for policy that changes quantities directly: the lever is the amount of money created, not its price.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用这个形容词指直接改变数量的政策：杠杆是创造出来的货币量，而不是货币的价格。

senses.title: Written as figures
senses.definition: presented in numerical form, as tables, charts or scores
senses.definitionCN: 以表格、图表或分数等数字形式呈现
senses.example: The results section is largely quantitative, with four tables and two graphs.
senses.exampleCN: 结果部分主要是数字呈现，有四张表与两幅图。
senses.why: Presentation is the visible half of the word: even before anyone counts, the material has been arranged as figures so that patterns can be read at a glance.
senses.whyCN: 呈现是这个词可见的一半：甚至在计数之前，材料已被排成数字，让模式一眼可读。

senses.title: On the more-or-less axis
senses.definition: judged by more or less rather than better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 按多与少判断，而不是按好与坏
senses.example: There was a quantitative gain in sales but no qualitative change in the product.
senses.exampleCN: 销售有数量上的增长，但产品没有性质上的改变。
senses.why: The word names the axis itself. A quantitative gain can be counted, even when nothing about the thing has become better in kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是轴本身。数量上的增长可以被计数，即使事物在性质上并未变好。

senses.title: The numerical side of science
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of a science that deals with measurable magnitudes and their relations
senses.definitionCN: 属于科学中处理可测大小及其关系的部分
senses.example: Quantitative chemistry asks how much of each substance reacts.
senses.exampleCN: 定量化学研究每种物质反应多少。
senses.why: Every science splits into a qualitative and a quantitative side. The quantitative side asks for magnitudes and laws that connect them.
senses.whyCN: 每门科学都分为定性与定量两面。定量的一面追问大小以及连接大小的规律。

intro.en: Quantitative is Medieval Latin quantitativus, from quantitas 'quantity', from quantus 'how much'. It was coined as the partner of qualitativus, the adjective for quality, and entered English through French in the 16th century.
intro.cn: quantitative 来自中古拉丁 quantitativus，出自 quantitas“数量”，再出自 quantus“多少”。它是作为 qualitativus（性质的形容词）的配对词被造出的，16 世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quantus asked 'how much, how many'. It belongs to the same interrogative family as qualis 'of what kind', and the pair still shapes scientific vocabulary.
items.cn: quantus 问“多少”。它与 qualis“何种”同属疑问词族，这对搭配至今塑造着科学词汇。

items.en: Quantitas named amount as a thing in itself. Roman writers used it for size, magnitude and number.
items.cn: quantitas 把数量当作一种事物来命名。罗马作者用它指大小、量值与数目。

items.en: Schoolmen built quantitativus for what belongs to quantity. The category was standard in philosophy before any modern science used it.
items.cn: 经院学者造出 quantitativus 指属于数量的东西。在现代科学使用它之前，这个范畴在哲学中已是标准。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English as quantitative, first in philosophy and mathematics.
items.cn: 法语把形容词 quantitatif 传给英语作 quantitative，最初用于哲学与数学。

items.en: Chemistry, physics and economics made quantitative the mark of reliable work: if it could be counted, it could be trusted.
items.cn: 化学、物理与经济学使 quantitative 成为可靠工作的标记：能计数就可信。

items.en: Quantitative easing named a monetary policy of the 2000s, while survey research made quantitative methods a standard phrase.
items.cn: 量化宽松命名了 2000 年代的货币政策，调查研究中“定量方法”也成为标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun, verb and the different-root qualitative. The meaning group contrasts numerical, measurable and statistical description.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与名词、动词，以及词根不同的 qualitative；词义组比较数值、可测与统计三类描述。

entries.definition: an amount or number. It is the noun that the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或数目。它是这个形容词所描述的名词。

entries.definition: to express something as a quantity. It is the action of making data quantitative.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物表示为数量。它就是把数据变成定量的动作。

entries.definition: in terms of amount. It tells how a comparison or measurement is made.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量上。它说明比较或测量如何进行。

entries.definition: relating to quality. It looks parallel but comes from qualis 'of what kind', not quantus 'how much'.
entries.definitionCN: 与性质相关的。它看起来结构平行，却来自 qualis“何种”，而非 quantus“多少”。

entries.definition: given in numbers. It says the form is numeric, while quantitative also implies measurement and amount.
entries.definitionCN: 以数字给出的。它说形式是数字的，而 quantitative 还隐含测量与数量。

entries.definition: able to be measured. It describes a property, while quantitative describes an approach or a body of data.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的。它描述一种属性，而 quantitative 描述一种做法或一批数据。

entries.definition: based on statistics. It adds sampling and probability to the plain idea of counting.
entries.definitionCN: 基于统计的。它在单纯计数之上加上了抽样与概率。

entries.definition: relating to measurement, especially in a system of units. It is narrower than quantitative.
entries.definitionCN: 与测量相关的，尤指单位制。它比 quantitative 更窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks put the word on the how-much axis, then let it cover data, studies, policies, tables and the numerical side of every science.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词放到“多少”这条轴上，再让它覆盖数据、研究、政策、表格与每门科学的数值一面。

normal.en: Split it as quant + itative: how much + adjective. It labels anything that answers with a number.
normal.cn: 拆成 quant + itative：多少、形容词。它标记任何用数字回答问题的事物。

normal.en: Picture a balance that converts two piles into two rows of figures.
normal.cn: 想象一架天平把两堆东西换算成两排数字。

normal.en: If the report counts households, it is quantitative; if it describes their lives, it is qualitative.
normal.cn: 如果报告统计户数，它是定量的；如果描述他们的生活，它是定性的。

normal.en: Quantitative easing changes the amount of money, not the price of borrowing.
normal.cn: 量化宽松改变货币的数量，而不是借贷的价格。

normal.en: A quantitative gain is more of the same, not a better kind of thing.
normal.cn: 数量上的增长是同类东西更多，而不是变成更好的种类。

abstract.en: Keep the quantus/qualis pair: one question asks how much, the other asks of what kind.
abstract.cn: 记住 quantus 与 qualis 的配对：一个问题问多少，另一个问何种。

abstract.en: Notice that the word describes both the data and the attitude: count it, then trust it.
abstract.cn: 注意这个词既描述数据，也描述态度：先计数，再相信。

abstract.en: Whenever you meet it, look for the unit: quantitative talk always carries a hidden 'of what'.
abstract.cn: 每次遇到它，都去找单位：定量话语总藏着一个“什么的多少”。

examples.en: The two reviews reached the same conclusion using different quantitative methods.
examples.cn: 这两篇综述用不同的定量方法得出了相同结论。

examples.en: Researchers reported a quantitative difference of about twelve percent.
examples.cn: 研究者报告了约百分之十二的数量差异。

examples.en: The bank's quantitative easing programme ran for three years.
examples.cn: 该银行的量化宽松计划持续了三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“宽提特提夫”：把宽窄高低都提出来，一条条变成数字。

root: 拉丁 quantus“多少”派生 quantitas“数量”，中古拉丁 quantitativus 作形容词；核心是“能数、能量、用数字回答”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all sit on the axis of amount: how many households, how much moisture, what speed, what study design, what money supply, what table, what gain, what magnitude. Qualitative asks what kind; quantitative asks how much.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都坐在“数量”这条轴上：多少户、多少水分、什么速度、什么研究设计、多少货币供给、哪张表、多少增长、多大数值。定性问“何种”，定量问“多少”。

core.en: Data are counted or measured and then written as figures that other people can compare.
core.cn: 数据被计数或测量，然后写成别人可以比较的数字。

branches.en: AXIS AND FORM: the subject is amount, and the form is numerical.
branches.cn: 轴与形式：主题是数量，形式是数字。

branches.en: DATA: counting and measurement make a value that can be repeated.
branches.cn: 数据：计数与测量造出可重复的数值。

branches.en: STUDY: a design turns behaviour into variables and gains into amounts.
branches.cn: 研究：设计把行为变成变量，把增益变成数量。

branches.en: POLICY: the lever is the quantity of money itself.
branches.cn: 政策：杠杆就是货币的数量本身。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the numerical branch asks for magnitudes and laws.
branches.cn: 科学：数值分支追问大小与规律。

intro.en: Quantitative is quantus plus quantitas plus the adjective suffix -ive. The items below follow the how-much stem and set it beside the how-kind stem.
intro.cn: quantitative 由 quantus、quantitas 与形容词后缀 -ive 构成。下列条目沿着“多少”词干，并与“何种”词干对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the question word and the noun. They show why quantity, quantify and quantitative all answer the same question.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出疑问词与名词，说明为什么 quantity、quantify 与 quantitative 都在回答同一个问题。

items.example: Quantitative measures dominated the report.
items.exampleCN: 报告以定量指标为主。

items.example: A small quantity of mercury remained.
items.exampleCN: 还剩下少量水银。

items.example: Scientists tried to quantify the damage.
items.exampleCN: 科学家试图量化损害。

items.example: The sites were compared quantitatively.
items.exampleCN: 这些地点作了定量比较。

items.example: Quantification made the claims testable.
items.exampleCN: 量化使这些主张可被检验。

items.example: Qualitative interviews added context.
items.exampleCN: 定性访谈补充了背景。

items.meaning: a specialist who measures building costs
items.example: The quantity surveyor priced the steelwork.
items.exampleCN: 工料测量师为钢结构估价。

items.meaning: a fixed amount; a discrete unit
items.example: Energy arrives in quanta, not in a smooth flow.
items.exampleCN: 能量以量子形式到来，而非平滑流动。

definition_zh: 不管；不顾；无论；不理会
definition_en: without being affected or stopped by; irrespective of
core_image: 巷道口的警铃连响，红灯旋转，送料车仍一辆接一辆往里开
scene: 警报连响三遍，红灯一直转，管理员仍让送料车往巷道里开。 The operator kept loading the shaft regardless of the warning lights.
sceneCN: 这里指不因警示而停止（第 2 个义项：不顾、不理会）；句意为操作员无视警示灯，继续往井巷送料。图中可辨识物件：警铃、红灯、送料车、巷道口。

pos.zh: 介词短语：不管；不顾；无论
相关副词用法（不带宾语）：无论如何；照样

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的名词与动词，义为「注视；看待；尊重」
由该词根加否定词尾构成，义为「无论如何；照样」
由现在分词转作介词，义为「关于」
由否定前缀加该词根构成，义为「无视；漠视」
由该词根加表示「充满」的形容词词尾构成，义为「留意的」

senses.title: Irrespective of a factor
senses.definition: without that factor making any difference to the result
senses.definitionCN: 某个因素对结果不产生任何影响
senses.example: Regardless of cost, the bridge must be rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 不论成本多少，这座桥都必须重建。
senses.why: The phrase removes a factor from consideration, leaving the decision unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语把某个因素从考虑中拿掉，决定因此不变。

senses.title: Despite a warning or obstacle
senses.definition: continuing an action even though something warns against it
senses.definitionCN: 即使有事物提出警告，仍继续行动
senses.example: He kept working regardless of the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 他不顾疼痛继续干活。
senses.why: Attention is what the word root means; the negative ending says attention is withheld.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「留意」，否定词尾表示「不留意」。

senses.title: Covering both alternatives
senses.definition: followed by whether or if to state that both alternatives are included
senses.definitionCN: 后接「是否」引出两种可能，表示两者都被包括
senses.example: The rule applies regardless of whether the firm is public.
senses.exampleCN: 无论公司是否上市，这条规定都适用。
senses.why: A choice between two cases is folded into one statement by naming them as irrelevant.
senses.whyCN: 把两种情形并列点出、再宣布其无关，就把选择折进了一句话。

senses.title: Without regard to a limit
senses.definition: spending or acting with no reference to a stated limit
senses.definitionCN: 花费或行动时不参照既定限度
senses.example: They spent regardless of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不顾预算限制地花钱。
senses.why: The phrase can cancel a limit as easily as it cancels a warning.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语取消警告，也同样可以取消限度。

senses.title: Ignoring a person's rank or feelings
senses.definition: treating everyone the same, or ignoring how someone feels
senses.definitionCN: 对所有人一视同仁，或无视某人的感受
senses.example: She spoke to everyone regardless of rank.
senses.exampleCN: 她跟每个人说话都不看级别。
senses.why: Social equality and social indifference use the same phrase, separated only by context.
senses.whyCN: 社会平等与社会冷漠用的是同一条短语，只靠语境区分。

senses.title: Universal rule in formal text
senses.titleCN: 正式文本中的普遍规定
senses.definition: in regulations, stating that a rule covers all cases without exception
senses.definitionCN: 在规章中说明某条规定无例外地覆盖所有情形
senses.example: Access is granted regardless of age.
senses.exampleCN: 不论年龄，均可进入。
senses.why: Regulations need a phrase that switches off every distinguishing condition at once.
senses.whyCN: 规章需要一条能把所有区分条件一次关掉的短语。

senses.title: Hedging a claim in academic writing
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的让步限定
senses.definition: used to say a pattern holds whatever method or sample is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明无论采用哪种方法或样本，规律都成立
senses.example: The pattern holds regardless of the method used.
senses.exampleCN: 无论采用哪种方法，这个规律都成立。
senses.why: A claim becomes more robust when it is said to survive every choice of method.
senses.whyCN: 一旦声称结论经得起任何方法选择，论点就显得更稳固。

senses.title: The fixed phrase regardless of the outcome
senses.titleCN: 固定说法「不管结果如何」
senses.definition: a set phrase stressing that effort will not depend on success
senses.definitionCN: 固定说法，强调努力不取决于成败
senses.example: The team trained hard regardless of the outcome.
senses.exampleCN: 无论结果如何，队伍都刻苦训练。
senses.why: Sporting and moral talk uses the phrase to separate effort from reward.
senses.whyCN: 体育与道德话语用它把努力与回报分开。

senses.title: The fixed phrase regardless of the consequences
senses.definition: a set phrase stressing that no later harm will change the decision
senses.definitionCN: 固定说法，强调后来的损害不会改变决定
senses.example: He approved the plan regardless of the consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 他不顾后果批准了这项计划。
senses.why: Naming the consequences and dismissing them is the strongest form of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 把后果点出来再宣布不顾，是这条短语最强的形式。

intro.en: Regardless of joins regard and the negative ending -less. Regard came through Old French regarder, to look at, from a Germanic verb of watching or guarding. The ending -less descends from Old English leas, free from. The phrase became common in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这条短语由表示「注视、留意」的词根与否定词尾合成。该词根经古法语进入英语，源头是日耳曼语中表示看守、注视的动词；否定词尾来自古英语中表示「脱离、没有」的形容词。整条短语在十九世纪通行起来。

items.en: The deep source meant to watch or guard, and it also gave English ward and guard.
items.cn: 更早的词源意为看守、注视，还给出了英语中表示「看守」的两个词。

items.en: The French verb meant to look at or look back at, built with a prefix of repetition.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为注视、回望，由表示重复的前缀构成。

items.en: English regard first meant a look or attention, then esteem, and later a single point looked at.
items.cn: 英语中这个词先指目光或留意，再指尊重，后来又指所关注的一点。

items.en: The Old English adjective meant free from or without, and it forms privative adjectives such as countless and hopeless.
items.cn: 这个古英语形容词意为「没有、脱离」，构成表示「无」的形容词，如无数与无望。

items.en: The adverb first meant without heed, and its earliest attested date is given only approximately.
items.cn: 这个副词最初意为「不留心」，其确切首见年代只能给约数。

items.en: The prepositional phrase with of spread in the nineteenth century, first in careless speech and later in formal rules.
items.cn: 带介词宾语的短语在十九世纪扩散，先出现在随意的口语，后进入正式规章。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the negative ending; the second group names other ways of setting a condition aside.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或否定词尾；第二组是其他把条件撇开的说法。

entries.definition: To look at, to consider, or esteem as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指注视、看待，作名词时指尊重。

entries.definition: The bare adverb meaning without heed, taking no object.
entries.definitionCN: 不带宾语的副词，意为「照样、不顾」。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning about or concerning.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「关于」的介词。

entries.definition: To ignore something deliberately, as verb or noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻意无视，可作动词或名词。

entries.definition: Attentive or mindful of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事留意的。

entries.definition: Without reference to a factor; the most formal twin.
entries.definitionCN: 不论某因素；最正式的对应说法。

entries.definition: Despite an obstacle that is actually present.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管存在实际阻碍。

entries.definition: A one-word preposition of concession.
entries.definitionCN: 表示让步的单词介词。

entries.definition: Paying no attention to a warning, with a note of blame.
entries.definitionCN: 指不理会警告，带责备意味。

entries.definition: A formal preposition or adverb meaning in spite of.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的介词或副词，意为「尽管」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal meaning of the parts: looking, and without.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用各部分的字面意思：注视，以及「没有」。

normal.en: Regard means to look at, and the negative ending means without, so the phrase says: without looking at it.
normal.cn: 词根意为注视，否定词尾意为没有，所以整条短语就是「不去看它」。

normal.en: The bare adverb takes no object; adding of lets a noun or a whether-clause follow.
normal.cn: 不带宾语的副词不接名词；加上介词后才能接名词或「是否」从句。

normal.en: Rules use the phrase to switch off exceptions, as in access regardless of age.
normal.cn: 规章用这条短语关掉例外，例如不论年龄都可进入。

normal.en: Sports talk uses regardless of the outcome to praise effort that does not depend on winning.
normal.cn: 体育话语用「不管结果如何」来称赞不取决于胜负的努力。

normal.en: The phrase regardless of the consequences is the strongest version, because the harm is named and then dismissed.
normal.cn: 「不顾后果」是最强版本，因为损害被点出来之后又被撇开。

abstract.en: The phrase is a switch that turns a whole category of facts off before the decision is made.
abstract.cn: 这条短语是一个开关，在做决定之前把一整类事实关掉。

abstract.en: Equality and recklessness speak with the same words, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 平等与鲁莽用同一套说法，只有语境能把它们分开。

abstract.en: To ignore something you must first have seen it: attention is denied, not absent.
abstract.cn: 要「不顾」某物，得先看见它：被否定的是留意，而不是留意本身不存在。

examples.en: Regardless of the weather, the survey team went out at dawn.
examples.cn: 无论天气如何，勘测队都在黎明出发。

examples.en: The scholarship is open to all students regardless of nationality.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金对所有学生开放，不论国籍。

examples.en: She kept the schedule regardless of the complaints.
examples.cn: 她不顾抱怨，坚持按日程执行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞嘎德莱斯」——眼睛都不往那边「看」，就是「不管、不顾」：不管、不顾、无论

root: 这个词根经古法语中意为「注视」的动词，源自日耳曼语中表示看守的动词；表示「没有、脱离」的形容词词尾来自古英语。这个词的确切首见年代不确定，带介词宾语的短语在十九世纪通行。无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a factor set aside, to a warning ignored, to fixed phrases that name outcomes and consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个被撇开的因素，走到被无视的警告，再到点明结果与后果的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rotating red lamp at a shaft mouth, and a cart that keeps rolling past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：井口旋转的红灯，以及一辆照样开过去的送料车。

branches.en: THE FACTOR REMOVED: cost or a limit makes no difference to the act.
branches.cn: 被拿掉的因素：成本或限度对行动不起作用。

branches.en: THE WARNING AND THE PERSON: pain is ignored, and rank or feeling is not consulted.
branches.cn: 警告与人：疼痛被无视，身份与感受也不被顾看。

branches.en: THE TWO CASES AND THE UNIVERSAL RULE: both alternatives are covered, and no exception remains.
branches.cn: 两种情形与普遍规定：两种可能都被覆盖，例外不再存在。

branches.en: THE ROBUST CLAIM: a pattern that survives every choice of method.
branches.cn: 稳固的论点：经得起任何方法选择的规律。

branches.en: THE FIXED PHRASES: outcome and consequences are named only to be dismissed.
branches.cn: 固定说法：结果与后果被点出，随即被撇开。

intro.en: The phrase is a Germanic root of watching plus an Old English negative ending, with no Latin layer.
intro.cn: 这条短语是「注视」的日耳曼词根加古英语否定词尾，没有拉丁语层次。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is involved, so the Latin list is empty for this entry.
latinIntro.cn: 本词条不涉及拉丁语来源，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: It also gave the English words ward and guard.
items.exampleCN: 它还给出了英语中表示看守的两个词。

items.example: The prefix added the idea of looking back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀加上了「回看」的意思。

items.example: The root carries attention in both uses.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在两种用法里都带「留意」。

items.example: It forms adjectives of absence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「缺少」的形容词。

items.example: The adverb takes no object of its own.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词本身不接宾语。

items.example: It lets a noun or a clause follow.
items.exampleCN: 它让名词或从句跟在后面。

items.example: It forms the verb disregard, to ignore deliberately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示刻意无视的动词。

items.example: The participle turned into a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个现在分词转成了介词。

items.example: The positive counterpart of the negative form.
items.exampleCN: 它是否定形式的肯定对应词。

items.example: The phrase as a whole cancels a condition.
items.exampleCN: 整条短语取消一个条件。

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的名词与动词，义为「注视；尊重」
加否定词尾构成，义为「不顾；照样」
由现在分词转成介词，义为「关于」
加表示「分开」的前缀构成，义为「无视」
加表示「充满」的词尾构成，义为「留意的」

definition_zh: 而不是；与……相对（用于对比两类事物，强调区别）
definition_en: rather than; used to contrast one kind of thing with another kind
core_image: 工作台上两个抽屉贴着不同标签，一边放工具，一边放零件
scene: 工作台上两个抽屉贴着不同标签，一边放工具，一边放零件。 The report counts full-time staff, as opposed to temporary workers.
sceneCN: 这里取「而不是」（第 1 个义项：对比两类，强调区别）；句意为报告统计的是全职员工，而不是临时工。

pos.zh: 介词短语：而不是；与……相对（强调区别）

collocations.phrase: as opposed to the previous method

senses.title: The contrast between two kinds
senses.definition: used to set one category against another so that the difference between kinds is clear
senses.definitionCN: 把一类与另一类并置，使种类差别清楚
senses.example: The report counts full-time staff, as opposed to temporary workers.
senses.exampleCN: 报告统计的是全职员工，而不是临时工。
senses.why: The phrase separates two categories rather than two individual things, which is why the nouns are usually plural or generic.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语分开的是两个类别而非两个个体，因此名词常为复数或统称。

senses.title: The preferred alternative
senses.definition: used to say that one option is chosen and the other is not
senses.definitionCN: 表示选定了某一选项，另一项未被选
senses.example: The committee chose the smaller site, as opposed to the cheaper one.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会选了较小的地块，而不是较便宜的那块。
senses.why: Here the contrast carries a decision: the first item is preferred, and the second is explicitly set aside.
senses.whyCN: 此处的对比带有决定：第一项被选中，第二项被明确搁置。

senses.title: The static comparison after a noun
senses.definition: used immediately after a noun phrase to name the contrasting kind
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟在名词短语之后，点出对照的另一类
senses.example: The study uses interviews, as opposed to questionnaires.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究使用访谈，而不是问卷。
senses.why: Static comparison does not describe an action; it fixes the identity of two kinds side by side.
senses.whyCN: 静态对比不描述动作，而是把两类事物的身份并排固定。

senses.title: The comparison of activities
senses.titleCN: 后接动名词：对比两种做法
senses.definition: used before an -ing form when two activities are being contrasted
senses.definitionCN: 对比两项活动时，用在动名词之前
senses.example: The team favoured testing early, as opposed to waiting for the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 团队倾向于尽早测试，而不是等到截止日期。
senses.why: Because the phrase is prepositional, an activity must be a gerund, not a bare verb or a clause.
senses.whyCN: 由于这是介词短语，活动必须用动名词，不能用光秃秃的动词或从句。

senses.title: The clarification rather than replacement
senses.titleCN: 澄清而非替换：与「代替」类说法分工
senses.definition: it clarifies which kind is meant instead of announcing that one thing replaces another
senses.definitionCN: 它澄清指的是哪一类，而不是宣布一物替代另一物
senses.example: The rule concerns employees, as opposed to contractors.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则针对雇员，而不是承包商。
senses.why: Nothing is being swapped here; the phrase is defining the scope of a word, which is the boundary against replacement phrases.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有东西被替换；短语是在界定一个词的范围，这就是与「代替」类说法的边界。

senses.title: The mid-clause or trailing aside
senses.titleCN: 句中或句末插入：补出对照项
senses.definition: inserted after a comma to add the contrasting kind without breaking the main clause
senses.definitionCN: 用逗号插入，补出对照类别而不打断主句
senses.example: The figures cover last year, as opposed to the year before.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数字涵盖去年，而不是前年。
senses.why: The aside keeps the main claim intact and attaches the excluded kind at the edge.
senses.whyCN: 旁白保持主要断言完整，把被排除的类别挂在边上。

senses.title: Defining terms in academic writing
senses.definition: in academic prose, used to define a term by excluding the neighbouring category
senses.definitionCN: 在学术文字中，通过排除相邻类别来界定一个术语
senses.example: The model measures adaptation, as opposed to adjustment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型衡量的是适应，而不是调整。
senses.why: Research often defines by contrast, and the phrase marks the excluded neighbour that gives the term its edge.
senses.whyCN: 研究常靠对比来定义，这个短语标出被排除的邻项，术语因此有了边界。

senses.title: The legal and technical classification
senses.titleCN: 法律与技术分类：相对而言
senses.definition: in legal or technical texts, used to separate two categories that carry different rules
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或技术文本中，分开适用不同规则的两个类别
senses.example: The clause applies to fixed assets, as opposed to current assets.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款适用于固定资产，而不是流动资产。
senses.why: Classification needs a phrase that keeps two categories apart without suggesting that one is better.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要一个把两类分开、又不暗示优劣的说法。

intro.en: Oppose comes from Latin opponere, to set against, itself ob-, against, and ponere, to place. The Latin line is clear; the English phrase is modern.
intro.cn: oppose 来自拉丁语 opponere「置于对面」，由 ob-「对着」与 ponere「放置」构成。拉丁语线索清楚，英语短语属近代。

items.en: Ponere, to place, is also the root of position and impose.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置」，也是 position 与 impose 的词根。

items.en: Opponere meant to place something in front of another as a counterweight.
items.cn: opponere 意为把某物放到另一物前面作为对抗。

items.en: English oppose appears in the Middle English period with the sense of resisting.
items.cn: 英语 oppose 见于中古英语，意为抵抗。

items.en: The past participle opposed supplies the fixed frame as opposed to.
items.cn: 过去分词 opposed 提供「as opposed to」这一固定框架。

items.en: The construction spreads in modern analytical writing; the exact date is approximate.
items.cn: 这一结构在近代分析性文字中传播，确切年代为约数。

note.en: The first group also contrasts two things but differs in grammar or in what is being replaced; the second group holds conjunctions and prepositions of preference.
note.cn: 第一组同样对比两物，但语法或替代关系不同；第二组是表取舍的连词与介词。

entries.definition: It says one thing takes the place of another, often in an action.
entries.definitionCN: 它指一物取代另一物，常用于动作。

entries.definition: It expresses preference between options and fits verbs as well as nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 它表达选项间的偏好，名词动词皆可。

entries.definition: It stresses divergence between two facts rather than two categories.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调两件事实的分歧，而非两个类别。

entries.definition: A formal phrase that stresses separateness of categories.
entries.definitionCN: 正式短语，强调类别的分离。

entries.definition: It opens a comparison by naming what the subject is not like.
entries.definitionCN: 通过点出主语不像什么来开启比较。

entries.definition: It simply denies and carries no category contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 它只作否定，不含类别对照。

entries.definition: It marks a preferred alternative in a lighter tone.
entries.definitionCN: 以较轻的语气标出更偏好的选项。

entries.definition: It weighs two things without defining either.
entries.definitionCN: 它衡量两物，不界定任何一方。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real placing root, the real category contrast and the real boundary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实「放置」词根、真实类别对比与真实边界。

normal.en: To oppose is to place one thing against another, so the phrase sets two kinds face to face.
normal.cn: 词根意为把一物放到另一物对面，所以短语把两类事物面对面摆开。

normal.en: It separates categories, not single objects.
normal.cn: 它分开的是类别，不是单个物体。

normal.en: It takes a noun or a gerund, never a clause.
normal.cn: 它接名词或动名词，从不接从句。

normal.en: It clarifies scope; it does not announce a replacement.
normal.cn: 它澄清范围，不宣布替代。

normal.en: In research it defines a term by excluding its neighbour.
normal.cn: 在研究中，它靠排除邻项来定义术语。

abstract.en: Like two drawers labelled differently, each holding a separate kind of thing.
abstract.cn: 像两个贴着不同标签的抽屉，各装一类东西。

abstract.en: Like a line drawn between two columns of a table before any counting begins.
abstract.cn: 像计数开始前，在表格两栏之间画的一道线。

abstract.en: Like a sign that says this path, not that one, without saying the other is worse.
abstract.cn: 像一块牌子写着走这条、不走那条，却不说另一条更差。

examples.en: The course is assessed by coursework, as opposed to a final examination.
examples.cn: 这门课以平时作业评定，而不是期末考试。

examples.en: The clause covers permanent staff, as opposed to seasonal workers.
examples.cn: 该条款涵盖正式员工，而不是季节工。

examples.en: They chose to renovate, as opposed to building anew.
examples.cn: 他们选择了翻修，而不是新建。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by grammar and purpose: two categories, a preferred option, a noun contrast, a gerund contrast, clarification rather than replacement, a mid-clause aside, academic definition, and legal classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按语法与用途区分：两类对比、取舍、名词对比、动名词对比、澄清而非替代、句中旁白、学术界定、法律分类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two drawers labelled differently, each holding a separate kind of thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个贴着不同标签的抽屉，各装一类东西。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: two kinds are separated, often in legal or technical texts.
branches.cn: 类别：分开两类，常见于法律或技术文本。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: one option is taken and the other set aside.
branches.cn: 取舍：选定一项，搁置另一项。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY: two practices are contrasted through gerunds.
branches.cn: 活动：通过动名词对比两种做法。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: scope is clarified by excluding the neighbouring term.
branches.cn: 定义：靠排除邻项来澄清范围。

branches.en: THE ASIDE: the excluded kind is attached at the edge of the clause.
branches.cn: 旁白：被排除的类别挂在从句边上。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin participle of placing against with English prepositions; the placing root is the core.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「置于对面」的分词与英语介词结合；「放置」词根是核心。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are opponere, to set against, and ponere, to place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 opponere「置于对面」与 ponere「放置」。

items.example: The verb also gives position and impose.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也给出两个相关英语词。

items.example: The prefix turns placing into opposition.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把「放置」变成「对抗」。

items.example: English keeps the resisting sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留「抵抗」义。

items.example: The participle supplies the fixed frame.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供固定框架。

items.example: The noun names the state of standing against.
items.exampleCN: 名词指对立状态。

items.example: The participle describes one side of a contest.
items.exampleCN: 分词描述竞争的一方。

items.example: The word names what lies across from something.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指位于对面之物。

items.example: The frame separates categories in formal prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在正式文字中分开类别。
