definition_zh: 矛盾的；相互抵触的；爱反驳的
definition_en: involving, containing, or causing a contradiction; expressing opposite ideas; given to contradicting others
core_image: 两个箭头指向相反方向，彼此顶撞
scene: 这组词中， The two witnesses gave contradictory accounts of what happened.
sceneCN: 这里 contradictory 是「矛盾的」（第 1 个义项：包含矛盾的）；句意：两位目击者对所发生的事给出了相互矛盾的描述。图中可辨识物件：两个人、两个相反的箭头、法庭、证词。

pos.zh: 矛盾的；抵触的
矛盾命题

senses.title: Involving a contradiction
senses.definition: containing or involving two statements that cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 包含两个不能同时为真的陈述的
senses.example: His explanation was contradictory and confusing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释自相矛盾，令人困惑。
senses.why: Latin dicere 'to say' + contra 'against': contradictory is 'said against', i.e., in conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dicere「说」+ contra「反对」：contradictory 是「对着说」，即冲突。

senses.title: Mutually opposed
senses.definition: so opposed that both cannot be true or possible at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 如此对立以至于不能同时为真或同时成立
senses.example: The two theories are contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个理论是相互矛盾的。
senses.why: Two things are contradictory when one asserts what the other denies.
senses.whyCN: 当一个断言另一个所否定的东西时，两者就是 contradictory 的。

senses.title: Given to contradicting others
senses.definition: tending to oppose or disagree with what others say
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于反对或不同意他人所说的
senses.example: He has a contradictory personality and always argues.
senses.exampleCN: 他性格爱唱反调，总要争论。
senses.why: A contradictory person speaks against others habitually.
senses.whyCN: 一个 contradictory 的人习惯性地对着他人说话。

senses.title: Conflicting with reality
senses.definition: conflicting with what is actually the case
senses.definitionCN: 与实际情况冲突的
senses.example: His claims are contradictory to the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与证据相矛盾。
senses.why: Something is contradictory to the facts when it says the opposite of them.
senses.whyCN: 当某物说的与事实相反时，它就与事实 contradictory。

senses.title: Inconsistent within itself
senses.definition: containing parts that disagree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 包含彼此不一致的部分的
senses.example: The report was internally contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告内部自相矛盾。
senses.why: When a single source contains opposing statements, it is internally contradictory.
senses.whyCN: 当一个来源包含对立陈述时，它就是内部 contradictory 的。

senses.title: In logic, a contradictory proposition
senses.definition: in logic, a proposition that denies exactly what another asserts
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中，恰好否定另一命题所断言内容的命题
senses.example: 'Some S is P' and 'No S is P' are contradictories.
senses.exampleCN: 「有些 S 是 P」和「没有 S 是 P」是矛盾命题。
senses.why: In logic, contradictories cannot both be true and cannot both be false.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学中，矛盾命题不能同真也不能同假。

senses.title: Impossible to reconcile
senses.definition: so different that they cannot be made compatible
senses.definitionCN: 如此不同以至于无法兼容的
senses.example: The two values are contradictory and cannot both be pursued.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种价值观相互矛盾，无法同时追求。
senses.why: Contradictory values pull in opposite directions and cannot both be satisfied.
senses.whyCN: 矛盾的价值观拉向相反方向，不能同时满足。

senses.title: Disagreeing loudly or habitually
senses.definition: characterized by habitual opposition in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以习惯性言语反对为特征的
senses.example: Her contradictory tone annoyed everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她动辄反驳的语气惹恼了桌上所有人。
senses.why: This sense stresses the manner of speaking against, not just logical conflict.
senses.whyCN: 此义强调对着说的方式，而不仅是逻辑冲突。

intro.en: Contradictory comes from Late Latin contradictorius, from contradicere 'to speak against'. The root is dicere 'to say', with contra 'against'.
intro.cn: contradictory 来自后期拉丁 contradictorius，源自 contradicere「对着说」。词根是 dicere「说」，前缀 contra「反对」。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, speak, declare'. It is the root of many English words: dictate, predict, verdict, dictionary.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲、宣告」。它是许多英语词的词根：dictate、predict、verdict、dictionary。

items.en: contra- means 'against'. contradicere is 'to speak against'.
items.cn: contra- 意为「反对」。contradicere 是「对着说」。

items.en: contradictus, past participle of contradicere, gave the stem used in English contradict.
items.cn: contradictus，contradicere 的过去分词，提供了英语 contradict 所用的词干。

items.en: contradictorius meant 'relating to contradiction'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: contradictorius 意为「与矛盾相关的」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Contradictory entered English in the 15th century, first in logic and rhetoric.
items.cn: contradictory 在 15 世纪进入英语，最初用于逻辑和修辞。

items.en: Today it appears in logic, law, science, and everyday talk about conflict.
items.cn: 如今它出现在逻辑、法律、科学以及关于冲突的日常谈论中。

note.en: The first group shares dicere; the second contains near-synonyms for conflicting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dicere；第二组是冲突的近义词。

entries.definition: to assert the opposite; the verb behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 断言相反；contradictory 背后的动词

entries.definition: a combination of opposite statements; the noun behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 相反陈述的组合；contradictory 背后的名词

entries.definition: to say before; pre- 'before' + dicere
entries.definitionCN: 预言；pre-「前」+ dicere

entries.definition: not staying the same throughout; close to contradictory but less absolute
entries.definitionCN: 前后不一致的；接近 contradictory 但不那么绝对

entries.definition: in disagreement or opposition; a more general term than contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 不一致或对立的；比 contradictory 更通用

entries.definition: completely different; contradictory adds the idea that both cannot be true
entries.definitionCN: 完全不同的；contradictory 还包含两者不能同真的含义

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: contra- 'against' + dicere 'to say': contradictory is speaking against, in conflict.
normal.cn: contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」：contradictory 是对着说，相冲突。

normal.en: contradict is the verb; contradictory is the adjective describing that conflict.
normal.cn: contradict 是动词；contradictory 是描述该冲突的形容词。

normal.en: predict says before; contradict says against; both use dicere 'to say'.
normal.cn: predict 向前说；contradict 对着说；都用 dicere「说」。

normal.en: self-contradictory means something disagrees with itself.
normal.cn: self-contradictory 意为某物与自己矛盾。

normal.en: In logic, contradictories are pairs that can't both be true or both be false.
normal.cn: 在逻辑中，矛盾命题是不能同真也不能同假的对子。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pointing at each other and colliding head-on: that's contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭对指着迎头相撞：这就是 contradictory。

abstract.en: Think of one person saying 'yes' while another says 'no' about the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人说「是」而另一个人对同一件事说「否」。

abstract.en: Think of a scale tipping both ways at once — impossible, hence contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平同时向两边倾斜——不可能，因此是 contradictory。

examples.en: The witness gave contradictory testimony on two different days.
examples.cn: 证人在两天里给出了相互矛盾的证词。

examples.en: These two findings are contradictory and cannot both be correct.
examples.cn: 这两个发现相互矛盾，不可能都正确。

examples.en: His policy is self-contradictory: it promises both higher spending and lower taxes.
examples.cn: 他的政策自相矛盾：既承诺更高支出又承诺更低税收。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康吹迪克特瑞」——康（con）师傅对着（contra）说（dicere）的人唱反调 → contradictory 矛盾的

root: 拉丁 contradicere「反驳、与……矛盾」（contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」）；contradict- 词干 + -ory 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'speaking against': statements, theories, personalities, or logical propositions may be contradictory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「对着说」：陈述、理论、性格或逻辑命题都可能是 contradictory 的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows clashing head-on.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭迎头相撞。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONFLICT: statements that cannot both hold.
branches.cn: 逻辑冲突：不能同时成立的陈述。

branches.en: MUTUAL OPPOSITION: things so opposed they cannot coexist.
branches.cn: 相互对立：如此对立以至于不能共存的事物。

branches.en: OPPOSITIONAL PERSON: someone who habitually speaks against.
branches.cn: 唱反调的人：习惯性对着说的人。

branches.en: AGAINST EVIDENCE: claims that clash with the facts.
branches.cn: 违背证据：与事实冲突的主张。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONTRADICTORY: a proposition that is the exact opposite.
branches.cn: 逻辑矛盾命题：恰好相反的命题。

intro.en: Contradictory is the -ory adjective from contradict. The suffix -ory means 'having the nature of'; the inner parts are fossilized.
intro.cn: contradictory 是 contradict 的 -ory 形容词。后缀 -ory 意为「具有……性质的」；内部部分已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere 'to say' produced a large family: dictate, predict, contradict, verdict, dictionary, dedicate, indicate. The root appears as dic-, dict-, or dit-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere「说」产生了大家族：dictate、predict、contradict、verdict、dictionary、dedicate、indicate。词根以 dic-、dict- 或 dit- 形式出现。

items.example: Don't contradict yourself.
items.exampleCN: 别自相矛盾。

items.example: There is a contradiction here.
items.exampleCN: 这里有个矛盾。

items.example: The reports are contradictory.
items.exampleCN: 报告相互矛盾。

items.example: Scientists predict rain.
items.exampleCN: 科学家预报有雨。

items.example: The boss dictated a letter.
items.exampleCN: 老板口述了一封信。

items.example: The jury gave a verdict.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团作出了裁决。

items.example: Look it up in the dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 在词典里查一下。

items.example: The sign indicates danger.
items.exampleCN: 标志指示危险。

items.example: She dedicated the book to her mother.
items.exampleCN: 她把书献给了母亲。

definition_zh: 感觉的；感官的；感觉信息的
definition_en: relating to the senses, or to the organs and nerves that receive information from the world
core_image: 一排朝外的小天线，把光、声、热、压力转成身体能读的信号
scene: 婴儿第一次摸到粗糙的毛毯，手指缩了一下，脸上露出惊讶： The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
sceneCN: 这里指「感觉的、与感官有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及感觉接收与传导）；句意为婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到毛毯粗糙的质地。

pos.zh: 感觉的；与感官有关的
感觉信息的；由感官接收的

senses.title: Relating to the senses
senses.definition: concerning the senses or the process of receiving impressions through them
senses.definitionCN: 关于感觉，或关于通过感官接收印象的过程
senses.example: The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到粗糙的质地。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the channel from world to body, so it points at the receiving side rather than the thinking side.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记从外界到身体这条通道上的一切，因此指向接收端而非思考端。

senses.title: Of the sense organs
senses.definition: belonging to organs such as the eyes, ears and skin that receive stimuli
senses.definitionCN: 属于眼、耳、皮肤等接收刺激的器官
senses.example: Sensory organs line the surface of the body and open into it.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉器官分布在体表，并向体内开口。
senses.why: Organs are the hardware of feeling, so the adjective attaches to the structures that face the outside world.
senses.whyCN: 器官是感觉的硬件，因此这个形容词附着在那些朝向外部世界的结构上。

senses.title: Of sensory nerves
senses.definition: relating to the nerves that carry signals from the body toward the brain
senses.definitionCN: 与把信号从身体传向脑的神经有关的
senses.example: A sensory nerve carries the signal from the fingertip to the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号从指尖传到脊柱。
senses.why: Once the signal leaves the organ it travels on a nerve, and the same adjective follows it inward.
senses.whyCN: 信号离开器官后由神经运输，同一个形容词也随之前行。

senses.title: Sensory input
senses.titleCN: 感觉输入：进入身体的信息
senses.definition: information coming into the body through the senses, treated as data
senses.definitionCN: 通过感官进入身体、被当作数据处理的信息
senses.example: Too much sensory input can overwhelm a small child.
senses.exampleCN: 过多的感觉输入会让幼童难以承受。
senses.why: The engineering metaphor turns feeling into a stream of signals, which is why input is the usual partner of sensory.
senses.whyCN: 工程比喻把感觉变成一股信号流，因此「输入」是这个形容词最常见的搭配。

senses.title: Sensory experience
senses.titleCN: 感官体验：由五种感觉组成的经历
senses.definition: an experience built from what can be seen, heard, touched, tasted or smelled
senses.definitionCN: 由视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉或嗅觉构成的体验
senses.example: The museum designs a sensory experience rather than a lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座博物馆设计的是感官体验，而非讲座。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes a whole event that is addressed to the body rather than to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述一整段面向身体的经历，而不是面向知识。

senses.title: Sensory evaluation of food
senses.definition: the professional testing of food by taste, smell, appearance and texture
senses.definitionCN: 靠味、嗅、外观与质地进行的食品专业测试
senses.example: Trained panellists carry out sensory evaluation of the new bread.
senses.exampleCN: 受训的评审员对新面包进行感官评价。
senses.why: Industry uses the word because the instrument is a human sense organ, and the measurement is what the senses report.
senses.whyCN: 行业使用这个词，因为仪器就是人的感官，测量结果就是感官所报告的东西。

senses.title: Sensory processing
senses.titleCN: 感觉加工：大脑整理信号的过程
senses.definition: the way the nervous system sorts, combines and interprets signals from the senses
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统对来自感官的信号进行分类、合并与解释的方式
senses.example: Sensory processing difficulties make noise feel painful.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉加工困难会让噪声变得难以忍受。
senses.why: The focus moves from reception to handling: signals are taken in, then sorted by the brain.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从接收转到处理：信号被接收后由脑整理。

senses.title: Sensory overload or deprivation
senses.definition: states in which the senses receive far too much stimulation or almost none
senses.definitionCN: 感官受到过多刺激或几乎没有刺激的状态
senses.example: Sensory deprivation in a silent room can distort time.
senses.exampleCN: 在无声房间里的感觉剥夺会扭曲时间感。
senses.why: Both extremes test the same channel, so the adjective marks conditions defined by the amount of incoming signal.
senses.whyCN: 两个极端考验的都是同一条通道，因此这个形容词标记由输入量多少来定义的状态。

intro.en: Sensory is sense plus the Latin suffix -orius, from Latin sensorius, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensory 由 sense 加拉丁后缀 -orius 构成，源头为拉丁 sensorius，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel, perceive or think, and its past participle sensus supplied the noun for feeling and the root of the whole family.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知或思考，其过去分词 sensus 提供表示感觉的名词，也是整个词族的词根。

items.en: The relational adjective sensorius meant belonging to feeling or to the seat of feeling; it survives mainly through English sensory.
items.cn: 关系形容词 sensorius 意为属于感觉或感觉中枢的，主要通过英语 sensory 留存下来。

items.en: Sense entered English through Old French sens, and the adjective sensory appears in English writing by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: sense 经古法语 sens 进入英语，形容词 sensory 在 17 世纪的英语写作中出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology split the nervous system into sensory and motor sides, fixing the modern technical use.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把神经系统分为感觉侧与运动侧，确立了现代技术用法。

items.en: Psychology extended the word to input, processing and experience, so sensory now covers far more than the organs themselves.
items.cn: 心理学把这个词扩展到输入、加工与体验，因此 sensory 现在涵盖的范围远大于器官本身。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of sensory is not firmly dated, and the earlier Medieval Latin status of sensorius is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensory 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，sensorius 在中世纪拉丁语中的使用状况也有争议。

note.en: The first group contains words built on the same root that are routinely confused; the second contains adjectives with a similar feel.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常被混淆的词；第二组是语感相近的形容词。

entries.definition: Appealing to the senses in a rich, pleasurable way; it praises the experience rather than describing the nerve pathway.
entries.definitionCN: 以丰富愉悦的方式取悦感官；它赞美体验，而非描述神经通路。

entries.definition: Relating to bodily pleasure, often sexual; it is about desire, not about sensory reception.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体快感有关，常指情欲；它讲欲望，而非感觉接收。

entries.definition: A device that detects a physical quantity; a sensor is a machine, while sensory describes a living system.
entries.definitionCN: 检测物理量的装置；sensor 是机器，sensory 描述活体系统。

entries.definition: An official who removes objectionable material; it sounds like sensor but comes from a different Latin verb meaning to assess.
entries.definitionCN: 删除不当内容的官员；读音像 sensor，但来自另一个意为「评估」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Relating to perception, the process of recognising what the senses deliver; sensory is the input, perceptual is the interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 与知觉有关的，即识别感官所给内容的过程；sensory 是输入，perceptual 是解释。

entries.definition: Relating to touch; it names one sense, while sensory covers all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 与触觉有关的；它只指一种感觉，而 sensory 涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves; sensory signals travel on neural pathways, but neural does not itself mean felt.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的；感觉信号走神经通路，但 neural 本身不表示「被感觉到」。

entries.definition: Quick to detect or react to small changes; it describes a capacity, not the whole sensory system.
entries.definitionCN: 对微小变化反应敏锐；它描述一种能力，而非整个感觉系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin participle, the real physiology split and the real industry phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁分词、真实的生理学分工与真实的行业短语。

normal.en: Sensus is the past participle of sentire to feel, so sensory means belonging to feeling.
normal.cn: sensus 是 sentire「感觉」的过去分词，因此 sensory 意为「属于感觉的」。

normal.en: Physiology pairs sensory with motor: signals come in on one side and commands go out on the other.
normal.cn: 生理学把 sensory 与 motor 配对：信号从一侧进入，指令从另一侧发出。

normal.en: Sensory input, sensory processing and sensory overload trace a signal from door to brain to breakdown.
normal.cn: sensory input、sensory processing、sensory overload 串起信号从入口到大脑再到过载的全过程。

normal.en: Sensory evaluation is the food industry phrase for judging with eyes, nose, tongue and teeth.
normal.cn: sensory evaluation 是食品行业用语，指用眼、鼻、舌与牙齿作评判。

normal.en: The same root gives sense, sensation, sensible and sensor, so the family can be read from one stem.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor，因此整个词族可由一个词干读出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of small antennae facing outward, each tuned to one kind of weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一排朝外的小天线，每一根只对一种天气敏感。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that is also a filter: everything enters, but only some of it is let through.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门同时是过滤器：一切都来到门口，只有一部分被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a volume knob turned to maximum and then to zero; both extremes test the same channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个音量旋钮先拧到最大再拧到零：两个极端考验的是同一条通道。

examples.en: Sensory nerves carry information from the skin to the brain.
examples.cn: 感觉神经把信息从皮肤传到大脑。

examples.en: The room was designed to reduce sensory input for autistic children.
examples.cn: 这个房间的设计目的是为自闭症儿童减少感觉输入。

examples.en: A trained panel performed a sensory evaluation of the cheese.
examples.cn: 一个受训评审组对这款奶酪做了感官评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三色瑞」（sensory）——三种颜色都靠眼睛去感觉 → 感觉的；感官的

root: 拉丁 sensorius「属于感觉的」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；sentire 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run along one channel: the senses in general, the organs, the nerves, the incoming data, the experience, the professional test, the processing, and the extremes of too much or too little.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条通道展开：泛指感觉、器官、神经、输入的数据、体验、专业测试、加工过程，以及过多与过少的两个极端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: antennae facing the world, turning light, sound and pressure into readable signals.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向世界的天线，把光、声与压力转成可读的信号。

branches.en: THE ORGANS: eyes, ears and skin that face the world.
branches.cn: 这些器官：面对外部世界的眼、耳与皮肤。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL'S TRIP: nerves carry it inward, input names it as data.
branches.cn: 信号的行进：神经把它带入体内，「输入」把它命名为数据。

branches.en: TWO USES OF THE SAME WORD: a personal experience, and a professional test of a product.
branches.cn: 同一个词的两种用法：个人的体验，以及对产品的专业测试。

branches.en: THE LOAD: too much or too little stimulation breaks the system.
branches.cn: 负荷：刺激过多或过少都会让系统失灵。

branches.en: FROM WORLD TO MIND: the same adjective covers reception and the processing that follows.
branches.cn: 从世界到心智：同一个形容词既涵盖接收，也涵盖随后的加工。

intro.en: Sensory is a Latin relational adjective in -orius; the stem sens- also builds sense, sensation, sensible and sensor.
intro.cn: sensory 是带 -orius 的拉丁关系形容词；词干 sens- 还构成 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire feel gives sensus feeling and sensorius of feeling; English also borrowed sensorium, the seat of the senses, from Late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」衍生 sensus「感觉」与 sensorius「属于感觉的」；英语还从晚期拉丁语借入 sensorium「感觉中枢」。

items.example: The verb covers both bodily feeling and opinion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既指身体感觉，也指看法。

items.example: Sensus is the source of sense and sensation.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 与 sensation 的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成关系形容词。

items.example: Sensory input shapes early learning.
items.exampleCN: 感觉输入塑造早期学习。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: The sensor records temperature every minute.
items.exampleCN: 传感器每分钟记录一次温度。

items.meaning: the seat or system of the senses
items.example: The sensorium gathers signals from the whole body.
items.exampleCN: 感觉系统汇集来自全身的信号。

items.example: Sensorineural hearing loss affects the inner ear.
items.exampleCN: 感音神经性听力损失影响内耳。

items.meaning: judging a product by the senses
items.example: Sensory evaluation scored the bread on texture.
items.exampleCN: 感官评价给面包的质地打了分。

definition_zh: 无记名投票；选票；投票总数；候选人名单
definition_en: a secret method of voting, or the paper on which a voter marks a choice
core_image: 一只封口的木箱摆在门口，人人把折好的纸片投进去，纸上不写名字
scene: 会场门口摆着一只封口的木箱，代表们排队把折好的纸片塞进缝里。 Each delegate folded the ballot and dropped it through the slot of the sealed box.
sceneCN: 会场门口摆着一只封口的木箱，代表们排队把折好的纸片塞进缝里；句中的这个词指「承载个人选择的那张选票纸」（第 2 个义项：选民在票面上作记号、再投入票箱的那张纸）。

pos.zh: 无记名投票；选票；投票总数；候选人名单
使投票表决；把……列入选票
投票

senses.title: Voting in secret
senses.titleCN: 不记名投票：不让别人看见你选谁
senses.definition: a system in which people vote secretly, so that no one knows how each person voted
senses.definitionCN: 一种不公开各人选择的投票方式
senses.example: The union decided to use a ballot rather than a show of hands.
senses.exampleCN: 工会决定采用不记名投票，而不是举手表决。
senses.why: The word began as the name of the little ball dropped into a box; the secrecy of that drop became the name of the whole method.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指投进箱子的小球；这种不让人看见的投法，后来成了整套制度的名字。

senses.title: The paper slip
senses.titleCN: 选票纸：承载一个人选择的那张纸
senses.definition: the printed paper on which a voter marks a choice
senses.definitionCN: 投票人在上面标记选择的印刷纸片
senses.example: She folded the ballot and pushed it through the slot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把选票折好，塞进投票口的缝里。
senses.why: From the ball to the paper: the object that carries one person's choice keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 从小球到纸片：承载一个人选择的那件东西沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: The counted total
senses.titleCN: 投票总数：所有票加起来的数目或结果
senses.definition: the total number of votes recorded in an election, or the result they produce
senses.definitionCN: 一次选举中记录下来的全部票数，或这些票造成的结果
senses.example: He won the ballot by a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 他以微弱优势赢得了这次投票。
senses.why: A ballot is also the count: once the slips are in the box, the word shifts from the container to the sum inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指计票：纸片进了箱子之后，词义就从容器转指箱内的总数。

senses.title: The right to vote
senses.titleCN: 投票权：投出那一票的资格
senses.definition: the right to vote, or the act of exercising that right
senses.definitionCN: 投票的权利，或行使这项权利的行为
senses.example: Women fought for the ballot for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性为争取投票权奋斗了几十年。
senses.why: Possession of a ballot slip implies permission to cast it, so the object came to stand for the right itself.
senses.whyCN: 手里有选票就意味着有权投出它，于是这件实物也代表了权利本身。

senses.title: The list of candidates
senses.titleCN: 候选人名单：供人挑选的那份名单
senses.definition: the list of candidates or measures that voters may choose among
senses.definitionCN: 供选民从中选择的候选人名单或议题清单
senses.example: Two new parties will be on the ballot in November.
senses.exampleCN: 两个新政党将出现在十一月的选票名单上。
senses.why: A ballot lists the choices before it records them; the sheet is both a menu and a tally.
senses.whyCN: 选票先列出可选项，再记录选择；一张纸既是菜单，也是计数表。

senses.title: Drawing lots
senses.titleCN: 抽签：从容器里摸出小球来决定
senses.definition: the old practice of deciding by drawing small balls or tokens from a container
senses.definitionCN: 旧时从容器中摸出小球或筹码来决定结果的作法
senses.example: In the old guild, officers were chosen by ballot from a bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的行会里，执事是从碗中抽签选出的。
senses.why: Before paper, a ballot was a ball; drawing balls from a bowl was the original random method.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张之前，这个词指的就是一颗球；从碗里摸球，正是最早的随机决定法。

senses.title: To hold a ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：组织一次投票表决
senses.definition: to ask a group of people to vote on an issue
senses.definitionCN: 让一群人就某个问题投票
senses.example: The committee balloted its members on the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就新规则让成员投票表决。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of arranging: to ballot is to put the question to a ballot.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示安排动作的动词：举行投票，就是把问题交给一次表决。

senses.title: To cast a vote by ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：以不记名方式投票
senses.definition: to vote by marking a ballot paper and placing it in the ballot box
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上作记号并投入票箱来投票
senses.example: Every delegate balloted before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 每位代表都在中午前投了票。
senses.why: The verb names the act of using the paper, not the counting that follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指使用那张纸的动作，而不是随后的计票。

intro.en: Ballot reached English through French from Italian ballotta 'little ball'. That Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball; what is clear is the box full of little balls.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语又借自意大利语中表示「小球」的词。那个意大利词一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式；可以确定的是那只装满小球的投票箱。

items.en: Italian ballotta meant 'little ball', a diminutive of balla 'ball'. Words for a ball of similar shape exist across the Romance languages.
items.cn: 意大利语中表示「小球」的那个词，是「球」的指小形式。罗曼语各族中都有形状相近的「球」的说法。

items.en: In Venice and other Italian city-states, voters dropped small balls or tokens into a container to record a choice without showing it.
items.cn: 在威尼斯等意大利城邦，投票人把小圆球或筹码投进容器，以记录不公开的选择。

items.en: French borrowed the Italian word as ballotte, and English took the same word from French in the same period.
items.cn: 法语借入这个意大利词，英语又在同一时期从法语借入同一个词。

items.en: The earliest English records show the word as the little ball used in voting; the paper-slip meaning appears considerably later.
items.cn: 英语最早记录中，这个词指投票用的小球；纸片选票的意思出现得晚得多。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word meant the paper slip and the whole secret method, and the verb followed. The first recorded dates are approximate.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词已指选票纸与整套无记名投票方式，动词用法也随之出现。首见年代为大致估计。

note.en: The first group looks similar in spelling or sound; the second group is close in meaning. None of the look-alikes shares the Italian origin.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上相近；第二组意思接近。第一组里的词没有一个是同一个意大利来源。

entries.definition: heavy material used to steady a ship; the ending is different and the source is Germanic, not Italian
entries.definitionCN: 压舱物；词尾不同，来源是日耳曼语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a narrative song or poem; it ends differently and comes from Old French, not Italian
entries.definitionCN: 叙事歌谣；词尾不同，来自古法语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a form of stage dance; its final vowel is pronounced, unlike the light final vowel of ballot
entries.definitionCN: 芭蕾舞；词尾元音要读出来，而目标词的词尾元音很轻。

entries.definition: a French verse form; it has an extra final letter and a different stress
entries.definitionCN: 一种法语诗体；词尾多一个字母，重音也不同。

entries.definition: the general act of expressing a choice in an election or meeting
entries.definitionCN: 在选举或会议中表达选择的统称。

entries.definition: the count of votes, or a survey of public opinion
entries.definitionCN: 票数统计，或对民意的调查。

entries.definition: a direct vote on a political question, often one about sovereignty
entries.definitionCN: 就政治问题举行的直接投票，常涉及主权归属。

entries.definition: a vote on one specific question put to the whole electorate
entries.definitionCN: 就某一个具体问题交给全体选民表决的投票。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real object behind the word, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词背后的真实物件、真实的复合词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The original ballot was a little ball: a voter dropped it into a box so no one could see which side it stood for.
normal.cn: 最早的选票是一颗小球：投票人把它投进箱子，谁也看不见它代表哪一边。

normal.en: Ballot box and ballot paper split the object in two: the container keeps the slips, the paper carries the choice.
normal.cn: 投票箱与选票纸把这件东西分成两半：箱子装纸片，纸片承载选择。

normal.en: Secret ballot is the fixed phrase that names the method; adding secret turns the object into a procedure.
normal.cn: 不记名投票是固定说法，加上「秘密的」这个修饰，就把物件变成了程序。

normal.en: The verb ballot means to send a question to a vote, and the prefix re- means to send it a second time.
normal.cn: 动词形式表示把问题交给投票；加上表示「再次」的前缀，就是再投一次。

normal.en: On the ballot simply means that a name or a question has reached the list voters will see.
normal.cn: 「列入选票」这个说法，意思是一个名字或问题已经进入选民会看到的那份名单。

abstract.en: Picture a ball dropped into a dark box: the hand is hidden, and only the sound of one small object falling is heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗球落进暗箱：手被遮住，只听得见一个小东西落下的声音。

abstract.en: Secrecy is the whole invention: the box hides the hand, and the paper hides the name.
abstract.cn: 保密正是这项发明的全部：箱子藏住手，纸片藏住名字。

abstract.en: So a ballot makes a choice countable but not traceable: the count is public, the chooser is not.
abstract.cn: 所以它让选择可以计数、却无法追溯：计数是公开的，选择者不是。

examples.en: Citizens cast their ballots before work.
examples.cn: 市民上班前投了票。

examples.en: The ballot paper was folded twice before it went into the box.
examples.cn: 选票纸折了两折才放进箱子。

examples.en: The club balloted its members on the change of meeting night.
examples.cn: 俱乐部就更改集会日期让会员投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴洛特」——把小球投进暗箱，谁也不知道你选了谁 → 无记名投票

root: 经法语上溯到意大利语 ballotta（小球），其更早来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object: a little ball dropped into a box, then the paper that replaces it, then the count and the right that grow out of that paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一样东西展开：先是一颗投进箱子的小球，接着是取代它的纸片，再由这张纸生出计数与权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small ball goes into a sealed box, and the choice is counted without being traced.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗小球落进封口的箱子，选择被计数却不被追溯。

branches.en: HIDDEN CHOICE: secret voting and drawing lots both hide the deciding hand inside a container.
branches.cn: 藏起选择：不记名投票与抽签都把做决定的手藏进容器里。

branches.en: ONE PAPER AND THE WHOLE COUNT: the slip carries a single choice, while the total turns those slips into a result.
branches.cn: 一张纸与全部票数：纸片承载单个选择，总数则把这些纸片变成一个结果。

branches.en: RIGHT AND PROCEDURE: the right to vote is exercised through the act of balloting a group.
branches.cn: 权利与程序：投票权正是通过让一群人投票这一程序来行使的。

branches.en: THE MENU: the same word also names the candidates among whom a choice is made.
branches.cn: 选项单：这个词也指供人挑选的候选人名单。

branches.en: CASTING THE PAPER: the verb names the act of marking a ballot and putting it in the box.
branches.cn: 投下纸片：动词指的是在选票上作记号并把它放进票箱的动作。

intro.en: Ballot is a borrowed noun, so its English family grows from compounds and the agent suffix rather than from a Latin root.
intro.cn: 这个词是借入的名词，所以它在英语里的词族靠复合词与表示人的后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin family for ballot; the deeper source of the Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball. The formations below are English, and the Italian origin is told in the history section.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族；那个意大利词的更深来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。下面列出的是英语中的构词，意大利语来源已在词源部分说明。

items.structure: ballot + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaning: a person who votes by ballot
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every balloter must sign the roll.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都必须在名册上签名。

items.meaning: the act of voting by ballot
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票这一行为（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Balloting lasted from morning until dusk.
items.exampleCN: 投票从早晨一直进行到黄昏。

items.meaning: voted by ballot; put to a ballot
items.meaningCN: 已以无记名方式投票的；被付诸表决的（后缀表示过去或被动）
items.example: The proposal was balloted last month.
items.exampleCN: 这项提议上个月已付诸表决。

items.structure: ballot + box (compound: the second element names the container)
items.meaning: the sealed box into which ballots are dropped
items.meaningCN: 投票箱（后一成分表示容器，语义从「票」转到「装票的箱子」）
items.example: Officials carried the ballot box to the counting room.
items.exampleCN: 工作人员把投票箱搬到计票室。

items.structure: ballot + paper (compound: the second element names the material)
items.meaning: the printed sheet on which a vote is marked
items.meaningCN: 选票纸（后一成分表示纸张，语义从「投票方式」转到「承载选择的纸」）
items.example: The ballot paper listed six names.
items.exampleCN: 选票纸上列着六个名字。

items.structure: secret + ballot (compound: the first element names the quality)
items.meaning: a ballot in which each vote is hidden
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票（前一成分表示「秘密的」，语义落在投票的保密性上）
items.example: The union adopted the secret ballot long before the law required it.
items.exampleCN: 早在法律要求之前，工会就采用了无记名投票。

items.structure: ballot + measure (compound: the second element names the question)
items.meaning: a question placed on a ballot for voters to decide
items.meaningCN: 付诸公投的议案（后一成分表示「议案」，语义从投票动作转到被表决的问题）
items.example: Voters rejected the ballot measure by a wide margin.
items.exampleCN: 选民以很大差距否决了这项公投议案。

items.meaningCN: 重新投票（前缀表示「再次」，语义加在投票动作之前）
items.example: The committee had to reballot the question.
items.exampleCN: 委员会不得不就这个问题重新投票。

definition_zh: 不可再生的（储量有限、补充速度远慢于消耗，因而终会耗尽的资源，如化石燃料与多数矿产）
definition_en: existing in a limited stock that is used far faster than nature can replace it, so that it is eventually exhausted
core_image: 一桶油从地下抽出，抽一桶少一桶；矿脉挖空只剩石渣，要再生成得等上地质年代
scene: 矿工在图表上把储量曲线一路往下画。 Coal is a nonrenewable resource because it formed over millions of years.
sceneCN: 这里 nonrenewable 指「补充远慢于消耗、终会耗尽的」（第 1 个义项：资源属性）；句意为煤是不可再生资源，因为它需要数百万年才形成。

pos.zh: 不可再生的（作定语，无比较级；英式拼写带连字符）
不可再生资源（名词化后常用复数形式）

derivatives.zh: non-（拉丁 non「不」）→ 不、非：加在词前表示否定
renew + -able → 可再生的：使用后能被自然补充的
re-（再次）+ novare（使新）→ 更新、续期
ex-（向外）+ haurire（拉丁「汲取」）+ -ible → 会耗尽的：能被抽干的
de-（去除）+ plere（拉丁「填满」）→ 耗尽：把填满的东西取空
finis（拉丁「界限」）+ -ite → 有限的：有边界的

senses.title: The exhaustible resource
senses.definition: a resource held in a fixed stock that shrinks with every unit taken
senses.definitionCN: 储量为固定存量、每取用一单位就减少一单位的资源
senses.example: Coal is a nonrenewable resource because it formed over millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 煤是不可再生资源，因为它需要数百万年才形成。
senses.why: the word is about the ratio of use to replacement, not about whether replacement ever happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词讲的是使用与补充的比值，而不是补充是否可能发生。

senses.title: Fossil fuels
senses.definition: coal, oil and gas made from ancient life and burned far faster than they formed
senses.definitionCN: 由远古生命形成、燃烧速度远快于形成速度的煤、石油与天然气
senses.example: The economy still runs mostly on nonrenewable fossil fuels.
senses.exampleCN: 经济仍主要依靠不可再生的化石燃料运转。
senses.why: the clearest case is fuel that took epochs to make and minutes to burn.
senses.whyCN: 最清楚的例子就是耗上纪元形成、几分钟烧完的燃料。

senses.title: Minerals and metals
senses.definition: ore bodies and rare elements concentrated by geology and mined out of rock
senses.definitionCN: 由地质作用富集、从岩石中采出的矿体与稀有元素
senses.example: Copper ore is nonrenewable even though copper can be recycled.
senses.exampleCN: 铜矿是不可再生的，尽管铜可以被回收。
senses.why: the ore is the resource; recycling saves the metal but does not rebuild the deposit.
senses.whyCN: 矿体才是资源；回收节省金属，却不会重建矿床。

senses.title: Fossil groundwater
senses.definition: water stored in deep aquifers during wetter climates and recharged only over millennia
senses.definitionCN: 在更湿润气候下储于深层含水层、只能以千年计补给的水
senses.example: Farming on fossil water is mining a nonrenewable reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 靠古地下水耕作，等于开采一份不可再生的储备。
senses.why: water can be renewable or not depending on the aquifer's recharge rate.
senses.whyCN: 水是否可再生，取决于含水层的补给速率。

senses.title: The rate-based test
senses.definition: the criterion that compares consumption with replenishment over a human timescale
senses.definitionCN: 在人类时间尺度上比较消耗与补充的标准
senses.example: A resource is nonrenewable if refilling takes longer than a human lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 如果补充时间长过人的一生，这种资源就是不可再生的。
senses.why: nothing on earth is truly destroyed; the question is whether it returns in time to matter.
senses.whyCN: 地球上没有东西真正消失；问题在于它能否及时回来。

senses.title: Recyclable but still finite
senses.definition: materials that can be reused yet still lose quality or end in dispersal
senses.definitionCN: 可以再利用、却仍会降质或最终散失的材料
senses.example: Aluminium is recyclable, yet its ore remains nonrenewable.
senses.exampleCN: 铝可以回收，但其矿石仍不可再生。
senses.why: recycling slows depletion instead of changing the geology that made the deposit.
senses.whyCN: 回收只是减慢耗竭，并不能改变形成矿床的地质过程。

senses.title: Nonrenewable energy
senses.definition: the energy category of fuels that are consumed rather than replenished
senses.definitionCN: 被消耗而非被补充的燃料能源类别
senses.example: Nonrenewable energy still supplies most of the world's heat and transport.
senses.exampleCN: 不可再生能源仍供应了世界上大部分的供暖与运输。
senses.why: the adjective pairs with energy to name the opposite of the renewable category.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与「能源」搭配，命名可再生能源类别的对立面。

senses.title: Policy and transition
senses.definition: the label used in phase-out laws, subsidy debates and stranded-asset warnings
senses.definitionCN: 用于退场立法、补贴争论与搁浅资产警告的标签
senses.example: The law sets a date for ending nonrenewable heating.
senses.exampleCN: 该法律为终止不可再生供暖设定了日期。
senses.why: policy needs a category to phase out, and this adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要一个要退场的类别，这个形容词提供了它。

senses.title: The figurative use
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：不可再生的东西
senses.definition: anything spent once and gone, such as time, trust or attention
senses.definitionCN: 用掉一次就没有的东西，如时间、信任或注意力
senses.example: A teacher's patience is a nonrenewable resource in a large class.
senses.exampleCN: 在大班里，教师的耐心是一种不可再生资源。
senses.why: the environmental word escaped its field because the underlying image is simply depletion.
senses.whyCN: 这个环境词逸出了本领域，因为底层意象就是单纯的耗竭。

intro.en: Nonrenewable is Latin non 'not' plus renewable, whose base is re- 'again' and novare 'to make new'. The word is a twentieth-century formation, built when resource accounting needed a clean antonym for renewable.
intro.cn: nonrenewable 是拉丁 non「不」加 renewable，后者的词基是 re-「再次」与 novare「使新」。这个词是二十世纪的构造，产生于资源核算需要一个与 renewable 干净对立的反义词时。

items.en: Non meant 'not' and became the English prefix that negates a word without changing its grammar.
items.cn: non 意为「不」，成为英语中否定一个词而不改变其语法的前缀。

items.en: Novus 'new' and novare 'to make new' supply the middle of renewable.
items.cn: novus「新」与 novare「使新」提供 renewable 的中段。

items.en: Latin -abilis became English -able, marking a capacity rather than a fact.
items.cn: 拉丁 -abilis 成为英语 -able，标记能力而非事实。

items.en: Resource economists of the early twentieth century separated exhaustible stocks from continuing yields.
items.cn: 二十世纪初的资源经济学家把会耗尽的存量与持续的产出区分开来。

items.en: The energy debates of the 1970s fixed nonrenewable as the everyday opposite of renewable.
items.cn: 一九七〇年代的能源争论把 nonrenewable 固定为 renewable 的日常反义词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest printed use of the derived adjective is not consistently dated, though its parts are fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个派生形容词最早的印刷使用各家年代不一，但其组成部分记载完整。

note.en: Group one holds the words most often used as if interchangeable with nonrenewable; group two holds the property words that describe depletion.
note.cn: 第一组是最常被当作可互换使用的词；第二组是描述耗竭性质的词。

entries.definition: Able to be replenished at least as fast as it is used; the two words form one pair, not two degrees of the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 补充速度至少与使用速度相当；两词构成一对，而不是同一事物的两个程度。

entries.definition: An uncommon synonym formed with un- instead of non-; it appears in older texts but never displaced the standard form.
entries.definitionCN: 用 un- 而非 non- 构成的罕见同义词；见于较旧文本，但从未取代标准形式。

entries.definition: Describing a container that cannot be sent back for reuse; the resemblance is only in the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不能退回再用的容器；相似之处只在前缀。

entries.definition: Incapable of being used up; this is a stronger and rarer claim than simply not renewable.
entries.definitionCN: 无法被耗尽；这比「不可再生」更强也更罕见的断言。

entries.definition: Having a limit; a finite stock may still last centuries, so it says nothing about the rate of use.
entries.definitionCN: 有界限的；有限的存量也可能维持数百年，因此不说明使用速率。

entries.definition: Capable of being drained completely; it is the technical term in resource economics.
entries.definitionCN: 能被完全抽干的；这是资源经济学中的技术术语。

entries.definition: Able to be reduced in quantity by use; it stresses the shrinking store rather than the missing replacement.
entries.definitionCN: 会因使用而减少数量；强调缩小的存量，而非缺失的补充。

entries.definition: Made from ancient life, as in fossil water or fossil fuel; origin and renewability are different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 由远古生命形成，如古地下水或化石燃料；来源与可再生性是两回事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin negation and the real rate comparison.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁否定词，以及真实的速率比较。

normal.en: non- is Latin 'not': the word simply denies that the supply comes back in time.
normal.cn: non- 即拉丁「不」：这个词只是否认供给能及时回来。

normal.en: Think of a barrel, not a field: every litre taken is gone.
normal.cn: 想一只桶，而不是一片田：取走一升就少一升。

normal.en: Three fossil fuels: coal, oil, gas, all made long before people existed.
normal.cn: 三种化石燃料：煤、石油、天然气，都在人类出现之前很久就形成了。

normal.en: Recyclable is not renewable: the metal returns, the ore does not.
normal.cn: 可回收不等于可再生：金属回来了，矿体没有。

normal.en: Fossil water is the hidden case: an aquifer that rains no longer reach.
normal.cn: 古地下水是隐蔽的例子：雨水已到不了的含水层。

abstract.en: Nonrenewable is a wallet with no income, only a balance.
abstract.cn: nonrenewable 是一只没有收入、只有余额的钱包。

abstract.en: It is a clock that only runs down.
abstract.cn: 它是一只只会走慢的钟。

abstract.en: We are spending a bank account that no one is paying into.
abstract.cn: 我们在花一个无人存入的银行账户。

examples.en: Oil is the textbook nonrenewable resource.
examples.cn: 石油是教科书式的不可再生资源。

examples.en: The report separates renewable from nonrenewable investment.
examples.cn: 报告把可再生与不可再生投资分开统计。

examples.en: Even a nonrenewable aquifer can be managed to last longer.
examples.cn: 即便是不可再生的含水层，也能通过管理维持更久。

dict_mnemonic.text: non（不）+ renewable（可再生的）＝不能再生的；判断标准是补充速度追不上使用速度。

root: non-（拉丁 non「不」）+ renewable（re-「再次」+ novare「使新」+ -able）；词为二十世纪资源核算与能源争论所立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the core property to its figurative use: the exhaustible stock, fossil fuels, minerals, fossil water, the rate test, recycling, the energy category, policy and plain depletion.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从核心属性走到比喻用法：会耗尽的存量、化石燃料、矿产、古地下水、速率标准、回收、能源类别、政策，以及日常的耗竭意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a barrel is drawn down litre by litre, and no rain or growth refills it within a human life.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只桶一升一升地被抽空，而在人的一生里没有雨水或生长把它重新填满。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY AND ITS TEST: a fixed stock, judged by the ratio of use to replenishment.
branches.cn: 属性与标准：先是固定存量，再以使用与补充的比值判定。

branches.en: FUELS: coal, oil and gas, then the energy category they define.
branches.cn: 燃料：先是煤、石油与天然气，再是它们所定义的能源类别。

branches.en: ORES: mined minerals, then the recycling that slows but does not renew them.
branches.cn: 矿石：先是采出的矿产，再是减慢却不使其再生的回收。

branches.en: WATER: aquifers filled in wetter climates and never refilled now.
branches.cn: 水：在更湿润气候中充填、如今不再补给的含水层。

branches.en: POLICY AND FIGURE: phase-out rules, then time and patience spent once.
branches.cn: 政策与比喻：先是退场规则，再是用掉一次就没有的时间与耐心。

intro.en: Nonrenewable is one Latin negative prefix on top of the Latin-based adjective renewable.
intro.cn: nonrenewable 是一个拉丁否定前缀，加在拉丁语源的形容词 renewable 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin non, re-, novare and -abilis supply every part; the word was assembled in English rather than borrowed whole.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 non、re-、novare 与 -abilis 提供了全部成分；这个词是在英语中拼装而成，而非整词借入。

items.example: Non- negates without changing the word class.
items.exampleCN: non- 只否定，不改变词类。

items.example: Novus is the core of renewable.
items.exampleCN: novus 是 renewable 的核心。

items.example: Novare turns the adjective into a process.
items.exampleCN: novare 把这个形容词变成过程。

items.example: Re- marks repetition.
items.exampleCN: re- 标记重复。

items.example: -able marks a capacity.
items.exampleCN: -able 标记一种能力。

items.example: Renewable is the positive member of the pair.
items.exampleCN: renewable 是这一对中的肯定项。

items.example: Nonrenewable is the negative member.
items.exampleCN: nonrenewable 是这一对中的否定项。

items.example: Exhaustible is the economist's synonym.
items.exampleCN: exhaustible 是经济学家的同义词。
